70    /// Apply the established unsupported-syscall refusal policy to a *supported*
71    /// syscall whose particular operation Detcore cannot serve deterministically.
72    ///
73    /// This exists so such a refusal cannot invent its own policy. Three separate
74    /// config knobs govern how a fail-closed run dies -- `shutdown_on_unsupported_syscall`
75    /// (hard `exit(1)` through `unrecoverable_shutdown`), `exit_on_unsupported_syscall`
76    /// (a typed `UnsupportedSyscallError` the backend terminates on without
77    /// unwinding), and the `panic!` fallback -- and `Detcore::handle_unsupported_syscall`
78    /// consults all three in that order. The normal `hermit run` CLI happens to set
79    /// `shutdown_on_unsupported_syscall = panic_on_unsupported_syscalls`, so reading
80    /// only the latter looks equivalent, but that coupling is a CLI default, not an
81    /// invariant: an embedder that sets just `exit_on_unsupported_syscall` would get a
82    /// process-wide `exit(1)` from a bespoke call site where the standard path returns
83    /// a catchable error.
84    ///
85    /// When the run is *not* fail-closed, the caller's `fallback` errno is returned,
86    /// because the operation itself is legal and the guest is entitled to a normal
87    /// failure code (`handle_unsupported_syscall` passes the call through instead,
88    /// which is not available here -- passing through is precisely the thing the
89    /// caller has determined it cannot do).
90    pub(crate) async fn refuse_unserviceable_operation<G: Guest<Self>>(
91        &self,
92        guest: &mut G,
93        sysno: reverie::syscalls::Sysno,
94        fallback: Errno,
95    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
96        refuse_unserviceable_operation_with(
97            guest,
98            self.cfg.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls,
99            sysno,
100            fallback,
101            None,
102        )
103        .await
104    }
105
106    /// [`Self::refuse_unserviceable_operation`], with the backend's own
107    /// description of why it cannot perform the operation, which a
108    /// fail-closed refusal reports as its reason.
109    pub(crate) async fn refuse_unserviceable_operation_because<G: Guest<Self>>(
110        &self,
111        guest: &mut G,
112        sysno: reverie::syscalls::Sysno,
113        fallback: Errno,
114        reason: &str,
115    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
116        refuse_unserviceable_operation_with(
117            guest,
118            self.cfg.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls,
119            sysno,
120            fallback,
121            Some(reason),
122        )
123        .await
124    }

126    /// Record or replay a BLOCKING syscall without stalling the current thread (and thus
127    /// deadlocking).  This uses a protocol of an extra resource request before/after the
128    /// syscall to inform the scheduler that the thread is leaving/rejoining the runnable
129    /// threads pool.
130    ///
131    /// This is only valid to use (1) in hermit record/replay modes, or (2)
132    /// when we're in "hermit run", but we're NOT sequentializing threads, because in
133    /// that case it's ok to use the blocking versions of system calls.
134    pub async fn record_or_replay_blocking<G: Guest<Self>>(
135        &self,
136        guest: &mut G,
137        call: Syscall,
138    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
139        self.record_or_replay_blocking_with_mask(guest, call, None)
140            .await
141    }
142
143    /// `record_or_replay_blocking`, with `run` the call that runs for `call`,
144    /// or that replay serves: the scheduler, the checks and the continuation
145    /// mask all see `call`. A kernel-run poll's restart is the one such pair:
146    /// the guest's own `restart_syscall` runs for the poll
147    /// (`Detcore::resume_kernel_poll`). Only x86_64 has `poll`.
148    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
149    pub(crate) async fn record_or_replay_blocking_as<G: Guest<Self>>(
150        &self,
151        guest: &mut G,
152        call: Syscall,
153        run: Syscall,
154    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
155        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
156        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(dettid, guest.thread_state().stats.syscall_count);
157        self.record_or_replay_blocking_resource_then(
158            guest,
159            (call, run),
160            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id),
161            None,
162            false,
163            |_| {},
164        )
165        .await
166    }

168    /// `record_or_replay_blocking` for a call that sleeps under its own
169    /// temporary signal mask (`ppoll`, `pselect6`, or an `rt_sigsuspend` that
170    /// finds a signal already pending): `blocked_signal_mask` is the mask the
171    /// kernel installs for the call, read in this thread's turn
172    /// (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask`). `None` means the call sleeps under
173    /// the thread's own mask.
174    pub async fn record_or_replay_blocking_with_mask<G: Guest<Self>>(
175        &self,
176        guest: &mut G,
177        call: Syscall,
178        blocked_signal_mask: Option<u64>,
179    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
180        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
181        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(dettid, guest.thread_state().stats.syscall_count);
182        self.record_or_replay_blocking_resource(
183            guest,
184            call,
185            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id),
186            blocked_signal_mask,
187            false,
188        )
189        .await
190    }

192    /// `record_or_replay_blocking` for a call that sleeps under a temporary
193    /// mask its turn cannot vouch for (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask_unknown`):
194    /// the scheduler records no sleeping mask for it.
195    pub async fn record_or_replay_blocking_with_unknown_mask<G: Guest<Self>>(
196        &self,
197        guest: &mut G,
198        call: Syscall,
199    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
200        self.record_or_replay_blocking_with_unknown_mask_then(guest, call, |_| {})

204    /// `record_or_replay_blocking_with_unknown_mask`, running `after_grant` once
205    /// the scheduler has granted the call and before it runs: after any
206    /// sibling that ran while the request waited. In replay nothing else runs
207    /// until the served call finishes; in recording a sibling turn may still
208    /// run before the call enters the kernel.
209    pub async fn record_or_replay_blocking_with_unknown_mask_then<G: Guest<Self>>(
210        &self,
211        guest: &mut G,
212        call: Syscall,
213        after_grant: impl FnOnce(&mut G),
214    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
215        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
216        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(dettid, guest.thread_state().stats.syscall_count);
217        self.record_or_replay_blocking_resource_then(
218            guest,
219            (call, call),
220            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id),
221            None,
222            true,
223            after_grant,
224        )
225        .await
226    }

228    /// Execute the real `rt_sigsuspend` outside the runnable set while preserving
229    /// its signal-only completion condition for the scheduler. `temporary_mask`
230    /// is the mask the call sleeps under, as `Resources::blocked_signal_mask`
231    /// describes.
232    pub async fn record_or_replay_rt_sigsuspend<G: Guest<Self>>(
233        &self,
234        guest: &mut G,
235        call: syscalls::RtSigsuspend,
236        temporary_mask: u64,
237    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
238        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
239        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(dettid, guest.thread_state().stats.syscall_count);
240        let result = self
241            .record_or_replay_blocking_resource(
242                guest,
243                call.into(),
244                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op_id),
245                Some(temporary_mask),
246                false,
247            )
248            .await;
249        // Linux's rt_sigsuspend ends only with ERESTARTNOHAND, which a handler
250        // turns into EINTR and never restarts. The host call reports
251        // ERESTARTSYS instead when the signal reached the thread before the
252        // call ran, which depends on host timing; under SA_RESTART the guest
253        // then slept again where Linux returns
254        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4320). This fixes the
255        // result and the restart only: in that case the call never ran, so
256        // the kernel never installed its temporary mask, and the handler runs
257        // under the thread's pre-call mask, still a host-timed difference when
258        // the two masks differ (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4338).
259        // Whether the kernel ran the call, before that normalization hides it
260        // (`signal_shadow::kernel_ran_the_wait`). A replayed result is not
261        // taken as evidence, so under replay the wait never counts as run.
262        if !self.cfg.replaying {
263            let ran = !matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)));
264            super::signal_shadow::note_wait_ran(guest, ran);
265        }
266        match result {
267            Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)) => Err(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND.into()),
268            other => other,
269        }
270    }

272    async fn record_or_replay_blocking_resource<G: Guest<Self>>(
273        &self,
274        guest: &mut G,
275        call: Syscall,
276        blocking_resource: ResourceID,
277        blocked_signal_mask: Option<u64>,
278        blocked_signal_mask_unknown: bool,
279    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
280        self.record_or_replay_blocking_resource_then(
281            guest,
282            (call, call),
283            blocking_resource,
284            blocked_signal_mask,
285            blocked_signal_mask_unknown,
286            |_| {},
287        )
288        .await
289    }

291    /// `record_or_replay_blocking_resource`, running `after_grant` between the
292    /// grant and the call, and running `run` for `call`
293    /// (`record_or_replay_blocking_as`).
294    async fn record_or_replay_blocking_resource_then<G: Guest<Self>>(
295        &self,
296        guest: &mut G,
297        (call, run): (Syscall, Syscall),
298        blocking_resource: ResourceID,
299        blocked_signal_mask: Option<u64>,
300        blocked_signal_mask_unknown: bool,
301        after_grant: impl FnOnce(&mut G),
302    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
303        // D41 (A5 step 3c.1c): the first statement of every background
304        // external call and `rt_sigsuspend`, the two kernel-run families
305        // filed here, before anything below refuses, files or runs it.
306        if let Some(refused) = kernel_run_entry_refusal(guest)? {
307            return Err(refused);
308        }
309        // A host wait on descriptors that may include a timerfd on virtual
310        // time would never see it readable (`crate::syscalls::timerfd`).
311        crate::syscalls::timerfd::refuse_host_wait_for(guest, call);
312        let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
313        let op_id = match &blocking_resource {
314            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id) | ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op_id) => {
315                *op_id
316            }
317            _ => unreachable!("blocking syscall helper requires a blocking resource"),
318        };
319        // Replay serves some of these calls from the recording, so they cannot block.
320        // They still run in the background, as they did during recording, so that the
321        // schedule matches the recording's. The flag makes the scheduler commit no
322        // other turn until they finish. Otherwise a stand-in descriptor that replay
323        // creates for an accepted connection could take its slot before or after
324        // another thread's open or close, and which of these calls had finished, and
325        // so the order in which they rejoin, would depend on host timing
326        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3871).
327        let replay_served_from_log = self.cfg.replaying
328            && (replay_serves_blocking_call_from_log(call)
329                || replay_serves_socket_call_from_log(guest, call));
330        // Internal-vs-external fd classification happens at the call sites that hold the
331        // typed, nonblockize-able syscall (see execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall):
332        // container-internal pipes are routed to the InternalIOPolling nonblockize-retry
333        // path and must NOT reach this external-blocking protocol. BlockingExternalIO
334        // deschedules the thread to run in the background and rejoin nondeterministically,
335        // which is unsafe for a pipe whose reader and writer are interdependent -- doing
336        // so is the root cause of the record/replay pipe deadlock. The remaining callers
337        // (external poll, wait4) are external by construction (their fd is not a single
338        // extractable internal pipe). Guard the invariant in debug builds while the
339        // deterministic scheduler is active. With thread sequentialization disabled,
340        // resource requests are no-ops and internal pipes intentionally use a blocking
341        // host syscall, as documented by this method.
342        debug_assert!(
343            !self.cfg.sequentialize_threads || !syscall_targets_internal_fd(guest, call),
344            "record_or_replay_blocking (BlockingExternalIO) reached for an internal fd \
345             (pipe or socketpair endpoint) on syscall {}; internal fds must use the \
346             InternalIOPolling path",
347            call.name()
348        );
349        {
350            let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
351            // With sequentialization enabled, only truly EXTERNAL endpoints reach here.
352            // Without it, resource_request is a no-op and internal fds may block directly.
353            rsrcs.reads_signalfd = matches!(blocking_resource, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_))
354                && call_reads_signalfd(guest, call);
355            if matches!(blocking_resource, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_)) {
356                rsrcs.read_fd =
357                    read_family_fd(call).map(|fd| (guest.thread_state().files_id(), fd));
358            }
359            rsrcs.insert(blocking_resource, Permission::RW);
360            rsrcs.fyi(call.name());
361            rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask = blocked_signal_mask;
362            rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask_unknown = blocked_signal_mask_unknown;
363            rsrcs.replay_served_from_log = replay_served_from_log;
364            resource_request(guest, rsrcs).await;
365        }
366        after_grant(guest);
367        // Race probes (docs/RACE_PROBES.md) may delay the call or its rejoin;
368        // both are host timing this protocol already treats as nondeterministic.
369        crate::race_probe::delay(crate::race_probe::BG_PRE_CALL).await;
370        tracing::trace!(
371            "Guest proceeding to execute potentially blocking call {}...",
372            call.name()
373        );
374        let res = self
375            .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, run)
376            .await;
377        crate::race_probe::delay(crate::race_probe::BG_POST_CALL).await;
378        // N.B. BlockingExternalIO is a "oneshot" resource, so no need to release
379        // explicitly here:
380        {
381            let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
382            rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
383            rsrcs.fyi(call.name());
384            // The mask the thread is stopped under here, as the scheduler may
385            // decide from it before this turn (`BlockedPool::continuation_masks`).
386            match continuation_mask(call, &res) {
387                ContinuationMask::Temporary => {
388                    rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask = blocked_signal_mask;
389                    rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask_unknown = blocked_signal_mask_unknown;
390                }
391                ContinuationMask::Unknown => rsrcs.blocked_signal_mask_unknown = true,
392                ContinuationMask::Restored => {}
393            }
394            resource_request(guest, rsrcs).await;
395        }
396        res
397    }

399    /// Whether [`Self::execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall`] runs `call` as a
400    /// blocking call outside this thread's turn
401    /// ([`Self::record_or_replay_blocking`]), where other threads may run
402    /// before the kernel reads the call's arguments: without sequentialized
403    /// threads, for an external descriptor under record and replay, for a
404    /// descriptor that is blocking in the kernel as well, and where the
405    /// descriptor cannot be classified. Decided as that function decides it.
406    pub(crate) fn nonblockable_call_runs_outside_turn<G, C>(&self, guest: &mut G, call: C) -> bool
407    where
408        G: Guest<Self>,
409        C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall> + Copy,
410    {
411        let wrapped: Syscall = call.into();
412        match ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, call) {
413            Err(_) => true,
414            Ok(action) => {
415                !self.cfg.sequentialize_threads
416                    || (self.cfg.recordreplay_modes && !syscall_targets_internal_fd(guest, wrapped))
417                    || action == IOAction::Blocking
418            }
419        }
420    }
421
422    /// Executes a nonblockable syscall according to the following strategy:
423    /// - Record mode: Execute possibly blocking syscall
424    /// - Run mode: Transform the syscall to nonblocking if required before executing
425    ///
426    /// These are fd-oriented syscalls in the sense that whether they block or not depends
427    /// on whether NONBLOCK was set on the corresponding file descriptor.
428    pub async fn execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall<
429        G: Guest<Self>,
430        C: SyscallInfo + NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
431    >(
432        &self,
433        guest: &mut G,
434        call: C,
435    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
436        let wrapped: Syscall = call.into();
437
438        let action = match ioaction_based_on_fd_status(guest, call) {
439            Ok(action) => action,
440            Err(errno) => {
441                // Descriptor metadata is advisory for choosing an execution strategy. If the
442                // descriptor is invalid or cannot be classified, execute through the
443                // scheduler-safe blocking path and let the kernel provide the syscall errno.
444                // Returning the metadata error (or panicking on it) can change Linux error
445                // precedence, for example connect(-1, invalid_sockaddr, ...).
446                tracing::trace!(
447                    "NonblockableSyscall: fd classification failed with {}; executing kernel-authoritatively: {}",
448                    errno,
449                    call.name()
450                );
451                return self.record_or_replay_blocking(guest, wrapped).await;
452            }
453        };
454
455        // Is this operation on a container-INTERNAL fd (a pipe, a socketpair
456        // endpoint, or a socket whose peer is a guest)? Internal fds are made
457        // physically nonblocking even in record/replay (see handle_pipe2,
458        // handle_socketpair and classify_socket_peer), so they can take the
459        // deterministic InternalIOPolling nonblockize-and-retry path. They must NOT be
460        // forced onto the BlockingExternalIO path in R/R: a reader and its paired
461        // writer are not independent, so descheduling the reader as "external
462        // blocking IO" deadlocks the sequentialized scheduler (the documented R/R pipe
463        // hang), and a one-shot read on the physically nonblocking fd returns EAGAIN.
464        // Truly external endpoints (host fds, network sockets, sockets whose peer
465        // is a host process) still use BlockingExternalIO.
466        let internal_fd = syscall_targets_internal_fd(guest, wrapped);
467
468        if !self.cfg.sequentialize_threads
469            || (self.cfg.recordreplay_modes && !internal_fd)
470            || action == IOAction::Blocking
471        {
472            tracing::trace!(
473                "NonblockableSyscall: executing in blocking mode after all: {}",
474                call.name()
475            );
476            // We let these have nondeterminstic timing in record mode:
477            Ok(self.record_or_replay_blocking(guest, wrapped).await?)
478            // If in the future we want to record EXTERNAL network traffic only, we have a
479            // challenge to overcome.  We don't know if we need to record until after the
480            // accept completes, so we need an API for *post-facto* recording.
481        } else if action == IOAction::NonblockizeRetry {
482            tracing::trace!(
483                "NonblockableSyscall: converting to nonblocking syscall (internal polling): {}",
484                call.name()
485            );
486            let mut rsrc = Resources::new(guest.thread_state().dettid);
487            rsrc.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
488            rsrc.fyi(call.name());
489            (rsrc.polls_guest_state_only, rsrc.relies_on_guest_held_marks) =
490                single_fd_poll_readiness(guest, wrapped, internal_fd);
491            // A pipe read: a recorded private `SIGCHLD` ends it as on Linux.
492            rsrc.private_sigchld_decides = reads_a_pipe(guest, wrapped);
493            // A read waits for data, a write for room (`--pipe-wake-latency`).
494            rsrc.polls_channel = crate::pipe_wake::poll_of(&wrapped).and_then(|(fd, wants)| {
495                self.pipe_channel_end(guest, fd)
496                    .map(|end| Box::new((end.channel, wants)))
497            });
498            // In record/replay mode, route an internal-fd (pipe or socketpair) read/write through the
499            // record/replay subtool so its data is captured on record and reproduced on
500            // replay (see retry_nonblocking_syscall). In plain `hermit run` there is no
501            // recorder, so execute directly (subtool = None).
502            let subtool = (self.cfg.recordreplay_modes && internal_fd).then_some(self);
503            Ok(retry_nonblocking_syscall(guest, call, rsrc, subtool).await?)
504        } else {
505            assert!(action == IOAction::PassThru);
506            tracing::trace!(
507                "NonblockableSyscall: just passing it through: {}",
508                call.name()
509            );
510            // Otherwise, the socket was already nonblocking, so we can safely execute it just once.
511            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, wrapped)
512                .await
513        }
514    }

517    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#547)
518    /// Complete a logically blocking pipe writev after Hermit has made the pipe physically
519    /// nonblocking. A positive short write is an implementation artifact here: without
520    /// O_NONBLOCK, Linux blocks until the full vector is written unless a signal or error
521    /// interrupts it. Atomic vectors retain a private iovec snapshot for every retry; larger
522    /// vectors advance a positive short-write remainder through scalar writes.
523    pub async fn execute_blocking_pipe_writev<G: Guest<Self>>(
524        &self,
525        guest: &mut G,
526        call: syscalls::Writev,
527        expected_open_file: OpenFileId,
528    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
529        const MAX_IOVECS: usize = 1024;
530        // Linux limits a single vectored transfer to INT_MAX rounded down to a page.
531        let max_rw_count = crate::page::max_rw_count();
532        // Linux guarantees pipe writes through this size are atomic.
533        const PIPE_BUF: usize = 4096;
534        // Every backend provides at least 512 bytes of tool scratch. Linux's
535        // own fast-iovec path is smaller; this covers common vectors.
536        const STACK_IOVECS: usize = 32;
537
538        let Some(iov_addr) = call.iov() else {
539            return self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
540        };
541        if call.len() == 0 || call.len() > MAX_IOVECS {
542            return self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
543        }
544
545        let iovecs: Vec<(usize, usize)> = {
546            let mut raw_iovecs = vec![
547                libc::iovec {
548                    iov_base: std::ptr::null_mut(),
549                    iov_len: 0,
550                };
551                call.len()
552            ];
553            guest.memory().read_values(iov_addr, &mut raw_iovecs)?;
554            raw_iovecs
555                .into_iter()
556                .map(|iovec| (iovec.iov_base as usize, iovec.iov_len))
557                .collect()
558        };
559        // The array as the call began, in the form the guest's own `writev`
560        // copies it: that attempt may come after another thread has run
561        // (`EntryImport`), unlike the later ones, which write from `iovecs`.
562        // Boxed, so the call's future stays small (`hot_path_futures_stay_small`).
563        let entry_import =
564            EntryImport::capture(&guest.memory(), &Syscall::Writev(call)).map(Box::new);
565        let requested = iovecs.iter().try_fold(0usize, |total, (_, length)| {
566            total.checked_add(*length).ok_or(Errno::EINVAL)
567        })?;
568        if requested > isize::MAX as usize {
569            return Err(Errno::EINVAL.into());
570        }
571        let target = requested.min(max_rw_count);
572        if target == 0 {
573            return self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
574        }
575
576        let atomic_pipe_write = target <= PIPE_BUF;
577
578        tracing::trace!(
579            "NonblockableSyscall: converting to nonblocking syscall (internal polling): writev"
580        );
581        let mut resources = pipe_writev_resources(guest.thread_state().dettid, call);
582        resources.polls_channel = self
583            .pipe_channel_end(guest, call.fd())
584            .map(|end| Box::new((end.channel, crate::pipe_wake::Wants::Space)));
585        let subtool = self.cfg.recordreplay_modes.then_some(self);
586        let mut current = Syscall::Writev(call);
587        let mut written_total = 0usize;
588
589        // Keep ordinary signals pending while the scheduler and the target-side
590        // disposition check decide whether a wakeup interrupts this write. The
591        // ptrace-owned backends need the explicit mask while inspecting the
592        // target's current disposition.
593        let blocked_mask = blocked_signal_mask();
594        let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
595        let atomic_scratch_iov = if atomic_pipe_write && iovecs.len() <= STACK_IOVECS {
596            let mut raw_iovecs = [libc::iovec {
597                iov_base: std::ptr::null_mut(),
598                iov_len: 0,
599            }; STACK_IOVECS];
600            for (raw, (base, length)) in raw_iovecs.iter_mut().zip(&iovecs) {
601                raw.iov_base = *base as *mut libc::c_void;
602                raw.iov_len = *length;
603            }
604            let scratch_iov: Addr<libc::iovec> = stack.push(raw_iovecs).cast();
605            Some(scratch_iov.as_raw())
606        } else {
607            None
608        };
609        let blocked_mask_addr = stack.push(blocked_mask);
610        let old_mask_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigset>();
611        let turn_mask_cell = stack.reserve::<KernelSigset>();
612        let action_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigaction>();
613        let _mask_guard = stack.commit()?;
614        // A parked pipe write under the in-guest delivery gate (A5 step 3c.1c,
615        // D50 reader 1) installs no private mask: once an attempt would wait
616        // for room, the design's deliverable set under the thread's published
617        // mask decides (`gated_wait_ends`).
618        let gated = guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery;
619        let checks_at_turn =
620            !gated && decides_interruption_at_turn(guest, guest_signal_state_task(guest));
621        // Where the turn decides (`read_turn_signals`), the state is read, and
622        // the first attempt made, in the slice of the call's own entry, as the
623        // scalar writer's first attempt is, under the guest's own mask: that
624        // attempt is the guest's own `writev`, which the backend runs as plain
625        // ptrace runs it, with every pending signal left queued in the kernel,
626        // and a copy pending at entry ends the call after it (rules 5 and 6).
627        // No other thread runs between Detcore's snapshot of the iovec array,
628        // taken as it handles the call, and that attempt, so the kernel imports
629        // the array Detcore copied, which every later attempt writes from. A
630        // rewrite that lands before the snapshot (while the call waits at a
631        // checkpoint before its handler runs) is one Linux could also see,
632        // before the call imports the array.
633        // Requesting a turn first let another thread rewrite the array before
634        // the import, and an atomic write to a full pipe then wrote its bytes
635        // (writev_determinism's atomic full-pipe case, which reverted the
636        // first landing of R2b-1). Only a call that goes on polling installs the
637        // private mask, through `KernelSignalWait::block`, in the same turn
638        // (`install_turn_mask`); no copy that ends the call is pending then,
639        // and one Linux discarded at send is held until the call returns.
640        // Installing it first let two such copies stop the installation, and
641        // the backend's single held slot kept only the second (the Claude
642        // implementation review of R2b-1, F2;
643        // https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1012).
644        let mut first_turn = if checks_at_turn {
645            let turn = read_turn_signals(guest, None, 0, NamedRealTime::ByDisposition).await?;
646            Some((ResumeStatus::Normal, turn))
647        } else {
648            None
649        };
650        let mut turn_wait = checks_at_turn
651            .then(|| KernelSignalWait::new(guest, 0, false, call.signal_interrupt_errno()));
652        let mut turn_mask: Option<KernelSigset> = None;
653        let guest_signal_mask = if checks_at_turn || gated {
654            0
655        } else {
656            block_signals_for_disposition(guest, blocked_mask_addr, old_mask_addr).await?
657        };
658
659        let result: Result<i64, Error> = loop {
660            let written_before = written_total;
661            // A cross-task signal can replace the initial scheduler request,
662            // before the first physical attempt, as well as a later retry.
663            let (status, turn) = match first_turn.take() {
664                Some((status, turn)) => (status, Some(turn)),
665                None => {
666                    if let Some(wait) = turn_wait.as_mut()
667                        && turn_mask.is_none()
668                    {
669                        match install_turn_mask(guest, wait, turn_mask_cell).await {
670                            Ok(mask) => turn_mask = Some(mask),
671                            Err(Error::Errno(errno)) => {
672                                break if written_total > 0 {
673                                    Ok(written_total as i64)
674                                } else {
675                                    Err(errno.into())
676                                };
677                            }
678                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
679                        }
680                    }
681                    let status = resource_request(guest, resources.clone()).await;
682                    let turn = if checks_at_turn {
683                        // A named signal counts if the guest's own mask leaves
684                        // it unblocked; the private mask keeps every such
685                        // signal pending until this read.
686                        match read_turn_signals(
687                            guest,
688                            turn_mask,
689                            committed_signals(&status),
690                            NamedRealTime::ByDisposition,
691                        )
692                        .await
693                        {
694                            Ok(turn) => Some(turn),
695                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
696                        }
697                    } else {
698                        None
699                    };
700                    (status, turn)
701                }
702            };
703            if turn.is_none() && !gated {
704                let disposition = match wait_signal_disposition(
705                    guest,
706                    status.clone(),
707                    &guest_signal_mask,
708                    action_addr,
709                    true,
710                )
711                .await
712                {
713                    Ok(disposition) => disposition,
714                    Err(error) => break Err(error),
715                };
716                if matches!(status, ResumeStatus::Signaled(_))
717                    && let Some(result) =
718                        interrupted_write_result(&call, written_total, disposition)
719                {
720                    break result;
721                }
722            }
723
724            if resources.poll_attempt > 0
725                && !guest
726                    .thread_state()
727                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
728                        detfd.open_file_id() == expected_open_file
729                    })
730                    .unwrap_or(false)
731            {
732                break if written_total > 0 {
733                    Ok(written_total as i64)
734                } else {
735                    self.refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::writev, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP)
736                        .await
737                };
738            }
739
740            // The first attempt of a call that decides at its turn runs under
741            // the guest's own mask, where a pending signal would stop a
742            // private injection and the backend's single held slot keeps only
743            // the last of two. So it is always the guest's own `writev`, which
744            // the backend runs with every pending signal left queued in the
745            // kernel (the Claude re-check of R2b-1, N2).
746            let own_first_attempt = turn_wait.is_some() && turn_mask.is_none();
747            let result = if atomic_pipe_write && !own_first_attempt {
748                self.execute_atomic_pipe_writev_attempt(guest, call, &iovecs, atomic_scratch_iov)
749                    .await
750            } else {
751                // The guest's own `writev` copies the guest's array again; a
752                // segment `write` names Hermit's copy.
753                let displaced = matches!(current, Syscall::Writev(_))
754                    .then(|| entry_import.as_ref())
755                    .flatten()
756                    .map(|entry| entry.reinstate(&mut guest.memory()));
757                let result = match subtool {
758                    Some(detcore) => {
759                        detcore
760                            .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, current)
761                            .await
762                    }
763                    None => guest.inject_with_retry(current).await.map_err(Error::from),
764                };
765                if let Err(error) =
766                    put_back_entry_import(guest, &entry_import, displaced, result.is_ok())
767                {
768                    break Err(error);
769                }
770                result
771            };
772            match result {
773                Ok(written) if written > 0 => {
774                    let written = match usize::try_from(written) {
775                        Ok(written) => written,
776                        Err(_) => break Err(Errno::EIO.into()),
777                    };
778                    written_total = match written_total.checked_add(written) {
779                        Some(written_total) => written_total,
780                        None => break Err(Errno::EIO.into()),
781                    };
782                    if written_total >= target {
783                        break Ok(written_total as i64);
784                    }
785                    if atomic_pipe_write {
786                        break Ok(written_total as i64);
787                    }
788                    // A short attempt filled the pipe, so the write would wait:
789                    // a wake ends it with the bytes written, decided after the
790                    // attempt, as Linux tests for room first (R2b-1 rule 6).
791                    if turn.is_some_and(|turn| turn.ends(true)) {
792                        break Ok(written_total as i64);
793                    }
794                    if gated {
795                        match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
796                            Ok(true) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
797                            Ok(false) => {}
798                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
799                        }
800                    }
801                    current = match remaining_writev_segment(
802                        call.fd(),
803                        &iovecs,
804                        written_total,
805                        target - written_total,
806                    ) {
807                        Ok(Some(write)) => Syscall::Write(write),
808                        Ok(None) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
809                        Err(_) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
810                    };
811                }
812                Ok(0) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
813                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EAGAIN))
814                    if turn.is_some_and(|turn| turn.ends(written_total > 0)) =>
815                {
816                    break if written_total > 0 {
817                        Ok(written_total as i64)
818                    } else {
819                        Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())
820                    };
821                }
822                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EAGAIN)) => {
823                    if gated {
824                        match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
825                            Ok(true) => {
826                                break if written_total > 0 {
827                                    Ok(written_total as i64)
828                                } else {
829                                    Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())
830                                };
831                            }
832                            Ok(false) => {}
833                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
834                        }
835                    }
836                    if !atomic_pipe_write && matches!(current, Syscall::Writev(_)) {
837                        current = match remaining_writev_segment(call.fd(), &iovecs, 0, target) {
838                            Ok(Some(write)) => Syscall::Write(write),
839                            Ok(None) => break Ok(0),
840                            Err(error) => break Err(error.into()),
841                        };
842                    }
843                }
844                Err(error) => {
845                    break finish_partial_record_or_replay_write(written_total as i64, error);
846                }
847                Ok(_) => break Err(Errno::EIO.into()),
848            }
849
850            resources.previous_attempt_made_progress = written_total > written_before;
851            // Bytes this attempt wrote ready the readers before this thread
852            // polls for room (`--pipe-wake-latency`).
853            if resources.previous_attempt_made_progress {
854                self.note_fd_readied(guest, call.fd(), crate::pipe_wake::Wants::Data)
855                    .await;
856            }
857            resources.poll_attempt += 1;
858            tracing::trace!(
859                "Retry #{} for {}blocking pipe writev after EAGAIN: {}",
860                resources.poll_attempt,
861                if atomic_pipe_write { "atomic " } else { "" },
862                call.display(&guest.memory())
863            );
864            record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
865        };
866        keep_entry_view(guest, entry_import);
867
868        match turn_wait {
869            Some(mut wait) => {
870                let restored = wait.restore(guest, Some(turn_mask_cell)).await;
871                if turn_mask.is_some() {
872                    crate::tool_global::set_saved_guest_sigmask(guest, None).await;
873                }
874                match result_after_restore(restored, result) {
875                    Ok(result) => refuse_held_signal_loss(guest, Sysno::writev, result).await,
876                    Err(error) => Err(error),
877                }
878            }
879            None if gated => result,
880            None => {
881                restore_signals_after_disposition(guest, old_mask_addr).await?;
882                result
883            }
884        }
885    }
886
887    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
888    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#2176): Review scalar blocking-pipe write completion and
889    // the fail-closed descriptor-replacement boundary.
890    /// Complete a logically blocking scalar pipe write after Hermit has made the pipe
891    /// physically nonblocking.
892    ///
893    /// Linux may return a positive short write for a request larger than `PIPE_BUF`, then
894    /// continue blocking for the remainder. Hermit's physical `O_NONBLOCK` is an internal
895    /// scheduler mechanism, so exposing that first short write changes guest behavior. Retry
896    /// the unconsumed suffix until the logical write completes, a signal arrives, or a real
897    /// error occurs. A signal or error after progress returns the partial byte count, matching
898    /// Linux.
899    ///
900    /// A concurrent close/dup2 can replace the numeric fd while this helper is yielded. Linux
901    /// keeps the original open-file description alive inside a blocking syscall, but Reverie
902    /// does not yet expose a backend-neutral retained-fd handle. Detect replacement before a
903    /// retry and fail closed rather than writing the suffix into an unrelated object.
904    pub async fn execute_blocking_pipe_write<G: Guest<Self>>(
905        &self,
906        guest: &mut G,
907        call: syscalls::Write,
908        expected_open_file: OpenFileId,
909    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
910        let max_rw_count = crate::page::max_rw_count();
911
912        let target = call.len().min(max_rw_count);
913        if target == 0 {
914            return self.execute_nonblockable_fd_syscall(guest, call).await;
915        }
916
917        tracing::trace!(
918            "NonblockableSyscall: converting to nonblocking syscall (internal polling): write"
919        );
920        let mut resources = Resources::new(guest.thread_state().dettid);
921        resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
922        resources.fyi(call.name());
923        // Interruptible by a cross-task signal the kernel would deliver, as a
924        // polled read is (`retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`): the scheduler
925        // answers the next request `Signaled`, and the write returns the
926        // bytes it wrote, or ERESTARTSYS before any
927        // (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4187>).
928        resources.set_signal_interrupt_errno(call.signal_interrupt_errno());
929        resources.signal_state_task = guest_signal_state_task(guest);
930        // A pipe write: a recorded private `SIGCHLD` ends it as on Linux
931        // (`Resources::private_sigchld_decides`).
932        resources.private_sigchld_decides = true;
933        resources.polls_guest_state_only = true;
934        resources.polls_channel = self
935            .pipe_channel_end(guest, call.fd())
936            .map(|end| Box::new((end.channel, crate::pipe_wake::Wants::Space)));
937        // Without a host task whose kernel state the scheduler can filter by
938        // (KVM), the scheduler keeps every signal and the write checks after
939        // the wake, as `execute_blocking_pipe_writev` does, whether one would
940        // be delivered: a blocked or ignored signal must not end a write that
941        // has made progress, which would return a short count where Linux
942        // keeps waiting.
943        let disposition_scratch = if resources.signal_state_task.is_none() {
944            resources.decides_signal_interruption_itself = true;
945            let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
946            let mask_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigset>();
947            let action_addr = stack.reserve::<KernelSigaction>();
948            let guard = stack.commit()?;
949            Some((mask_addr, action_addr, guard))
950        } else {
951            None
952        };
953        let subtool = self.cfg.recordreplay_modes.then_some(self);
954        let mut current = call;
955        let mut written_total = 0usize;
956        // Under the in-guest delivery gate (A5 step 3c.1c, D50 reader 1), as
957        // for a pipe `writev`: no private mask, and the design's deliverable
958        // set decides once an attempt would wait for room.
959        let gated = guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery;
960        let checks_at_turn =
961            !gated && decides_interruption_at_turn(guest, resources.signal_state_task);
962        // The write owns the guest's mask while it blocks every blockable
963        // signal, as the generic poll does (`retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`):
964        // an attempt after the first is a private injection of the
965        // unwritten suffix, which a pending signal could stop and move into
966        // the backend's single held slot, where a second one replaces it
967        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, stage 2).
968        let mut turn_wait = checks_at_turn
969            .then(|| KernelSignalWait::new(guest, 0, false, call.signal_interrupt_errno()));
970        let mut published = PublishedWaitMask::default();
971
972        let result: Result<i64, Error> = loop {
973            let written_before = written_total;
974            // A signal ends the write only if it would still wait for room:
975            // the attempt below runs first, as Linux's `pipe_write` checks
976            // for a pending signal only when it must wait. After the signal,
977            // the bytes written so far are returned, or the restart errno if
978            // there are none.
979            let status = if resources.poll_attempt > 0 {
980                Some(resource_request(guest, resources.clone()).await)
981            } else {
982                None
983            };
984            // Read before every attempt, the turnless first one included
985            // (`read_turn_signals`): a copy pending at the write's own entry
986            // is decided in this slice, before the writer can yield, so a later
987            // `SIG_IGN` and a new handler cannot take it
988            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, R2b-1 rule 4).
989            // Once the write blocks, the turn decides under the guest's own
990            // mask, which the write owns (Codex review of the R2b-2 design
991            // rev3, P2-1).
992            let turn = if checks_at_turn {
993                let committed = status.as_ref().map_or(0, committed_signals);
994                // The first attempt is the guest's own write, which the
995                // backend runs with every pending signal left queued, so only
996                // a later attempt needs the block.
997                match turn_signals_with_block(
998                    guest,
999                    &mut turn_wait,
1000                    resources.poll_attempt > 0,
1001                    committed,
1002                    resources.private_sigchld_decides,
1003                    &mut published,
1004                )
1005                .await
1006                {
1007                    Ok(turn) => Some(turn),
1008                    Err(error) => break Err(error),
1009                }
1010            } else {
1011                None
1012            };
1013            let signaled = if turn.is_some() || gated {
1014                false
1015            } else {
1016                match (&status, &disposition_scratch) {
1017                    (Some(ResumeStatus::Signaled(_)), None) => true,
1018                    (
1019                        Some(status @ ResumeStatus::Signaled(_)),
1020                        Some((mask_addr, action_addr, _)),
1021                    ) => {
1022                        match own_disposition_interrupts(
1023                            guest,
1024                            status.clone(),
1025                            *mask_addr,
1026                            *action_addr,
1027                        )
1028                        .await
1029                        {
1030                            Ok(interrupts) => interrupts,
1031                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
1032                        }
1033                    }
1034                    _ => false,
1035                }
1036            };
1037
1038            if resources.poll_attempt > 0
1039                && !guest
1040                    .thread_state()
1041                    .with_detfd(call.fd(), |detfd| {
1042                        detfd.open_file_id() == expected_open_file
1043                    })
1044                    .unwrap_or(false)
1045            {
1046                break if written_total > 0 {
1047                    Ok(written_total as i64)
1048                } else {
1049                    self.refuse_unserviceable_operation(guest, Sysno::write, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP)
1050                        .await
1051                };
1052            }
1053
1054            let result = match subtool {
1055                Some(detcore) => {
1056                    detcore
1057                        .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, current)
1058                        .await
1059                }
1060                None => guest.inject_with_retry(current).await.map_err(Error::from),
1061            };
1062            // As in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`, an attempt that the
1063            // pending signal stopped under record and replay is not made again.
1064            match result {
1065                Ok(written) if written > 0 => {
1066                    let Ok(written) = usize::try_from(written) else {
1067                        break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
1068                    };
1069                    let Some(remaining) = target.checked_sub(written_total) else {
1070                        break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
1071                    };
1072                    if written > remaining {
1073                        break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
1074                    }
1075                    let Some(total) = written_total.checked_add(written) else {
1076                        break Err(Errno::EIO.into());
1077                    };
1078                    written_total = total;
1079                    // A short attempt filled the pipe, so the write would wait:
1080                    // a wake ends it with the bytes written (`TurnSignals::ends`).
1081                    if written_total == target || turn.map_or(signaled, |turn| turn.ends(true)) {
1082                        break Ok(written_total as i64);
1083                    }
1084                    if gated {
1085                        match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
1086                            Ok(true) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
1087                            Ok(false) => {}
1088                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
1089                        }
1090                    }
1091                    let Some(buffer) = call.buf() else {
1092                        break Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
1093                    };
1094                    let Some(next_buffer) = buffer
1095                        .as_raw()
1096                        .checked_add(written_total)
1097                        .and_then(Addr::<u8>::from_raw)
1098                    else {
1099                        break finish_partial_record_or_replay_write(
1100                            written_total as i64,
1101                            Errno::EFAULT.into(),
1102                        );
1103                    };
1104                    current = call
1105                        .with_buf(Some(next_buffer))
1106                        .with_len(target - written_total);
1107                }
1108                Ok(0) => break Ok(written_total as i64),
1109                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EAGAIN))
1110                    if turn.map_or(signaled, |turn| turn.ends(written_total > 0)) =>
1111                {
1112                    break if written_total > 0 {
1113                        Ok(written_total as i64)
1114                    } else {
1115                        Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())
1116                    };
1117                }
1118                Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EAGAIN)) => {
1119                    if gated {
1120                        match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
1121                            Ok(true) => {
1122                                break if written_total > 0 {
1123                                    Ok(written_total as i64)
1124                                } else {
1125                                    Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())
1126                                };
1127                            }
1128                            Ok(false) => {}
1129                            Err(error) => break Err(error),
1130                        }
1131                    }
1132                }
1133                Err(error) => {
1134                    break finish_partial_record_or_replay_write(written_total as i64, error);
1135                }
1136                Ok(_) => break Err(Errno::EIO.into()),
1137            }
1138
1139            resources.previous_attempt_made_progress = written_total > written_before;
1140            // Bytes this attempt wrote ready the readers before this thread
1141            // polls for room (`--pipe-wake-latency`).
1142            if resources.previous_attempt_made_progress {
1143                self.note_fd_readied(guest, call.fd(), crate::pipe_wake::Wants::Data)
1144                    .await;
1145            }
1146            resources.poll_attempt += 1;
1147            tracing::trace!(
1148                "Retry #{} for blocking pipe write: {}",
1149                resources.poll_attempt,
1150                call.display(&guest.memory())
1151            );
1152            record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
1153        };
1154
1155        // The single exit, as in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`: the
1156        // guest's mask goes back, through `Guest::set_blocked_signals` with no
1157        // scratch memory, before the result is returned.
1158        match turn_wait {
1159            Some(mut wait) if wait.effective_mask().is_some() => {
1160                let restored = wait.restore(guest, None).await;
1161                publish_wait_mask(guest, None, &mut published).await;
1162                match result_after_restore(restored, result) {
1163                    Ok(result) => refuse_held_signal_loss(guest, Sysno::write, result).await,
1164                    Err(error) => Err(error),
1165                }
1166            }
1167            _ => result,
1168        }
1169    }
1170
1171    async fn execute_atomic_pipe_writev_attempt<G: Guest<Self>>(
1172        &self,
1173        guest: &mut G,
1174        call: syscalls::Writev,
1175        iovecs: &[(usize, usize)],
1176        stack_iov: Option<usize>,
1177    ) -> Result<i64, Error> {
1178        if let Some(stack_iov) = stack_iov {
1179            let scratch_call = call.with_iov(Addr::from_raw(stack_iov));
1180            return if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
1181                self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, scratch_call)
1182                    .await
1183            } else {
1184                guest
1185                    .inject_with_retry(scratch_call)
1186                    .await
1187                    .map_err(Error::from)
1188            };
1189        }
1190
1191        let mapping_len = iovecs
1192            .len()
1193            .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<libc::iovec>())
1194            .expect("validated iovec count cannot overflow scratch length");
1195        let mapped = guest
1196            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Mmap(
1197                syscalls::Mmap::new()
1198                    .with_addr(None)
1199                    .with_len(mapping_len)
1200                    .with_prot(ProtFlags::PROT_READ | ProtFlags::PROT_WRITE)
1201                    .with_flags(MapFlags::MAP_PRIVATE | MapFlags::MAP_ANONYMOUS)
1202                    .with_fd(-1)
1203                    .with_offset(0),
1204            ))
1205            .await
1206            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("failed to map atomic writev scratch: {error}"));
1207        let mapped = usize::try_from(mapped)
1208            .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("atomic writev scratch mmap returned {mapped}"));
1209        let scratch_iov = Addr::<libc::iovec>::from_raw(mapped)
1210            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("atomic writev scratch mmap returned a null address"));
1211        let mapping_addr: Addr<libc::c_void> = scratch_iov.cast();
1212        let write_result = {
1213            let raw_iovecs: Vec<libc::iovec> = iovecs
1214                .iter()
1215                .map(|(base, length)| libc::iovec {
1216                    iov_base: *base as *mut libc::c_void,
1217                    iov_len: *length,
1218                })
1219                .collect();
1220            // SAFETY: the injected anonymous mapping is exclusively owned scratch space.
1221            guest
1222                .memory()
1223                .write_values(unsafe { scratch_iov.into_mut() }, &raw_iovecs)
1224        };
1225        if let Err(write_error) = write_result {
1226            guest
1227                .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
1228                    syscalls::Munmap::new()
1229                        .with_addr(Some(mapping_addr))
1230                        .with_len(mapping_len),
1231                ))
1232                .await
1233                .unwrap_or_else(|cleanup_error| {
1234                    panic!(
1235                        "failed to populate atomic writev scratch ({write_error}); cleanup failed ({cleanup_error})"
1236                    )
1237                });
1238            panic!("failed to populate atomic writev scratch: {write_error}");
1239        }
1240
1241        let scratch_call = call.with_iov(Some(scratch_iov));
1242        let result = if self.cfg.recordreplay_modes {
1243            self.record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, scratch_call)
1244                .await
1245        } else {
1246            guest
1247                .inject_with_retry(scratch_call)
1248                .await
1249                .map_err(Error::from)
1250        };
1251        guest
1252            .inject_with_retry(Syscall::Munmap(
1253                syscalls::Munmap::new()
1254                    .with_addr(Some(mapping_addr))
1255                    .with_len(mapping_len),
1256            ))
1257            .await
1258            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("failed to unmap atomic writev scratch: {error}"));
1259        result
1260    }
1261
1262    /// Override physically_nonblocking to true for the file descriptor, if appropriate.
1263    pub fn maybe_set_nonblocking_fd<G: Guest<Self>>(&self, guest: &G, fd: i32) {
1264        if self.cfg.sequentialize_threads && !self.cfg.debug_externalize_sockets {
1265            guest
1266                .thread_state()
1267                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
1268                    detfd.set_physically_nonblocking();
1269                })
1270                .unwrap();
1271        }
1272    }
1273}
1274
1275fn remaining_writev_segment(
1276    fd: i32,
1277    iovecs: &[(usize, usize)],
1278    mut consumed: usize,
1279    remaining_limit: usize,
1280) -> Result<Option<syscalls::Write>, Errno> {
1281    for (base, length) in iovecs {
1282        if consumed >= *length {
1283            consumed -= *length;
1284            continue;
1285        }
1286        let base = base.checked_add(consumed).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
1287        let buffer = Addr::<u8>::from_raw(base).ok_or(Errno::EFAULT)?;
1288        return Ok(Some(
1289            syscalls::Write::new()
1290                .with_fd(fd)
1291                .with_buf(Some(buffer))
1292                .with_len((*length - consumed).min(remaining_limit)),
1293        ));
1294    }
1295    Ok(None)
1296}
1297
1298/// A blocking syscall that involves a fail descriptor may be handled in these three ways:
1299#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
1300pub enum IOAction {
1301    /// It may physically block and we can't change that.  Treat it as ExternalBlockingIO.
1302    Blocking,
1303    /// We can nonblockize and retry the call.
1304    NonblockizeRetry,
1305    /// The call is nonblocking already, and safe to execute.
1306    PassThru,
1307}
1308
1309/// Returns the strategy for an FD-based call that may block when executed.
1310///
1311/// Failure means descriptor metadata could not classify the call; the caller must preserve the
1312/// kernel's authority over the syscall result rather than exposing this advisory lookup error.
1313pub fn ioaction_based_on_fd_status<
1314    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
1315    T: RecordOrReplay,
1316    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
1317>(
1318    guest: &mut G,
1319    call: C,
1320) -> Result<IOAction, Errno> {
1321    let wrapped: Syscall = call.into();
1322    let fd = get_fd(wrapped).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("Failed to get fd for {}", call.name()));
1323    let (phys, virt, error_queue_never_waits) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
1324        (
1325            detfd.physically_nonblocking(),
1326            detfd.is_nonblocking(),
1327            detfd.error_queue_never_waits(),
1328        )
1329    })?;
1330    tracing::trace!(
1331        "Checking FD {} for nonblocking: physical {} / virtual {}",
1332        fd,
1333        phys,
1334        virt
1335    );
1336    let action = ioaction_for_fd_status(fd, virt, phys, call.flags_forbid_waiting());
1337    // A receive with MSG_ERRQUEUE on a socket whose protocol reads that
1338    // queue without waiting also runs once, as Linux does.
1339    if action == IOAction::NonblockizeRetry && error_queue_never_waits && call.reads_error_queue() {
1340        Ok(IOAction::PassThru)
1341    } else {
1342        Ok(action)
1343    }
1344}
1345
1346/// [`ioaction_based_on_fd_status`] for the descriptor `fd` alone, before any
1347/// flag of the call itself, for a caller whose call does not implement
1348/// [`NonblockableSyscall`].
1349pub(crate) fn ioaction_based_on_fd<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1350    guest: &mut G,
1351    fd: i32,
1352) -> Result<IOAction, Errno> {
1353    let (phys, virt) = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
1354        (detfd.physically_nonblocking(), detfd.is_nonblocking())
1355    })?;
1356    Ok(ioaction_for_fd_status(fd, virt, phys, false))
1357}
1358
1359/// The decision of [`ioaction_based_on_fd_status`] from the descriptor's
1360/// virtual and physical nonblocking state and the call's own no-wait flags,
1361/// split out so the decision itself is unit-testable without a guest.
1362fn ioaction_for_fd_status(fd: i32, virt: bool, phys: bool, flags_forbid_waiting: bool) -> IOAction {
1363    if virt && !phys {
1364        // TF: simulate nonblocking on top of physically blocking? How?
1365        panic!(
1366            "Invariant violation, fd {fd}: we cannot simulate nonblocking behavior when set to blocking mode in the kernel."
1367        );
1368    } else if !virt && !phys {
1369        // FF: logically blocking, physically blocking, this could only work with BlockingExternalIO.
1370        IOAction::Blocking
1371    } else if virt && phys {
1372        // TT: both nonblocking, so firing once is sufficient
1373        IOAction::PassThru
1374    } else if flags_forbid_waiting {
1375        // FT, but the call itself does not wait (MSG_DONTWAIT), so firing once
1376        // is what Linux does.
1377        IOAction::PassThru
1378    } else {
1379        // FT: Need to simulate blocking on top of nonblocking.
1380        IOAction::NonblockizeRetry
1381    }
1382}
1383
1384/// Does this single-fd syscall operate on a container-INTERNAL file descriptor?
1385///
1386/// This is an execution-routing classification, not proof that only guests can
1387/// change readiness. It recognizes pipes and `socketpair(2)` endpoints. Internal
1388/// fds are made physically
1389/// nonblocking (see `handle_pipe2` and `handle_socketpair`) so a potentially-blocking
1390/// op on them can use the deterministic `InternalIOPolling` nonblockize-and-retry
1391/// strategy instead of `BlockingExternalIO`. Treating an internal fd as external
1392/// blocking IO deadlocks the sequentialized scheduler in record/replay, because a
1393/// reader and its paired writer are not independent.
1394///
1395/// Socketpair origin is known at creation time, and remains useful for routing
1396/// even after an endpoint is exported or a datagram endpoint changes its peer.
1397/// Under record and replay a connected socket whose peer is a guest, which
1398/// `Detcore::classify_socket_peer` finds from the peer's credentials after
1399/// `connect`, `accept` or an `SCM_RIGHTS` receive, is internal too. Every other
1400/// socket, including every loopback IP socket, conservatively remains external.
1401///
1402/// Readiness needs a separate decision: a socketpair endpoint can leave the guest
1403/// through `SCM_RIGHTS`, and a bound, disconnected datagram endpoint can receive
1404/// from an outside sender. See `single_fd_poll_readiness`.
1405///
1406/// A descriptor a guest RECEIVES over `SCM_RIGHTS` is recorded
1407/// (`Detcore::record_received_descriptors`) or discovered. One that names an open
1408/// file the table models joins it as an alias and keeps that file's marks. Any
1409/// other is recorded from the kernel's facts: a received pipe is a pipe here, and
1410/// under record and replay a received socket is internal when its peer is a guest
1411/// (`Detcore::classify_socket_peer`). A received socketpair end from another process
1412/// outside record and replay is not recognized as internal: its open file
1413/// description is still physically nonblocking, and the kernel's `O_NONBLOCK` is all
1414/// the receiver's record knows, so a blocking read through it can return EAGAIN
1415/// where Linux would wait.
1416///
1417/// Syscalls whose fd is not directly extractable (e.g. poll/ppoll, which carry a
1418/// pointer to an fd array) return false and keep their existing handling.
1419pub fn syscall_targets_internal_fd<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1420    guest: &mut G,
1421    call: Syscall,
1422) -> bool {
1423    // An epoll wait's descriptor is the epoll set it waits on, never a pipe it
1424    // reads; a guest that passes a pipe gets EINVAL from the kernel.
1425    match call {
1426        Syscall::EpollPwait(_) => return false,
1427        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
1428        Syscall::EpollWait(_) => return false,
1429        _ => {}
1430    }
1431    match get_fd(call) {
1432        Some(fd) => guest
1433            .thread_state()
1434            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
1435                // This is read-end provenance, not a blanket external-fd
1436                // classification: writes and socketpairs retain the guard.
1437                if matches!(call, Syscall::Read(_) | Syscall::Readv(_))
1438                    && detfd.inherited_external_read().is_some()
1439                {
1440                    return false;
1441                }
1442                matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Pipe) || detfd.is_internal_socket()
1443            })
1444            .unwrap_or(false),
1445        None => false,
1446    }
1447}
1448
1449/// Whether `call`'s one descriptor is guest-held (`DetFd::is_guest_held`):
1450/// only guests hold its other end, so only a guest can make the call ready.
1451/// It feeds only `Resources::polls_guest_state_only`, never the record/replay
1452/// routing `syscall_targets_internal_fd` decides. An epoll wait's descriptor
1453/// is its set, which this does not track.
1454fn syscall_targets_guest_held_fd<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1455    guest: &mut G,
1456    call: Syscall,
1457) -> bool {
1458    if matches!(call, Syscall::EpollWait(_) | Syscall::EpollPwait(_)) {
1459        return false;
1460    }
1461    get_fd(call).is_some_and(|fd| {
1462        guest
1463            .thread_state()
1464            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.is_guest_held())
1465            .unwrap_or(false)
1466    })
1467}
1468
1469/// The generic single-fd poll's guest-only claim and whether it rests on
1470/// revocable guest-held marks. Socketpair origin selects live internal routing,
1471/// but only its current guest-held mark can establish guest-only readiness.
1472/// Mark-dependent requests remain subject to the scheduler's export revocation,
1473/// including requests that were already published when the export was reported.
1474/// Other internal descriptors retain their existing readiness classification.
1475/// In particular, this does not repair guest-only claims for pipes exported
1476/// through SCM_RIGHTS or received from outside the guest.
1477fn single_fd_poll_readiness<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1478    guest: &mut G,
1479    call: Syscall,
1480    internal_fd: bool,
1481) -> (bool, bool) {
1482    let socketpair = get_fd(call).is_some_and(|fd| {
1483        guest
1484            .thread_state()
1485            .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.is_socketpair_endpoint())
1486            .unwrap_or(false)
1487    });
1488    let relies_on_guest_held_marks =
1489        (!internal_fd || socketpair) && syscall_targets_guest_held_fd(guest, call);
1490    let polls_guest_state_only = (internal_fd && !socketpair) || relies_on_guest_held_marks;
1491    (polls_guest_state_only, relies_on_guest_held_marks)
1492}
1493
1494/// The most entries a `poll` or `ppoll` may have for
1495/// `poll_targets_guest_held` to read them.
1496const GUEST_HELD_POLL_MAX_FDS: usize = 1024;
1497
1498/// Whether only guests can make a `poll` or `ppoll` of the `nfds` entries at
1499/// `fds` ready: every entry Linux polls (a non-negative descriptor) names a
1500/// guest-held descriptor (`DetFd::is_guest_held`) in the caller's table.
1501/// Linux ignores an entry with a negative descriptor. An empty array, one
1502/// larger than `GUEST_HELD_POLL_MAX_FDS` or one Detcore cannot read counts as
1503/// not guest-held, which keeps the call's classification as it was. It feeds
1504/// only `Resources::polls_guest_state_only`.
1505pub(crate) fn poll_targets_guest_held<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1506    guest: &mut G,
1507    fds: Option<usize>,
1508    nfds: usize,
1509) -> bool {
1510    if nfds == 0 || nfds > GUEST_HELD_POLL_MAX_FDS {
1511        return false;
1512    }
1513    let Some(address) = fds.and_then(Addr::<u8>::from_raw) else {
1514        return false;
1515    };
1516    let mut bytes = vec![0u8; nfds * std::mem::size_of::<libc::pollfd>()];
1517    if guest.memory().read_exact(address, &mut bytes).is_err() {
1518        return false;
1519    }
1520    let polled = pollfd_descriptors(&bytes);
1521    !polled.is_empty()
1522        && polled.into_iter().all(|fd| {
1523            guest
1524                .thread_state()
1525                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.is_guest_held())
1526                .unwrap_or(false)
1527        })
1528}
1529
1530/// The descriptors Linux polls in a `pollfd` array's bytes: each entry's
1531/// `fd` when it is not negative.
1532fn pollfd_descriptors(bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<i32> {
1533    let (entries, _) = bytes.as_chunks::<{ std::mem::size_of::<libc::pollfd>() }>();
1534    entries
1535        .iter()
1536        .map(|entry| i32::from_ne_bytes([entry[0], entry[1], entry[2], entry[3]]))
1537        .filter(|fd| *fd >= 0)
1538        .collect()
1539}
1540
1541/// Whether `call` is a `read` or `readv` of a descriptor Detcore records as
1542/// a pipe (`FdType::Pipe`: a pipe, or a FIFO that joined internal polling),
1543/// the restartable reads a recorded private `SIGCHLD` ends
1544/// (`Resources::private_sigchld_decides`; R2b-2 stage 3,
1545/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273). A socket read keeps
1546/// holding it (rev4 1e).
1547fn reads_a_pipe<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(guest: &mut G, call: Syscall) -> bool {
1548    matches!(call, Syscall::Read(_) | Syscall::Readv(_))
1549        && get_fd(call).is_some_and(|fd| {
1550            guest
1551                .thread_state()
1552                .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Pipe))
1553                .unwrap_or(false)
1554        })
1555}
1556
1557/// Does `call` read a descriptor Detcore records as a signalfd
1558/// (`Resources::reads_signalfd`)? Only `read`, `readv` and `preadv2` at the
1559/// current offset can: a positioned read of a signalfd fails with ESPIPE.
1560fn call_reads_signalfd<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1561    guest: &mut G,
1562    call: Syscall,
1563) -> bool {
1564    let fd = match call {
1565        Syscall::Read(c) => c.fd(),
1566        Syscall::Readv(c) => c.fd(),
1567        Syscall::Preadv2(c) => c.fd(),
1568        _ => return false,
1569    };
1570    guest
1571        .thread_state()
1572        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.ty() == crate::fd::FdType::Signalfd)
1573        .unwrap_or(false)
1574}
1575
1576/// The descriptor a `read`, `readv` or `preadv2` reads (`Resources::read_fd`).
1577fn read_family_fd(call: Syscall) -> Option<i32> {
1578    match call {
1579        Syscall::Read(c) => Some(c.fd()),
1580        Syscall::Readv(c) => Some(c.fd()),
1581        Syscall::Preadv2(c) => Some(c.fd()),
1582        _ => None,
1583    }
1584}
1585
1586/// Does replay answer this call from the recording rather than by running it?
1587///
1588/// This follows the replayer's dispatch. It serves `accept`, `accept4`, `connect`,
1589/// `sendto`, `sendmsg`, `recvfrom` and `recvmsg` from its log whatever the descriptor
1590/// is, so they count on any descriptor, a listener received over `SCM_RIGHTS` (an
1591/// exported alias, or a new description another process sent) included; an
1592/// untagged accept there would let its stand-in take a slot at a host-timed point.
1593/// `read`, `readv`, `write` and `writev` count only on a
1594/// socket Detcore created with `socket(2)` or `accept(2)`: on other descriptors,
1595/// replay may run them for real as eventfd operations, which can block, so an unknown
1596/// descriptor is not assumed to be served from the log. `recvmmsg` and `sendmmsg` are
1597/// recorded by neither recorder nor replayer (on an accepted connection record/replay
1598/// refuses them, see `refuse_log_served_mmsg`).
1599fn replay_serves_socket_call_from_log<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1600    guest: &mut G,
1601    call: Syscall,
1602) -> bool {
1603    let fd = match call {
1604        Syscall::Accept(_)
1605        | Syscall::Accept4(_)
1606        | Syscall::Connect(_)
1607        | Syscall::Sendto(_)
1608        | Syscall::Sendmsg(_)
1609        | Syscall::Recvfrom(_)
1610        | Syscall::Recvmsg(_) => return true,
1611        Syscall::Read(s) => s.fd(),
1612        Syscall::Readv(s) => s.fd(),
1613        Syscall::Write(s) => s.fd(),
1614        Syscall::Writev(s) => s.fd(),
1615        _ => return false,
1616    };
1617    is_log_served_socket(guest, fd)
1618}
1619
1620/// Does replay answer this otherwise blocking call from the recording alone?
1621///
1622/// The replayer serves `poll`, `ppoll`, `select` and `pselect6` from the log
1623/// without running them. `epoll_wait` is excluded because replay reapplies its
1624/// side effects on live descriptors, which may block.
1625fn replay_serves_blocking_call_from_log(call: Syscall) -> bool {
1626    match call {
1627        Syscall::Ppoll(_) | Syscall::Pselect6(_) => true,
1628        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
1629        Syscall::Poll(_) | Syscall::Select(_) => true,
1630        _ => false,
1631    }
1632}
1633
1634/// Is `fd` a socket whose connection record and replay keep only in the log?
1635///
1636/// That is a socket Detcore created with `socket(2)` or `accept(2)`, but not a
1637/// socketpair endpoint: replay recreates a socketpair, and its operations run
1638/// live.
1639fn is_log_served_socket<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(guest: &mut G, fd: i32) -> bool {
1640    guest
1641        .thread_state()
1642        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
1643            matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Socket) && !detfd.is_socketpair_endpoint()
1644        })
1645        .unwrap_or(false)
1646}
1647
1648/// Is `fd` a connection that `accept(2)` or `accept4(2)` returned? Record and
1649/// replay keep such a connection only in the log, and replay stands in an
1650/// eventfd for it, so an operation that runs live during replay meets that
1651/// eventfd rather than a connected socket.
1652pub(crate) fn is_accepted_connection<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
1653    guest: &mut G,
1654    fd: i32,
1655) -> bool {
1656    guest
1657        .thread_state()
1658        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| detfd.is_accepted_connection())
1659        .unwrap_or(false)
1660}
