1787/// A system call which may or may not block, but which can be MADE nonblocking.
1788// `async_trait` rewrites `into_nonblocking` to return a boxed future and marks it
1789// `#[must_use]`; the future is already `#[must_use]` in its own right, so clippy sees a double
1790// annotation. Both are generated, so the lint's own suggestion -- give the `must_use` an explicit
1791// reason -- cannot be applied at this source. Allowed at the item rather than crate-wide so any
1792// hand-written double `must_use` elsewhere still fails `#![deny(clippy::all)]` (detcore/src/lib.rs:35).
1793// Appeared with nightly-2026-08-08 (rustc 1.99.0-nightly 1a98b1e13) against an unchanged tree.
1794#[allow(clippy::double_must_use)]
1795#[async_trait]
1796pub trait NonblockableSyscall: SyscallInfo {
1797    /// Convert the system call to a nonblocking version of itself.  Sometimes this means
1798    /// setting a zero timeout, and sometimes it means something else.
1799    ///
1800    /// This may need to stack allocate, so it returns a StackGuard.
1801    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
1802        self,
1803        guest: &mut G,
1804    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>);
1805
1806    /// Check if the result (in nonblocking mode) is analogous to blocking in blocking mode.
1807    /// I.e. the result means "try again".
1808    fn syscall_would_have_blocked(&self, res: Result<i64, Errno>) -> bool {
1809        res == Ok(0)
1810    }
1811
1812    /// Whether the call's own flags keep it from waiting on a file the guest
1813    /// left blocking: `MSG_DONTWAIT` on a socket send or receive, which Linux
1814    /// turns into a zero timeout (`sock_rcvtimeo`, `sock_sndtimeo`), so the
1815    /// call returns at once, failing with `EAGAIN` where it would wait. Linux
1816    /// adds the same flag to every call on an `O_NONBLOCK` socket, so such a
1817    /// call runs once, as on a nonblocking file (`IOAction::PassThru`), instead
1818    /// of being retried until it stops failing with `EAGAIN`.
1819    fn flags_forbid_waiting(&self) -> bool {
1820        false
1821    }
1822
1823    /// Whether the call is a receive with `MSG_ERRQUEUE`, which reads the
1824    /// socket's error queue. Whether that waits depends on the socket's
1825    /// protocol (`crate::fd::error_queue_read_never_waits`): a UDP or TCP socket
1826    /// fails with `EAGAIN` at once when the queue is empty, while AF_UNIX
1827    /// ignores the flag and receives as usual.
1828    fn reads_error_queue(&self) -> bool {
1829        false
1830    }
1831
1832    /// Return the errno used when a signal interrupts this internally polled syscall.
1833    /// Most blocking I/O is restartable when its handler uses `SA_RESTART`.
1834    fn signal_interrupt_errno(&self) -> Errno {
1835        Errno::ERESTARTSYS
1836    }
1837
1838    /// Return the errno for an interrupting signal that ends this wait after it began,
1839    /// on a backend that decides interruption from the kernel's signal state
1840    /// (`supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`). The kernel applies the
1841    /// guest's disposition to it on resume, so it must be the restart code Linux uses
1842    /// for this call: a handler then turns it into `EINTR` or a restart, and a signal
1843    /// with no handler restarts the call.
1844    fn kernel_restart_errno(&self) -> Errno {
1845        self.signal_interrupt_errno()
1846    }
1847
1848    /// Whether Linux restarts this call, after [`kernel_restart_errno`](Self::kernel_restart_errno)
1849    /// with no handler, through a restart block that keeps its absolute deadline: a
1850    /// `poll` with a positive timeout (`do_restart_poll`) and a timed `FUTEX_WAIT` or
1851    /// `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` (`futex_wait_restart`). Its restart code is then
1852    /// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, and
1853    /// Detcore keeps the deadline in a [`RestartBlock`] for the `restart_syscall` that
1854    /// the kernel runs next (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358>).
1855    ///
1856    /// Such a wait is also not ended by a default job-control stop signal
1857    /// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting_wait`), so that a stop Linux discards in an
1858    /// orphaned process group does not end the call before its deadline.
1859    fn restart_keeps_deadline(&self) -> bool {
1860        false
1861    }
1862
1863    /// Signals the wait itself accepts rather than being interrupted by, read from
1864    /// guest memory. Only `rt_sigtimedwait` has any.
1865    fn signals_consumed_by_wait<M: MemoryAccess>(&self, _memory: &M) -> KernelSigset {
1866        0
1867    }
1868
1869    /// Whether this call is a receive that Linux ends without waiting once
1870    /// its socket's read side is shut down (`finish_after_read_shutdown`).
1871    fn ends_at_read_shutdown(&self) -> bool {
1872        false
1873    }
1874
1875    /// Convert a physical nonblocking completion into the result expected by the guest.
1876    /// `retried` is true after a prior result was classified as blocked.
1877    fn normalize_nonblocking_result(
1878        &self,
1879        res: Result<i64, Errno>,
1880        _retried: bool,
1881    ) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
1882        res
1883    }
1884}
1885
1886/// A system call which can logically timeout and then would return a given value
1887/// indicating that timeout.
1888pub trait TimeoutableSyscall: SyscallInfo {
1889    /// What would the syscall return IF it timed out?
1890    fn timeout_return_val(&self) -> Result<i64, Errno>;
1891}
1892
1893fn interrupted_write_result<C: NonblockableSyscall>(
1894    call: &C,
1895    written_total: usize,
1896    disposition: Option<WaitSignalDisposition>,
1897) -> Option<Result<i64, Error>> {
1898    match disposition {
1899        None => None,
1900        Some(_) if written_total > 0 => Some(Ok(written_total as i64)),
1901        Some(_) => Some(Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into())),
1902    }
1903}
1904
1905fn pipe_writev_resources(dettid: DetTid, call: reverie::syscalls::Writev) -> Resources {
1906    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
1907    resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
1908    resources.fyi(call.name());
1909    resources.set_signal_interrupt_errno(call.signal_interrupt_errno());
1910    // Polls with every ordinary signal blocked and checks the target's
1911    // disposition itself after a `Signaled` wake, so the scheduler's drain
1912    // must not filter by the kernel mask (`execute_blocking_pipe_writev`).
1913    resources.decides_signal_interruption_itself = true;
1914    resources.polls_guest_state_only = true;
1915    resources
1916}

1918#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
1919#[async_trait]
1920impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Poll {
1921    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
1922        self,
1923        _guest: &mut G,
1924    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
1925        (self.with_timeout(0), None)
1926    }
1927
1928    fn signal_interrupt_errno(&self) -> Errno {
1929        Errno::EINTR
1930    }
1931
1932    /// Linux ends an interrupted `poll` with a restart code that a handler turns into
1933    /// `EINTR` and that restarts the call when no handler runs.
1934    ///
1935    /// With a positive timeout that code is Linux's own, `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`: the
1936    /// kernel then runs `restart_syscall`, which Detcore resumes with the deadline it
1937    /// kept ([`RestartBlock`]), as `do_restart_poll` does
1938    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358). An infinite timeout has no
1939    /// deadline to keep, so it returns `ERESTARTNOHAND`, and running `poll` again with
1940    /// its original arguments is the same restart.
1941    fn kernel_restart_errno(&self) -> Errno {
1942        if self.restart_keeps_deadline() {
1943            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
1944        } else {
1945            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
1946        }
1947    }
1948
1949    /// A zero timeout never blocks, and a negative one never expires.
1950    fn restart_keeps_deadline(&self) -> bool {
1951        self.timeout() > 0
1952    }
1953}

1957    fn timeout_return_val(&self) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
1958        Ok(0)
1959    }
1960}

1962#[async_trait]
1963impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Ppoll {
1964    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
1965        self,
1966        guest: &mut G,
1967    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
1968        let (tp, guard) = zero_timespec(guest).await;
1969        // SAFETY: `tp` points to exclusively owned scratch storage kept alive by `guard`.
1970        let tp = unsafe { tp.into_mut() };
1971        (self.with_timeout(Some(tp)), Some(guard))
1972    }
1973
1974    fn signal_interrupt_errno(&self) -> Errno {
1975        Errno::EINTR
1976    }
1977
1978    /// Linux ends an interrupted `ppoll` with a restart code that a handler turns into
1979    /// `EINTR` and that restarts the call when no handler runs.
1980    fn kernel_restart_errno(&self) -> Errno {
1981        Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
1982    }
1983}

1986    fn timeout_return_val(&self) -> Result<i64, Errno> {

2013// `epoll_pwait` was the one member of the
2014// poll/epoll family with no nonblocking form, even though `Ppoll` -- the
2015// sigmask variant of `poll` -- has had one all along. Programs that issue
2016// `epoll_pwait` DIRECTLY (libuv does, which is how the `cmake` hang surfaced)
2017// therefore reached an unhandled path while the `EpollWait` impl above went
2018// unused by them. Note this is NOT glibc's `epoll_wait(2)` on x86_64: glibc
2019// only spells it `epoll_pwait` where `__NR_epoll_wait` is absent, which x86_64
2020// is not. With a NULL sigmask the two calls are semantically identical, so the
2021// nonblocking form is the same: timeout 0, EINTR, and a 0 (no events) timeout
2022// return.
2023#[async_trait]

2026        self,
2027        _guest: &mut G,
2028    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2029        (self.with_timeout(0), None)
2030    }
2031
2032    fn signal_interrupt_errno(&self) -> Errno {
2033        Errno::EINTR
2034    }
2035}

2037impl TimeoutableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::EpollPwait {
2038    fn timeout_return_val(&self) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
2039        Ok(0)

2043/// What to do with the copy of the standard `signal` this thread just took
2044/// (`rt_sigtimedwait`, a signalfd record), after which its queues held
2045/// `after` (when read): drop it, as a copy Linux discarded when it was sent
2046/// or a stale POSIX timer entry, or return it with another siginfo
2047/// (`DiscardedSignalControl::Take`). The scheduler pops and promotes either
2048/// way.
2049pub(crate) async fn take_outcome<T, G>(
2050    guest: &mut G,
2051    signal: i32,
2052    after: Option<(u64, u64)>,
2053) -> crate::scheduler::posix_timer_coalesce::TakeOutcome
2054where
2055    T: RecordOrReplay,
2056    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2057{
2058    use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::DiscardedSignalAnswer;
2059    use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::DiscardedSignalControl;
2060    use crate::scheduler::posix_timer_coalesce::TakeOutcome;
2061    let at = guest.thread_state().thread_logical_time.as_nanos();
2062    match crate::tool_global::discarded_signal(
2063        guest,
2064        DiscardedSignalControl::Take { signal, at, after },
2065    )
2066    .await
2067    {
2068        DiscardedSignalAnswer::Taken(outcome) => outcome,
2069        _ => TakeOutcome {
2070            skip: false,
2071            rewrite: None,
2072        },
2073    }
2074}
2075
2076async fn zero_timespec<'stack, T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2077    guest: &mut G,
2078) -> (Addr<'stack, Timespec>, <G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard) {
2079    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
2080    let tp_val = Timespec {
2081        tv_sec: 0,
2082        tv_nsec: 0,
2083    };
2084    let tp = stack.push(tp_val);
2085    let guard = stack.commit().expect("stack.commit to succeed");
2086    (tp, guard)
2087}
2088
2089#[async_trait]
2090impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Wait4 {
2091    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2092        self,
2093        _guest: &mut G,
2094    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2095        let call2 = self.with_options(self.options() | WaitPidFlag::WNOHANG);
2096        (call2, None)
2097    }
2098
2099    // Child has not changed state yet, so we go to the scheduler and wait to poll again.
2100    // In scenarios with lots of outstanding waits, this polling strategy can change the asymptotic
2101    // complexity of the program. Ideally, we would model the blocking `wait4` (and process state
2102    // transitions) directly in the scheduler, and execute it only when we know it will complete.
2103    //
2104    // The polling backoff strategy mitigates this problem however.
2105    fn syscall_would_have_blocked(&self, res: Result<i64, Errno>) -> bool {
2106        res == Ok(0)
2107    }
2108}
2109
2110#[async_trait]
2111/// Used only for FUTEX_WAIT
2112impl NonblockableSyscall for reverie::syscalls::Futex {
2113    async fn into_nonblocking<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>>(
2114        self,
2115        guest: &mut G,
2116    ) -> (Self, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2117        let (tp, guard) = zero_timespec(guest).await;
2118        (self.with_timeout(Some(tp)), Some(guard))
2119    }
2120
2121    fn syscall_would_have_blocked(&self, res: Result<i64, Errno>) -> bool {
2122        // EAGAIN can mean the futex wait's compare-and-block failed and we should return that to
2123        // the guest.  With timeout=0, the timeout is what shows that it would have blocked.
2124        res == Err(Errno::ETIMEDOUT)
2125    }
2126
2127    /// Linux restarts an untimed `FUTEX_WAIT` under `SA_RESTART` (`-ERESTARTSYS`), but a
2128    /// timed wait returns `-ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, which a handler always turns into
2129    /// `EINTR` (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
2130    ///
2131    /// A timed `FUTEX_WAIT` or `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` returns Linux's code: with no
2132    /// handler the kernel then runs `restart_syscall`, which Detcore resumes with the
2133    /// deadline it kept ([`RestartBlock`]), as `futex_wait_restart` does
2134    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358). Linux's `futex_wait` keeps
2135    /// the absolute deadline of every timed wait in the restart block, so a
2136    /// `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` deadline the guest moves in memory after the wait began
2137    /// does not change when the restarted wait ends. `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET` used to
2138    /// return `ERESTARTNOHAND`, which ran the call again with its original
2139    /// arguments and so read the deadline again (round-10 finding Medium 4 on
2140    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
2141    ///
2142    /// FUTEX_LOCK_PI and FUTEX_LOCK_PI2 return `-ERESTARTNOINTR`, which the
2143    /// kernel restarts whatever the handler (`futex_lock_pi`,
2144    /// kernel/futex/pi.c:1124 at v6.16).
2145    fn kernel_restart_errno(&self) -> Errno {
2146        if matches!(
2147            self.futex_op() & libc::FUTEX_CMD_MASK,
2148            libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI | libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI2
2149        ) {
2150            Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR
2151        } else if self.restart_keeps_deadline() {
2152            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
2153        } else if self.timeout().is_some() {
2154            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
2155        } else {
2156            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
2157        }
2158    }
2159
2160    /// Every timed wait: `FUTEX_WAIT`'s relative timeout and `FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET`'s
2161    /// absolute deadline both become the absolute deadline Linux's restart keeps.
2162    fn restart_keeps_deadline(&self) -> bool {
2163        matches!(
2164            self.futex_op() & libc::FUTEX_CMD_MASK,
2165            libc::FUTEX_WAIT | libc::FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET
2166        ) && self.timeout().is_some()
2167    }
2168}

2196    /// Signals in the wait's own set are accepted by it, not interrupting. A set
2197    /// that cannot be read counts as empty, which nothing observes: the wait's
2198    /// first probe runs before any pending signal is considered
2199    /// (`KernelSignalWait::inject_first_probe`) and fails with `EFAULT`, as Linux
2200    /// fails the call when it cannot copy the set.
2201    fn signals_consumed_by_wait<M: MemoryAccess>(&self, memory: &M) -> KernelSigset {
2202        self.set()
2203            .and_then(|set| memory.read_value(set.cast::<KernelSigset>()).ok())
2204            .unwrap_or(0)
2205    }

2319/// A common helper shared among several network syscalls.
2320/// We can't actually CONVERT these syscalls into nonblocking, but we can assert that they are by
2321/// checking the status of their file descriptor.
2322fn network_comm_syscall<T: RecordOrReplay, G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, C: SyscallInfo + Into<Syscall>>(
2323    call: C,
2324    guest: &mut G,
2325) -> (C, Option<<G::Stack as Stack>::StackGuard>) {
2326    // Already nonblocking because we've assured the socket is.
2327    let fd = get_fd(call.into()).unwrap_or_else(|| {
2328        panic!(
2329            "network_comm_syscall called on invalid syscall / unknown fd: {}",
2330            call.name()
2331        );
2332    });
2333    guest
2334        .thread_state()
2335        .with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
2336            assert!(
2337                detfd.physically_nonblocking(),
2338                "expecting sockets/pipes to be physically nonblocking"
2339            );
2340        })
2341        .unwrap();
2342    (call, None)
2343}

2530/// Transform a syscall to nonblocking, then retry it until it returns a successful result.
2531/// Retry a nonblockizable syscall (e.g. a pipe/socket read or write) until it succeeds.
2532///
2533/// `subtool` selects how each poll iteration executes the underlying syscall. Pass
2534/// `Some(detcore)` in record/replay mode for a container-INTERNAL fd (currently pipes):
2535/// each iteration is then routed through `Detcore::record_or_replay`, so the read's
2536/// bytes (and every intervening `EAGAIN`) are captured in the recording and reproduced
2537/// verbatim on replay. Without this, an internal-pipe read on the InternalIOPolling path
2538/// bypasses the recorder and replay reads live from a pipe whose cross-process writer
2539/// schedule is not reproduced -- the reader sees EOF instead of the recorded data and
2540/// replay desyncs. Pass `None` for plain `hermit run` (no recording) or for external fds.
2541pub async fn retry_nonblocking_syscall<T, G, C>(
2542    guest: &mut G,
2543    call: C,
2544    rsrc: Resources,
2545    subtool: Option<&Detcore<T>>,
2546) -> Result<i64, Error>
2547where
2548    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
2549    T: RecordOrReplay,
2550    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2551{
2552    // Bogus 99 return value is dead code below:
2553    retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(guest, call, rsrc, None, subtool).await
2554}

2556/// What a wait that ended with `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` keeps for the
2557/// `restart_syscall` that Linux runs next when no handler runs
2558/// (`NonblockableSyscall::restart_keeps_deadline`). Linux keeps the call and its
2559/// absolute deadline in the thread's restart block (`do_restart_poll`,
2560/// `futex_wait_restart`). Detcore emulates the wait, so the kernel's restart block
2561/// does not describe it, and Detcore keeps its own
2562/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358). A `poll` with a positive
2563/// timeout that Detcore runs in the kernel keeps one too: the kernel's restart
2564/// block describes that poll, but Detcore runs the restart through its
2565/// recorder (`RestartCall::KernelPoll`).
2566///
2567/// The record lives until the thread's next syscall, which takes it
2568/// (`Detcore::handle_syscall_event`). Other first syscalls, sigreturn and exec
2569/// discard the record; separate threads and newly initialized children have
2570/// independent records. A caught handler does not discard it: Linux resets its
2571/// restart block at sigreturn (`restore_sigcontext`), not when it sets up the
2572/// handler, so a handler whose first syscall is `restart_syscall` resumes the
2573/// interrupted wait with the copied arguments and deadline. Detcore does the
2574/// same when that call stops at the interrupted call's address, as it does
2575/// through libc's `syscall()` (the `restartfirst` mode of the
2576/// `external_signal_interrupt` guest). Linux also keeps its restart block across
2577/// the handler's other syscalls and resumes it from any address; Detcore does
2578/// not, so a `restart_syscall` after another syscall or at another address takes
2579/// the unsupported-syscall policy.
2580///
2581/// A wait that Detcore ran in the kernel as the guest made it keeps a record
2582/// too, holding no deadline: its `restart_syscall` then goes to the kernel,
2583/// whose restart block describes the wait (`RestartCall::InKernel`).
2584#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
2585pub(crate) struct RestartBlock {
2586    /// The instruction pointer at the interrupted call's syscall stop: the address
2587    /// after its `syscall` instruction. The kernel's restart moves the instruction
2588    /// pointer back onto that instruction with `restart_syscall` in `rax`, so the
2589    /// restart stops at the same address.
2590    pub(crate) rip: u64,
2591    /// The wait's absolute deadline, or `None` for a wait without one and for a
2592    /// kernel-run poll, which keeps its own (`RestartCall::KernelPoll`).
2593    pub(crate) deadline: Option<LogicalTime>,
2594    /// The interrupted call.
2595    pub(crate) call: RestartCall,
2596}
2597
2598/// Guest scratch for one injected `poll` probe, reserved with the rest of a
2599/// caller's scratch before it commits the stack ([`PollProbe::reserve`]).
2600///
2601/// aarch64 has no `poll` syscall. Its `ppoll` runs the same `do_sys_poll`
2602/// (`fs/select.c`) but takes the timeout by pointer, so a probe there needs a
2603/// slot of guest memory for the timeout. x86_64 injects `poll` itself and
2604/// reserves nothing.
2605#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
2606pub(crate) struct PollProbe {
2607    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
2608    timeout: AddrMut<'static, Timespec>,
2609}
2610
2611impl PollProbe {
2612    /// Reserve the probe's scratch on `stack`, before the caller commits it.
2613    pub(crate) fn reserve<S: Stack>(stack: &mut S) -> Self {
2614        #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2615        return {
2616            let _ = stack;
2617            Self {}
2618        };
2619        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
2620        return Self {
2621            timeout: stack.reserve(),
2622        };
2623    }
2624
2625    /// The probe of the `nfds` entries at `fds`, waiting at most
2626    /// `timeout_millis` (forever when negative), as `poll` takes them.
2627    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2628    pub(crate) fn call<M: MemoryAccess>(
2629        self,
2630        _memory: M,
2631        fds: AddrMut<'_, libc::pollfd>,
2632        nfds: libc::nfds_t,
2633        timeout_millis: libc::c_int,
2634    ) -> Result<syscalls::Poll, Errno> {
2635        Ok(syscalls::Poll::new()
2636            .with_fds(Some(fds.cast()))
2637            .with_nfds(nfds)
2638            .with_timeout(timeout_millis))
2639    }
2640
2641    /// The probe of the `nfds` entries at `fds`, waiting at most
2642    /// `timeout_millis` (forever when negative), as `poll` takes them: a
2643    /// `ppoll` with no signal mask, whose timeout this stages first.
2644    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
2645    pub(crate) fn call<M: MemoryAccess>(
2646        self,
2647        mut memory: M,
2648        fds: AddrMut<'_, libc::pollfd>,
2649        nfds: libc::nfds_t,
2650        timeout_millis: libc::c_int,
2651    ) -> Result<syscalls::Ppoll, Errno> {
2652        let timeout = if timeout_millis < 0 {
2653            None
2654        } else {
2655            let timeout = Timespec {
2656                tv_sec: libc::time_t::from(timeout_millis / 1000),
2657                tv_nsec: libc::c_long::from(timeout_millis % 1000) * 1_000_000,
2658            };
2659            memory.write_value(self.timeout, &timeout)?;
2660            Some(self.timeout)
2661        };
2662        Ok(syscalls::Ppoll::new()
2663            .with_fds(Some(fds.cast()))
2664            .with_nfds(nfds)
2665            .with_timeout(timeout)
2666            .with_sigmask(None)
2667            .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE))
2668    }
2669}
2670
2671/// A call whose restart keeps its deadline.
2672#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
2673pub(crate) enum RestartCall {
2674    /// Only x86_64 has `poll`; aarch64's `ppoll` restarts with
2675    /// `ERESTARTNOHAND`, not a restart block.
2676    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2677    Poll(syscalls::Poll),
2678    /// A `poll` with a positive timeout that Detcore ran in the kernel
2679    /// (`Detcore::handle_external_poll`: record and replay, and
2680    /// `--no-sequentialize-threads`), with the end of its timeout. Its restart
2681    /// runs the poll again in the kernel, through the recorder, with the time
2682    /// left (`Detcore::resume_kernel_poll`). Only x86_64 has `poll`.
2683    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2684    KernelPoll(syscalls::Poll, KernelPollDeadline),
2685    Futex(syscalls::Futex),
2686    /// A relative `nanosleep` or `clock_nanosleep` that ended for a claimed
2687    /// `SIGCHLD` (`syscalls::signal::SleepSignal::Claimed`).
2688    Nanosleep(reverie::syscalls::family::NanosleepFamily),
2689    /// A timed wait that Detcore ran in the kernel as the guest made it, which
2690    /// the kernel's own restart block describes (`inject_keeping_kernel_restart`):
2691    /// a sleep or futex wait without sequentialized threads. Its
2692    /// `restart_syscall` goes to the kernel, which resumes the wait until the
2693    /// end it kept.
2694    InKernel(Sysno),
2695}
2696
2697/// Where the timeout of a `poll` Detcore runs in the kernel ends
2698/// (`RestartCall::KernelPoll`), on the host's monotonic clock. That clock is
2699/// the one the kernel wait runs on and the one Linux's restart keeps its end
2700/// time on (`poll_select_set_timeout`, `do_restart_poll`), while the thread's
2701/// logical time stands still as long as it blocks in the kernel, so an end on
2702/// logical time would let every restart wait the whole timeout again.
2703///
2704/// `None` under record and replay: there the restart reruns the poll with the
2705/// timeout it was issued with. The recording holds each poll's arguments and
2706/// replay checks them, and no clock that replay reproduces moves while the
2707/// poll blocks, so a time left is not replayed today.
2708#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
2709#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
2710pub(crate) struct KernelPollDeadline(pub(crate) Option<std::time::Instant>);
2711
2712/// The result of an injected `restart_syscall` (`resume_kernel_wait`).
2713fn resumed_kernel_wait_result(result: Result<i64, Errno>) -> Result<i64, Errno> {
2714    match result {
2715        Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS) => Err(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK),
2716        other => other,
2717    }
2718}
2719
2720impl RestartBlock {
2721    /// The record, if a `restart_syscall` that stopped at `rip` is the kernel's
2722    /// restart of the interrupted call. At any other address the guest made the
2723    /// call itself.
2724    pub(crate) fn resumed_at(self, rip: u64) -> Option<Self> {
2725        (self.rip == rip).then_some(self)
2726    }
2727}
2728
2729/// Injects `call`, which the kernel runs as the guest made it, and keeps a
2730/// record for the kernel's restart when a signal ends it with
2731/// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` (`RestartCall::InKernel`). Linux then restarts the
2732/// wait through `restart_syscall` with the end time it stored in the thread's
2733/// restart block (`hrtimer_nanosleep_restart`, `futex_wait_restart`), and that
2734/// block is the one this call left: nothing else Detcore runs for the thread
2735/// before the restart sets or resets it.
2736pub(crate) async fn inject_keeping_kernel_restart<T, G, S>(
2737    guest: &mut G,
2738    call: S,
2739) -> Result<i64, Error>
2740where
2741    T: RecordOrReplay,
2742    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2743    S: SyscallInfo,
2744{
2745    let sysno = call.number();
2746    let result = guest.inject(call).await.map_err(Error::from);
2747    keep_restart_block(guest, &result, RestartCall::InKernel(sysno), None).await;
2748    result
2749}
2750
2751/// The kernel's restart of a wait Detcore ran in the kernel
2752/// (`RestartCall::InKernel`): `restart_syscall` itself, which resumes the wait
2753/// from the thread's restart block. A signal that ends the resumed wait
2754/// leaves `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` and the block again, so the record is kept
2755/// again. A signal that stops the injected call before it runs leaves the
2756/// block unused; the result is then the same `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, never
2757/// the `ERESTARTSYS` the backend reports, which would make the kernel rerun
2758/// `restart_syscall` without a record (`resumed_kernel_wait_result`).
2759pub(crate) async fn resume_kernel_wait<T, G>(
2760    guest: &mut G,
2761    restart: Syscall,
2762    sysno: Sysno,
2763) -> Result<i64, Error>
2764where
2765    T: RecordOrReplay,
2766    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2767{
2768    let result = resumed_kernel_wait_result(guest.inject(restart).await).map_err(Error::from);
2769    keep_restart_block(guest, &result, RestartCall::InKernel(sysno), None).await;
2770    result
2771}
2772
2773/// Keeps `deadline` for the kernel's restart of `call` when the wait ended with
2774/// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` (`RestartBlock`).
2775pub(crate) async fn keep_restart_block<T, G>(
2776    guest: &mut G,
2777    result: &Result<i64, Error>,
2778    call: RestartCall,
2779    deadline: Option<LogicalTime>,
2780) where
2781    T: RecordOrReplay,
2782    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2783{
2784    if matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(errno)) if *errno == Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK) {
2785        let rip = crate::arch::instruction_pointer(&guest.regs().await);
2786        let block = RestartBlock {
2787            rip,
2788            deadline,
2789            call,
2790        };
2791        tracing::trace!(
2792            "[tid {}] the wait keeps {:?} for its restart",
2793            guest.tid(),
2794            block
2795        );
2796        guest.thread_state_mut().restart_block = Some(block);
2797    }
2798}
2799
2800/// The restart code that ends a wait for a signal the backend holds and delivers
2801/// when the guest resumes. The backend passes a held signal on without reporting it
2802/// to the tool when the call returns `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, so for any signal but
2803/// `SIGSTOP`, which it never reports, the wait returns `ERESTARTNOHAND` instead. A
2804/// handler turns either code into `EINTR`, and a signal that kills the process
2805/// leaves no restart. The difference is a stop, which `SIGSTOP` alone can be here:
2806/// a default job-control stop does not end a wait whose restart keeps its deadline
2807/// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting_wait`).
2808///
2809/// A claimed relative `nanosleep` makes the opposite choice on purpose
2810/// (`syscalls::time`, `RestartCall::Nanosleep`): it returns
2811/// `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK`, so the held `SIGCHLD` is passed on unreported, and
2812/// the kernel's `restart_syscall` alone says no handler ran
2813/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4346).
2814fn held_signal_restart_errno(restart_errno: Errno, signal: i32) -> Errno {
2815    if restart_errno == Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK && signal != libc::SIGSTOP {
2816        Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
2817    } else {
2818        restart_errno
2819    }
2820}
2821
2822/// The deadline a polling request carries so the scheduler can restore a
2823/// backed-off poller once committed virtual time passes it
2824/// (`Resources::poll_deadline`, <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
2825/// `None` under record/replay, whose schedule must not change.
2826pub(crate) fn poll_deadline_for<T, G>(
2827    guest: &G,
2828    deadline: Option<LogicalTime>,
2829) -> Option<LogicalTime>
2830where
2831    T: RecordOrReplay,
2832    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2833{
2834    if guest.config().recordreplay_modes {
2835        None
2836    } else {
2837        deadline
2838    }
2839}
2840
2841/// Retry a non-blocking syscall until it succeeds. Set the timeout to zero for the actual
2842/// syscalls (retries), while monitoring the clock to see if/when the logical timeout
2843/// should trigger.  Timeout is passed as an ABSOLUTE TIME (not duration).
2844pub async fn retry_nonblocking_syscall_with_timeout<T, G, C>(
2845    guest: &mut G,
2846    call: C,
2847    rsrc: Resources,
2848    // Logical timeout:
2849    maybe_timeout: Option<LogicalTime>,
2850) -> Result<i64, Error>
2851where
2852    C: NonblockableSyscall + TimeoutableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
2853    T: RecordOrReplay,
2854    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2855{
2856    let maybe_tup = maybe_timeout.map(|t| (t, call.timeout_return_val()));
2857    // Under the in-guest delivery gate the private-mask machinery is never
2858    // taken (A5 step 3c.1c, D50): the helper below decides by the published
2859    // mask instead (`gated_wait_ends`).
2860    if guest
2861        .config()
2862        .backend
2863        .supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption
2864        && !guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery
2865    {
2866        return retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state(guest, call, rsrc, maybe_tup).await;
2867    }
2868    // poll/epoll_wait/futex/rt_sigtimedwait keep their existing execution (raw
2869    // inject_with_retry): their record/replay handling is out of scope for the internal
2870    // pipe data-ordering fix, and their fds are not necessarily internal pipes.
2871    retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper(guest, call, rsrc, maybe_tup, None).await
2872}
2873
2874/// The task whose kernel signal state the scheduler may read to decide which
2875/// signal ends an internal IO poll: the guest thread itself where guest thread
2876/// IDs name host tasks, and `None` elsewhere (KVM), where
2877/// `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>` would describe an unrelated host task.
2878pub(crate) fn guest_signal_state_task<T, G>(guest: &G) -> Option<(i32, i32)>
2879where
2880    T: RecordOrReplay,
2881    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2882{
2883    crate::procfs_inode::guest_tids_name_host_tasks(&guest.config().backend, None)
2884        .then(|| (guest.pid().as_raw(), guest.tid().as_raw()))
2885}
2886
2887/// Whether a signal that woke a poll would be delivered to this thread now,
2888/// read from the backend's own state of the thread: its current mask (the
2889/// old set of a query-only `rt_sigprocmask`) and each signal's disposition
2890/// (`wait_signal_disposition`). A blocked or ignored signal, or one whose
2891/// default action ignores it, does not.
2892async fn own_disposition_interrupts<T, G>(
2893    guest: &mut G,
2894    status: ResumeStatus,
2895    mask_addr: AddrMut<'_, KernelSigset>,
2896    action_addr: AddrMut<'_, KernelSigaction>,
2897) -> Result<bool, Error>
2898where
2899    T: RecordOrReplay,
2900    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2901{
2902    let query = syscalls::RtSigprocmask::new()
2903        .with_how(libc::SIG_BLOCK)
2904        .with_set(None)
2905        .with_oldset(Some(mask_addr.cast()))
2906        .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE);
2907    guest.inject_with_retry(query).await?;
2908    let mask: KernelSigset = guest.memory().read_value(mask_addr)?;
2909    Ok(
2910        wait_signal_disposition(guest, status, &mask, action_addr, true)
2911            .await?
2912            .is_some(),
2913    )
2914}
2915
2916// Private helper.
2917async fn retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper<T, G, C>(
2918    guest: &mut G,
2919    call0: C,
2920    rsrc: Resources,
2921    maybe_timeout: Option<(LogicalTime, Result<i64, Errno>)>,
2922    subtool: Option<&Detcore<T>>,
2923) -> Result<i64, Error>
2924where
2925    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
2926    T: RecordOrReplay,
2927    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
2928{
2929    // The signals the wait takes from the queue (rt_sigtimedwait's set).
2930    let consumed = call0.signals_consumed_by_wait(&guest.memory());
2931    // The memory a vectored call copies when it begins (its iovec array, and
2932    // a message's header, address and control data), which every attempt
2933    // below sees as it was now, as the kernel's one copy would be
2934    // (`EntryImport`). Linux copies it before the call can wait, so a thread
2935    // that rewrites it while the call waits changes nothing the call moves.
2936    // Boxed, so the call's future stays small (`hot_path_futures_stay_small`).
2937    let entry_import = EntryImport::capture(&guest.memory(), &call0.into()).map(Box::new);
2938    let mut completed_observation = None;
2939    // The stack-allocated memory here needs to live across the loop, which means
2940    // surviving multiple syscall injections:
2941    let (mut call, mut maybe_stackguard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
2942    let mut rsrc = rsrc.clone();
2943    rsrc.poll_deadline = poll_deadline_for(guest, maybe_timeout.map(|(deadline, _)| deadline));
2944    // A restartable call parked in internal IO polling, such as a `read` of an
2945    // empty pipe, is interrupted by a signal another task sends, as a parked
2946    // pipe write is (`pipe_writev_resources`). The marker lets the scheduler
2947    // record the signal for it (`Scheduler::notify_signal_pending`) and answer
2948    // its next turn `Signaled`; the call then returns `ERESTARTSYS`, and the
2949    // kernel applies the guest's disposition when it resumes: a handler runs
2950    // and the call fails with `EINTR` or restarts under `SA_RESTART`. Without
2951    // it, the poll never saw the signal and waited forever
2952    // (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4187>).
2953    if rsrc.signal_interrupt_errno().is_none()
2954        && rsrc.resources.len() == 1
2955        && rsrc.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
2956        && call.signal_interrupt_errno() == Errno::ERESTARTSYS
2957    {
2958        rsrc.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
2959        // Where guest thread IDs are not host tasks (KVM) the scheduler keeps
2960        // every signal: the call has made no progress when it returns
2961        // ERESTARTSYS, and the backend restarts it unless a signal it would
2962        // deliver is pending, so a blocked or ignored signal leaves it waiting.
2963        rsrc.signal_state_task = guest_signal_state_task(guest);
2964    }
2965    // D50 reader 2 under the in-guest delivery gate (A5 step 3c.1c): no
2966    // private kernel mask; once an attempt would block, the design's
2967    // deliverable set under the thread's published mask decides
2968    // (`gated_wait_ends`), at each turn, the first included.
2969    let gated = guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery;
2970    let checks_at_turn = !gated
2971        && rsrc.signal_interrupt_errno() == Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into_raw())
2972        && decides_interruption_at_turn(guest, rsrc.signal_state_task);
2973    // Where the turn decides, the call owns the guest's mask while it blocks
2974    // every blockable signal (`KernelSignalWait::block_in_place`), from the
2975    // first turn that finds a pending signal a private injection could take
2976    // until the call returns: two such signals once stopped the probe and
2977    // its retry in turn, and the backend's single held slot kept only the
2978    // second, so one handler never ran (Claude review of the R2b-2 design,
2979    // F1; https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, stage 2).
2980    let mut turn_wait = checks_at_turn
2981        .then(|| KernelSignalWait::new(guest, 0, false, call.signal_interrupt_errno()));
2982    let mut published = PublishedWaitMask::default();
2983
2984    let result: Result<i64, Error> = loop {
2985        let resumed = match call.into() {
2986            Syscall::Read(read) if maybe_timeout.is_none() && maybe_stackguard.is_none() => {
2987                crate::tool_global::polled_read_request(guest, read, rsrc.clone()).await
2988            }
2989            _ => resource_request(guest, rsrc.clone()).await,
2990        };
2991        // The turn's signals, read before its first injection
2992        // (`read_turn_signals`): the timerfd publication and the real-time
2993        // action below may inject, and a pending copy could stop that
2994        // injection and move into the backend's held slot. Every turn reads,
2995        // the first included, since a signal sent before the poll filed its
2996        // first request was admitted by no drain
2997        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273). A backend's own
2998        // observation of a signal (`Signaled(None)`) is trusted as it is: that
2999        // signal has already left the kernel's queue.
3000        // Once the call blocks, the turn decides under the guest's own mask,
3001        // which the call owns, never under the full one now installed (Codex
3002        // review of the R2b-2 design rev3, P2-1).
3003        let turn = if checks_at_turn && !matches!(resumed, ResumeStatus::Signaled(None)) {
3004            match turn_signals_with_block(
3005                guest,
3006                &mut turn_wait,
3007                true,
3008                committed_signals(&resumed),
3009                rsrc.private_sigchld_decides,
3010                &mut published,
3011            )
3012            .await
3013            {
3014                Ok(turn) => Some(turn),
3015                Err(error) => break Err(error),
3016            }
3017        } else {
3018            None
3019        };
3020        // A virtual timerfd this probe may observe is readable on the host
3021        // exactly when its virtual deadline has passed by this turn
3022        // (`crate::syscalls::timerfd`); its next deadline restores this
3023        // poller if it backs off.
3024        // Publishing may take the scratch stack, which the nonblocking form
3025        // holds; release it first and convert again after.
3026        let reconvert =
3027            maybe_stackguard.is_some() && crate::syscalls::timerfd::may_publish(guest, call.into());
3028        if reconvert {
3029            maybe_stackguard = None;
3030        }
3031        rsrc.poll_deadline = crate::syscalls::timerfd::publish_before_probe(
3032            guest,
3033            call.into(),
3034            maybe_timeout.map(|(deadline, _)| deadline),
3035        )
3036        .await;
3037        if reconvert {
3038            (call, maybe_stackguard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
3039        }
3040        // A signal ends the call only if it would still block, as Linux
3041        // checks for a pending signal only when the call must wait: a byte
3042        // written, or the last writer closed, before the signal is read
3043        // first. The probe below goes through the record/replay path like
3044        // every attempt (Codex review of
3045        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4198).
3046        // This call transfers nothing until it completes, so only a copy still
3047        // pending ends it (`TurnSignals::ends`).
3048        let signaled = match turn {
3049            Some(turn) => turn.ends(false),
3050            None => !gated && matches!(resumed, ResumeStatus::Signaled(_)),
3051        };
3052        // A pending real-time timer expiration in the set this wait takes
3053        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089).
3054        let pending = pending_real_time_among(guest, consumed).await;
3055        act_on_pending_real_time(guest, pending, consumed, 0).await;
3056        // The call's memory as it began, for this attempt and for the reads
3057        // of it below, and what another thread wrote over it meanwhile, which
3058        // goes back once the attempt is made.
3059        let displaced = entry_import
3060            .as_ref()
3061            .map(|entry| entry.reinstate(&mut guest.memory()));
3062        // A receive whose descriptors Detcore names reads its geometry again
3063        // right before each attempt: a sibling may have changed it while an
3064        // earlier attempt waited (`ThreadState::receive_geometry`).
3065        if guest.thread_state().receive_geometry.is_some() {
3066            let geometry =
3067                crate::syscalls::scm_rights::ReceiveGeometry::before(&guest.memory(), &call.into());
3068            guest.thread_state_mut().receive_geometry = Some(geometry);
3069        }
3070        // A send whose `SCM_RIGHTS` descriptors Detcore inspected reads them
3071        // again right before each attempt: a sibling may have rewritten its
3072        // messages, or replaced what their descriptor numbers name, since the
3073        // inspection or while an earlier attempt waited
3074        // (`ThreadState::send_inspection`). An attempt that would pass other
3075        // placeholders than those whose copies Detcore counted is refused by
3076        // name. Boxed: only a send that may pass a placeholder carries it.
3077        if let Some(inspection) = guest.thread_state().send_inspection.clone()
3078            && let Some(reason) =
3079                Box::pin(Detcore::<T>::changed_placeholder_send(guest, &inspection)).await
3080        {
3081            tracing::error!("Detcore refuses {}: {reason}", inspection.sysno);
3082            if let Err(error) = put_back_entry_import(guest, &entry_import, displaced, false) {
3083                break Err(error);
3084            }
3085            let panic_on_unsupported_syscalls = guest.config().panic_on_unsupported_syscalls;
3086            break refuse_unserviceable_operation_with(
3087                guest,
3088                panic_on_unsupported_syscalls,
3089                inspection.sysno,
3090                Errno::EOPNOTSUPP,
3091                Some(&reason),
3092            )
3093            .await;
3094        }
3095        // Read actual metadata after reinstatement and all earlier awaits.
3096        // Observation adds no reads or allocation when buffer logging is off.
3097        let attempt_observation =
3098            if guest.config().detlog_io_buffers && crate::io_buffers::observed() {
3099                EntryImport::capture_observation(&guest.memory(), &call.into())
3100            } else {
3101                None
3102            };
3103        // Route through the record/replay subtool for internal pipes so each poll (an
3104        // EAGAIN, or the final data-bearing read) becomes one recorded event that replay
3105        // reproduces deterministically; otherwise execute the syscall directly.
3106        let res = match subtool {
3107            Some(detcore) => {
3108                detcore
3109                    .record_or_replay_preserving_tool_errors(guest, call)
3110                    .await
3111            }
3112            None => guest.inject_with_retry(call).await.map_err(Error::from),
3113        };
3114        if let Err(error) = put_back_entry_import(guest, &entry_import, displaced, res.is_ok()) {
3115            break Err(error);
3116        }
3117        // Under record and replay the attempt is a plain injection, which the
3118        // signal that woke this call, still pending, stops before it runs
3119        // (ERESTARTSYS, not run): the call then returns that restart errno,
3120        // as on main, though a byte, end of file or room may have been ready.
3121        // Making the attempt again would replace the held signal with any
3122        // other pending one (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1012),
3123        // and record and replay could not agree on when it is safe.
3124        let syscall_result = match res {
3125            Ok(value) => Ok(value),
3126            Err(Error::Errno(error)) => Err(error),
3127            Err(error) => break Err(error),
3128        };
3129        // Before the signal check: Linux looks for a pending signal only when
3130        // the call must wait, and a receive on a socket shut down for reading
3131        // does not. Record and replay poll a receive here only on a
3132        // socketpair, through `subtool`; finishing it there would add
3133        // recorded calls, a new recording format, so they keep polling.
3134        if subtool.is_none()
3135            && call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result)
3136            && let Some(result) = finish_after_read_shutdown(guest, call).await
3137        {
3138            break result;
3139        }
3140        if signaled && call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result) {
3141            let errno = call.signal_interrupt_errno();
3142            tracing::trace!(
3143                "retry_nonblocking_syscall: interrupted by signal while {} would block: {:?}",
3144                call.display(&guest.memory()),
3145                errno
3146            );
3147            break Err(errno.into());
3148        }
3149        // Under the gate the wait ends here, where it would block (as
3150        // Linux checks for a pending signal only then), for a signal sent
3151        // before it parked or one whose commit woke it.
3152        if gated && call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result) {
3153            match gated_wait_ends(guest, None) {
3154                Ok(true) => break Err(call.signal_interrupt_errno().into()),
3155                Ok(false) => {}
3156                Err(error) => break Err(error),
3157            }
3158        }
3159        if call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result) {
3160            rsrc.poll_attempt += 1;
3161            if let Some((timeout, timeout_result)) = maybe_timeout {
3162                let new_time = thread_observe_time(guest).await;
3163                if new_time >= timeout {
3164                    tracing::trace!(
3165                        "Timing out syscall after #{} retries: {}",
3166                        rsrc.poll_attempt - 1,
3167                        call.display(&guest.memory())
3168                    );
3169                    break timeout_result.map_err(|e| e.into());
3170                } else {
3171                    tracing::trace!(
3172                        "Retry #{} for syscall due to result {:?}, {} from timeout: {}",
3173                        rsrc.poll_attempt,
3174                        syscall_result,
3175                        timeout - new_time,
3176                        call.display(&guest.memory())
3177                    );
3178                    record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
3179                }
3180            } else {
3181                tracing::trace!(
3182                    "Retry #{} for syscall due to result {:?}: {}",
3183                    rsrc.poll_attempt,
3184                    syscall_result,
3185                    call.display(&guest.memory())
3186                );
3187                record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
3188            }
3189        } else {
3190            let res = call
3191                .normalize_nonblocking_result(syscall_result, rsrc.poll_attempt > 0)
3192                .map_err(|e| e.into());
3193            if res.is_ok() {
3194                completed_observation = attempt_observation;
3195            }
3196            tracing::trace!(
3197                "retry_nonblocking_syscall: syscall completed after {} retries: {} = {:?}",
3198                rsrc.poll_attempt,
3199                call.display(&guest.memory()),
3200                res
3201            );
3202            break res;
3203        }
3204    };
3205    let entry_import =
3206        EntryImport::with_observation(entry_import, call0.into(), completed_observation);
3207    keep_entry_view(guest, entry_import);
3208
3209    // The single exit: the guest's mask goes back before the result is
3210    // returned. A mask `block_in_place` installed goes back through
3211    // `Guest::set_blocked_signals`, with no scratch memory, and only a
3212    // refusal falls back to an injected restoration (`KernelSignalWait::restore`).
3213    // A mask that cannot be put back ends the run before the guest resumes.
3214    match turn_wait {
3215        Some(mut wait) if wait.effective_mask().is_some() => {
3216            let restored = wait.restore(guest, None).await;
3217            publish_wait_mask(guest, None, &mut published).await;
3218            match result_after_restore(restored, result) {
3219                Ok(result) => refuse_held_signal_loss(guest, call0.number(), result).await,
3220                Err(error) => Err(error),
3221            }
3222        }
3223        _ => result,
3224    }
3225}
3226
3227/// Ends a polled blocking receive as Linux does once its socket's read side is
3228/// shut down.
3229///
3230/// Detcore polls a blocking receive on a physically nonblocking socket with
3231/// nonblocking attempts (`retry_nonblocking_syscall`). On a datagram socket
3232/// whose read side is shut down, Linux's blocking receive does not wait: with
3233/// nothing queued it returns 0 at once (`__skb_wait_for_more_packets`). The
3234/// nonblocking attempt fails with `EAGAIN` instead, every time, so the polled
3235/// receive never ended, and a thread that shut a reader's socket down and then
3236/// joined the reader waited forever.
3237///
3238/// After an attempt that would block on a socket whose read side a guest shut
3239/// down (`DetFd::read_shutdown_requested`), this asks the kernel whether it is
3240/// still shut (`read_side_shut_down`): a TCP disconnect opens it again. If it
3241/// is, the blocking call cannot wait, so this runs the guest's call once with
3242/// `O_NONBLOCK` cleared, then sets the flag back, and returns what Linux
3243/// returned, with the address lengths it wrote. `None` for any other call or
3244/// socket, or while the read side is open: the attempt's `EAGAIN` stands and
3245/// the poll goes on, with no extra call.
3246async fn finish_after_read_shutdown<T, G, C>(guest: &mut G, call: C) -> Option<Result<i64, Error>>
3247where
3248    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
3249    T: RecordOrReplay,
3250    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3251{
3252    let fd = get_fd(call.into()).filter(|_| call.ends_at_read_shutdown())?;
3253    let shut_down_by_guest = guest.thread_state().with_detfd(fd, |detfd| {
3254        matches!(detfd.ty(), FdType::Socket) && detfd.read_shutdown_requested()
3255    });
3256    if shut_down_by_guest != Ok(true) || !read_side_shut_down(guest, fd).await {
3257        return None;
3258    }
3259    let fcntl = |cmd| syscalls::Fcntl::new().with_fd(fd).with_cmd(cmd);
3260    // Nothing has changed if either of these fails: the attempt's EAGAIN stands.
3261    let flags = match guest.inject_with_retry(fcntl(FcntlCmd::F_GETFL)).await {
3262        Ok(flags) => flags as libc::c_int,
3263        Err(errno) => {
3264            tracing::warn!("socket {fd}: F_GETFL before a read-shutdown receive failed: {errno}");
3265            return None;
3266        }
3267    };
3268    let blocking = fcntl(FcntlCmd::F_SETFL(flags & !libc::O_NONBLOCK));
3269    if let Err(errno) = guest.inject_with_retry(blocking).await {
3270        tracing::warn!(
3271            "socket {fd}: clearing O_NONBLOCK for a read-shutdown receive failed: {errno}"
3272        );
3273        return None;
3274    }
3275    let result = guest.inject_with_retry(call).await.map_err(Error::from);
3276    // Every later attempt on this description assumes it is nonblocking; one
3277    // that blocked would hold the turn forever.
3278    if let Err(errno) = guest
3279        .inject_with_retry(fcntl(FcntlCmd::F_SETFL(flags)))
3280        .await
3281    {
3282        panic!("socket {fd}: restoring O_NONBLOCK after a read-shutdown receive failed: {errno}");
3283    }
3284    tracing::trace!(
3285        "retry_nonblocking_syscall: {} ran blocking after a read shutdown: {:?}",
3286        call.display(&guest.memory()),
3287        result
3288    );
3289    Some(result)
3290}
3291
3292/// Whether the kernel reports `fd`'s read side shut down: `POLLRDHUP` from a
3293/// `poll` with a zero timeout, which Linux sets exactly when the socket's
3294/// `RCV_SHUTDOWN` is set (`datagram_poll`, `unix_dgram_poll`, `tcp_poll`).
3295async fn read_side_shut_down<T, G>(guest: &mut G, fd: i32) -> bool
3296where
3297    T: RecordOrReplay,
3298    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3299{
3300    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
3301    let pollfd: AddrMut<libc::pollfd> = stack.reserve();
3302    let Ok(_guard) = stack.commit() else {
3303        return false;
3304    };
3305    let probe = syscalls::Poll::new()
3306        .with_fds(Some(pollfd.cast()))
3307        .with_nfds(1)
3308        .with_timeout(0);
3309    let request = libc::pollfd {
3310        fd,
3311        events: libc::POLLRDHUP,
3312        revents: 0,
3313    };
3314    guest.memory().write_value(pollfd, &request).is_ok()
3315        && guest.inject_with_retry(probe).await == Ok(1)
3316        && guest
3317            .memory()
3318            .read_value(pollfd)
3319            .is_ok_and(|polled| polled.revents & libc::POLLRDHUP != 0)
3320}
3321
3322/// Put back what another thread wrote over a call's memory as it began
3323/// (`EntryImport::put_back`), after an attempt that `completed` or not. The
3324/// bytes were written once already, and no guest thread has run since, so a
3325/// failure is Detcore's own and ends the call rather than leave the guest's
3326/// memory as the call began.
3327fn put_back_entry_import<T, G>(
3328    guest: &mut G,
3329    entry_import: &Option<Box<EntryImport>>,
3330    displaced: Option<Displaced>,
3331    completed: bool,
3332) -> Result<(), Error>
3333where
3334    T: RecordOrReplay,
3335    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3336{
3337    let (Some(entry), Some(displaced)) = (entry_import, displaced) else {
3338        return Ok(());
3339    };
3340    if displaced.is_empty() {
3341        return Ok(());
3342    }
3343    entry
3344        .put_back(&mut guest.memory(), displaced, completed)
3345        .map_err(|errno| {
3346            tracing::error!(
3347                "Detcore could not put back the guest's rewrite of a vectored call's memory: {errno}"
3348            );
3349            Error::from(errno)
3350        })
3351}
3352
3353/// Keep a call's memory as it began (`EntryImport`) for the observers that
3354/// read the call's arguments after it returns (`ThreadState::entry_import`),
3355/// when another thread has rewritten it since; otherwise those arguments are
3356/// still the ones the call moved its bytes through.
3357fn keep_entry_view<T, G>(guest: &mut G, entry_import: Option<Box<EntryImport>>)
3358where
3359    T: RecordOrReplay,
3360    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3361{
3362    let view =
3363        entry_import.filter(|entry| entry.has_observation() || entry.differs(&guest.memory()));
3364    guest.thread_state_mut().entry_import = view;
3365}
3366
3367/// Retry a blocking wait on a backend that decides signal interruption from the
3368/// kernel's signal state (`supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`).
3369///
3370/// A wait ends early only for a signal that would end it natively: one the guest
3371/// does not block and that is caught, or whose default action terminates or stops
3372/// the process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Blocked,
3373/// ignored, and default-ignored signals do not end it, and neither does a default
3374/// job-control stop when Linux's restart of the call keeps its deadline
3375/// (`NonblockableSyscall::restart_keeps_deadline`). Such a signal that stops one
3376/// of the wait's injections is absorbed, and the wait runs on. A stop that
3377/// `KernelSignalWait::inject_absorbing` cannot absorb ends the wait with a
3378/// transparent restart when the backend holds nothing whose loss matters, and
3379/// otherwise with a [`HeldSignalRefusal`], which `refuse_held_signal_loss`
3380/// turns into the unsupported-operation refusal once the guest's mask is back.
3381///
3382/// The first probe runs under the guest's own mask, and before the first check
3383/// for a pending signal (`KernelSignalWait::inject_first_probe`): Linux reports a
3384/// descriptor that is ready when the call begins, a queued event, and an
3385/// argument error before it looks at pending signals, so the probe's result
3386/// stands whenever the signal arrived. If it would block, every blockable signal
3387/// is blocked for the rest of the wait, so later probes cannot be stopped by one
3388/// and every signal that arrives stays pending in the kernel, where `/proc`
3389/// reports it. Each turn classifies the pending set against the guest's mask and
3390/// dispositions, and an interrupting signal ends the wait with the call's restart
3391/// errno (see `KernelSignalWait::interrupted_with_state`). The guest's mask is
3392/// restored before returning, so the signal is delivered as the call returns.
3393/// The signals a scheduler resume names (`ResumeStatus::Signaled`): signals the
3394/// scheduler committed to the thread at that point.
3395fn committed_signals(resumed: &ResumeStatus) -> KernelSigset {
3396    match resumed {
3397        ResumeStatus::Signaled(Some(signals)) => signals.iter().fold(0, |set, signal| {
3398            set | kernel_sigset_bit(signal.0 as libc::c_int)
3399        }),
3400        _ => 0,
3401    }
3402}
3403
3404/// What a restartable internal IO poll or a parked pipe write finds at a turn,
3405/// read from the thread's own state before the turn's first injection, while it
3406/// is still stopped at its request: every signal sent since is still in the
3407/// kernel's pending set, and none is yet in the backend's held slot. A copy
3408/// the turn's own injections later absorb is counted here
3409/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273>, R2b-1 rules 2-4).
3410#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
3411struct TurnSignals {
3412    /// The signals the turn's answer names (`committed_signals`) that the
3413    /// call's mask leaves unblocked: a kept send's wake, which Linux's
3414    /// `TIF_SIGPENDING` keeps in force until the call returns, whatever a later
3415    /// flush does. For `writev`, which the drain never filters, a real-time
3416    /// signal, outside the record of copies discarded at send, counts only if
3417    /// its disposition delivers it now (`NamedRealTime::ByDisposition`); for
3418    /// the generic poll and the scalar writer the drain's own disposition test
3419    /// has already decided it, at the wake (R2b-1 rules 1 and 2).
3420    named: KernelSigset,
3421    /// The kept copies pending now that would end the call: unblocked under the
3422    /// call's mask, caught or acting by default, not held (`SIGCHLD` and the
3423    /// host-timed signals, except one the scheduler committed:
3424    /// `futex_wait_held_after_wake`), and not discarded at send
3425    /// (`threads::without_discarded`).
3426    pending: KernelSigset,
3427}
3428
3429impl TurnSignals {
3430    /// Whether a call that would wait now ends. After progress (`progress`),
3431    /// Linux returns the bytes transferred on any wake, so a named wake or a
3432    /// pending copy ends the call. With none, Linux returns `-ERESTARTSYS`,
3433    /// which delivers a pending copy or restarts invisibly, so only a pending
3434    /// copy ends it; otherwise the call keeps polling, which the guest cannot
3435    /// tell from that restart (R2b-1 rule 3).
3436    fn ends(&self, progress: bool) -> bool {
3437        self.pending != 0 || (progress && self.named != 0)
3438    }
3439}
3440
3441/// [`TurnSignals`] for a call whose mask is `mask` (the kernel's, by default:
3442/// the generic poll and the scalar writer install none) and to which the
3443/// scheduler committed `committed` at this wake (`committed_signals`; none
3444/// before a turnless first attempt). A thread that is gone ends the call with
3445/// `ERESTARTNOINTR`, which nothing observes, and a live one whose state cannot
3446/// be read ends the run (`read_wait_signal_state`).
3447async fn read_turn_signals<T, G>(
3448    guest: &mut G,
3449    mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
3450    committed: KernelSigset,
3451    real_time: NamedRealTime,
3452) -> Result<TurnSignals, Error>
3453where
3454    T: RecordOrReplay,
3455    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3456{
3457    Ok(
3458        read_turn_signals_and_state(guest, mask, committed, real_time)
3459            .await?
3460            .0,
3461    )
3462}
3463
3464/// `read_turn_signals`, also returning the thread's signal state that the
3465/// turn read.
3466async fn read_turn_signals_and_state<T, G>(
3467    guest: &mut G,
3468    mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
3469    committed: KernelSigset,
3470    real_time: NamedRealTime,
3471) -> Result<(TurnSignals, KernelSignalState), Error>
3472where
3473    T: RecordOrReplay,
3474    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3475{
3476    let state = read_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())?;
3477    let mask = mask.unwrap_or(state.blocked);
3478    let host_timed = host_timed_signals(guest).await;
3479    Ok((
3480        turn_signals_from_state(guest, &state, mask, host_timed, committed, real_time, 0).await,
3481        state,
3482    ))
3483}
3484
3485/// [`TurnSignals`] from the thread's state `state` read in this turn, with the
3486/// record of copies Linux discarded at send applied
3487/// (`threads::without_discarded`); `private` as for
3488/// `turn_signals_before_discard`.
3489async fn turn_signals_from_state<T, G>(
3490    guest: &mut G,
3491    state: &KernelSignalState,
3492    mask: KernelSigset,
3493    host_timed: KernelSigset,
3494    committed: KernelSigset,
3495    real_time: NamedRealTime,
3496    private: KernelSigset,
3497) -> TurnSignals
3498where
3499    T: RecordOrReplay,
3500    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3501{
3502    let before =
3503        turn_signals_before_discard(state, mask, host_timed, committed, real_time, private);
3504    let pending =
3505        crate::syscalls::threads::without_discarded(guest, state, before.pending, committed).await;
3506    TurnSignals { pending, ..before }
3507}
3508
3509/// A restartable poll's turn on a pipe or a socket that decides at its turn:
3510/// read the thread's signal state before the turn's first injection, block
3511/// every blockable signal in place if one pending could stop that injection
3512/// and `may_block` (`KernelSignalWait::block_in_place`, stage 2 of
3513/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273), then decide the turn's
3514/// signals under the guest's own mask, which the call owns once it blocks.
3515///
3516/// A `SIGCHLD` a guest sent the thread, which the schedule recorded in its
3517/// private queue, ends the call where `private_decides`
3518/// (`Resources::private_sigchld_decides`), as on Linux (stage 3): it is
3519/// admitted only while the block holds (`saved_mask`), so no injection of
3520/// this turn can take it into the backend's single held slot, and only if
3521/// the read found it in the thread's own queue, from which only this stopped
3522/// thread can take it. Nothing runs between the read and the block. The
3523/// host-timed signals and the record come in one round trip, before any
3524/// injection (`host_timed_and_private_sigchld`).
3525async fn turn_signals_with_block<T, G>(
3526    guest: &mut G,
3527    wait: &mut Option<KernelSignalWait>,
3528    may_block: bool,
3529    committed: KernelSigset,
3530    private_decides: bool,
3531    published: &mut PublishedWaitMask,
3532) -> Result<TurnSignals, Error>
3533where
3534    T: RecordOrReplay,
3535    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3536{
3537    let mask = wait.as_ref().and_then(KernelSignalWait::effective_mask);
3538    let state = read_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())?;
3539    let (host_timed, recorded) = crate::tool_global::host_timed_and_private_sigchld(guest).await;
3540    let mut private = 0;
3541    if let Some(wait) = wait.as_mut() {
3542        // Block before the publication and the probe, so neither can be
3543        // stopped by a blockable signal, and every pending one stays in the
3544        // kernel's queue until the guest resumes.
3545        if may_block
3546            && wait.needs_block()
3547            && pending_could_stop_injection(&state)
3548            && wait.block_in_place(guest, host_timed).await?
3549        {
3550            publish_wait_mask(guest, wait.effective_mask(), published).await;
3551        }
3552        if private_decides
3553            && wait.saved_mask.is_some()
3554            && state.thread_pending & kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) != 0
3555        {
3556            private = recorded;
3557        }
3558    }
3559    let mask = mask.unwrap_or(state.blocked);
3560    Ok(turn_signals_from_state(
3561        guest,
3562        &state,
3563        mask,
3564        host_timed,
3565        committed,
3566        NamedRealTime::Woken,
3567        private,
3568    )
3569    .await)
3570}
3571
3572/// Whether a private injection could be stopped by a signal pending in
3573/// `state`: one pending, on the thread's or the process's queue, that the
3574/// thread's current mask leaves unblocked and that a mask can block. Such a
3575/// stop moves the signal into the backend's single held slot, where a second
3576/// stop replaces it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, stage 2).
3577fn pending_could_stop_injection(state: &KernelSignalState) -> bool {
3578    state.pending & !state.blocked & blocked_signal_mask() != 0
3579}
3580
3581/// [`TurnSignals`] from the thread's state (`state`), the call's mask (`mask`),
3582/// the host-timed signals (`host_timed`) and the scheduler's commitment
3583/// (`committed`), before the record of copies Linux discarded at send is
3584/// applied to `pending` (`threads::without_discarded`). The hold leaves out
3585/// `SIGCHLD` and every host-timed signal, except a signal the scheduler
3586/// committed that no host-timed source can post (`futex_wait_held_after_wake`),
3587/// and a recorded private `SIGCHLD` the turn admits (`private`).
3588fn turn_signals_before_discard(
3589    state: &KernelSignalState,
3590    mask: KernelSigset,
3591    host_timed: KernelSigset,
3592    committed: KernelSigset,
3593    real_time: NamedRealTime,
3594    private: KernelSigset,
3595) -> TurnSignals {
3596    use crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::STANDARD_SIGNALS;
3597    // A `SIGCHLD` a guest sent this thread, which the schedule recorded in its
3598    // private queue, is not held where the turn admits it (`private`,
3599    // `turn_signals_with_block`).
3600    let held =
3601        crate::syscalls::threads::futex_wait_held_after_wake(host_timed, committed) & !private;
3602    let pending = state.pending_interrupting(mask, false) & !held;
3603    let counted = match real_time {
3604        NamedRealTime::Woken => !0,
3605        NamedRealTime::ByDisposition => {
3606            STANDARD_SIGNALS | (state.interrupting(mask) & !STANDARD_SIGNALS)
3607        }
3608    };
3609    let named = committed & !mask & counted;
3610    TurnSignals { named, pending }
3611}
3612
3613/// How a turn counts a real-time signal its answer names
3614/// ([`TurnSignals::named`]).
3615#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
3616enum NamedRealTime {
3617    /// As any named signal: the drain woke the call only for one whose
3618    /// disposition delivered it then, and Linux's wake stands after a later
3619    /// flush (the generic poll and the scalar writer).
3620    Woken,
3621    /// Only if its disposition delivers it now: the drain never filters
3622    /// `writev` (R2b-1 rule 2).
3623    ByDisposition,
3624}
3625
3626/// Whether a poll or a parked pipe write decides interruption at its own turn
3627/// (`signals_interrupting_poll`): where the record of copies Linux discarded
3628/// at send is kept (`discarded_at_send::records`, ptrace with sequentialized
3629/// threads) and the thread's state can be read (`task`, its
3630/// `Resources::signal_state_task`, which needs guest thread IDs that name host
3631/// tasks). Elsewhere the earlier decision stands: on KVM the backend restarts
3632/// the call unless it would deliver a signal, and its polled-read observation
3633/// (`Guest::polled_read_signal_site`) takes a caught signal before the turn,
3634/// where a `/proc` read could not see it (the Claude re-check of the R2b-1
3635/// design, R4-4).
3636fn decides_interruption_at_turn<T, G>(guest: &G, task: Option<(i32, i32)>) -> bool
3637where
3638    T: RecordOrReplay,
3639    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3640{
3641    task.is_some() && crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::records(guest.config())
3642}
3643
3644/// Install the private mask of a pipe `writev` that decides at its turn
3645/// (`decides_interruption_at_turn`) and goes on polling after its first
3646/// attempt, through `wait` (`KernelSignalWait::block`, scratch `cell`), and
3647/// publish the guest's own mask to the scheduler while it is installed
3648/// (`set_saved_guest_sigmask`). Returns the guest's own mask. A signal that
3649/// stops the installation is held as `inject_absorbing` holds one, a
3650/// host-timed one and a copy Linux discarded at send included
3651/// (`hold_until_return`), and one that would replace a
3652/// held signal whose loss matters ends the call: with the restart errno, as
3653/// `Error::Errno`, when the held one would end it natively, and otherwise with
3654/// a [`HeldSignalRefusal`], which the caller turns into the refusal once the
3655/// guest's mask is back (`refuse_held_signal_loss`; R2b-1 rule 5). A mask that
3656/// cannot be installed ends the call with `EFAULT`, as a failed
3657/// scratch-stack commit does.
3658async fn install_turn_mask<T, G>(
3659    guest: &mut G,
3660    wait: &mut KernelSignalWait,
3661    cell: AddrMut<'_, KernelSigset>,
3662) -> Result<KernelSigset, Error>
3663where
3664    T: RecordOrReplay,
3665    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3666{
3667    // A copy Linux discarded at send that the kernel still holds (a traced
3668    // task's copy is queued whatever its disposition) is left out of the
3669    // turn's `pending` (`without_discarded`), so it must not end the call
3670    // here either: it is held until the call returns, where it is delivered
3671    // late (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3995), as the turn
3672    // decided (the Claude re-check of R2b-1, N1).
3673    let state = read_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())?;
3674    let kept = crate::syscalls::threads::without_discarded(guest, &state, state.pending, 0).await;
3675    wait.hold_until_return(host_timed_signals(guest).await | (state.pending & !kept));
3676    wait.block(guest, Some(cell)).await?;
3677    let Some(mask) = wait.effective_mask() else {
3678        return Err(Errno::EFAULT.into());
3679    };
3680    crate::tool_global::set_saved_guest_sigmask(guest, Some(mask)).await;
3681    Ok(mask)
3682}
3683
3684/// A5 step 3c.1c (design 16.11, D50): under the in-guest delivery gate, the
3685/// guest mask a wait under the thread's own mask decides by, in the thread's
3686/// own turn: the mask it publishes at its requests
3687/// (`tool_global::publish_request_guest_mask`), or, when it publishes none,
3688/// `fallback`, which is the kernel's `SigBlk` unless the caller knows the
3689/// guest's mask better. No backend records the guest's mask apart from the
3690/// kernel's before step 3c.1e, and step 3c.1b's readers take `SigBlk` then
3691/// too.
3692pub(crate) fn gated_own_mask<T, G>(guest: &G, fallback: KernelSigset) -> KernelSigset
3693where
3694    T: RecordOrReplay,
3695    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3696{
3697    let own = Resources::new(guest.thread_state().dettid);
3698    crate::tool_global::publish_request_guest_mask(guest, &own).unwrap_or(fallback)
3699}
3700
3701/// A5 step 3c.1c (design 16.11, D50): under the in-guest delivery gate, what
3702/// ends this thread's wait now, read in its own turn from its `/proc` status
3703/// and its own published mask ([`gated_own_mask`], with `fallback` for
3704/// `SigBlk` when the caller knows the guest's own mask better). `None` when no
3705/// signal is deliverable, and always with the gate off. A state that cannot be
3706/// read is handled as a wait's first read is (`read_thread_wait_signal_state`):
3707/// a thread that no longer exists ends the call with `ERESTARTNOINTR`, and
3708/// otherwise the run ends with a diagnostic.
3709pub(crate) fn gated_wait_end<T, G>(
3710    guest: &G,
3711    fallback: Option<KernelSigset>,
3712) -> Result<Option<crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd>, Error>
3713where
3714    T: RecordOrReplay,
3715    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3716{
3717    gated_wait_end_with_virtual(guest, fallback, 0)
3718}
3719
3720/// [`gated_wait_end`] with `virtual_caught`, caught signals the scheduler
3721/// knows are pending on the process's shared queue with no physical copy
3722/// (signal phase 1's virtual SIGALRM;
3723/// `wait_signal_end::wait_end_with_virtual`).
3724pub(crate) fn gated_wait_end_with_virtual<T, G>(
3725    guest: &G,
3726    fallback: Option<KernelSigset>,
3727    virtual_caught: KernelSigset,
3728) -> Result<Option<crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd>, Error>
3729where
3730    T: RecordOrReplay,
3731    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3732{
3733    if !guest.config().in_guest_signal_delivery {
3734        return Ok(None);
3735    }
3736    let state = crate::syscalls::threads::read_thread_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())?;
3737    let mask = gated_own_mask(guest, fallback.unwrap_or(state.blocked));
3738    Ok(crate::wait_signal_end::wait_end_with_virtual(
3739        &state,
3740        mask,
3741        guest.config().in_guest_reserved_signals,
3742        virtual_caught,
3743    ))
3744}
3745
3746/// [`gated_wait_end`], recording a found end as the current call's D40 flag
3747/// (`ThreadState::wait_signal_end`) for the restart checkpoint. Returns
3748/// whether a signal ends the wait.
3749pub(crate) fn gated_wait_ends<T, G>(
3750    guest: &mut G,
3751    fallback: Option<KernelSigset>,
3752) -> Result<bool, Error>
3753where
3754    T: RecordOrReplay,
3755    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3756{
3757    let end = gated_wait_end(guest, fallback)?;
3758    if let Some(end) = end {
3759        tracing::info!(
3760            "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, {:?} ends the wait",
3761            guest.thread_state().dettid,
3762            end
3763        );
3764        guest.thread_state_mut().wait_signal_end = Some(end);
3765    }
3766    Ok(end.is_some())
3767}
3768
3769/// A5 step 3c.1c, design D41 (amending 16.26), with IR-5 and IR-14: under the
3770/// in-guest delivery gate, a default-fatal signal already deliverable when a
3771/// kernel-run call begins (`ResourceID::is_kernel_run_blocking`: a background
3772/// external call, `rt_sigsuspend`, `vfork`) is one Linux would have delivered
3773/// before the call, ending the process. So the call is not run: its handler
3774/// calls this as its first statement, before any guest-visible effect, and
3775/// returns the error this gives, `ERESTARTNOINTR` with the D40 flag `Fatal`
3776/// recorded, which the restart checkpoint turns into `-EINTR` (the death path
3777/// of step 3c.1e follows at the return). A `BehindCaught` end (a caught
3778/// signal first, and a later delivery in the same loop that could end the
3779/// process) means the call is not run either: the flag is recorded as it is,
3780/// and the checkpoint resolves it. `Fatal` gives `-EINTR`. `Caught` (the
3781/// handlers' masks hold the default-fatal signal, or no reset instance is
