3782/// reached) would need the handler run and then the call restarted, which
3783/// 3c.1 cannot do, so the checkpoint refuses it by name
3784/// (HERMIT_RESTART_AFTER_HANDLER, fail closed); in that schedule Linux runs
3785/// the handler and, unless it changes the default-fatal signal's disposition
3786/// or mask, ends the process at its `rt_sigreturn`, before the call is made
3787/// again. Only a single caught signal at entry, or none, keeps today's path
3788/// (`None`): the call runs. With the gate off, `None`.
3789pub(crate) fn kernel_run_entry_refusal<T, G>(guest: &mut G) -> Result<Option<Error>, Error>
3790where
3791    T: RecordOrReplay,
3792    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3793{
3794    match gated_wait_end(guest, None)? {
3795        Some(
3796            end @ (crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd::Fatal(_)
3797            | crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd::BehindCaught(_)),
3798        ) => {
3799            tracing::info!(
3800                "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, {:?} is deliverable at a kernel-run \
3801                 call's entry: the call is not run",
3802                guest.thread_state().dettid,
3803                end
3804            );
3805            guest.thread_state_mut().wait_signal_end = Some(end);
3806            Ok(Some(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR.into()))
3807        }
3808        _ => Ok(None),
3809    }
3810}
3811
3812/// The most instances [`remove_ignored_signals`] dequeues in one call before
3813/// it gives up: far more than a thread's queues can hold, which
3814/// `RLIMIT_SIGPENDING` bounds for real-time signals and one per queue bounds
3815/// for standard ones; reached, the removal fails closed.
3816const MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS: usize = 1 << 16;
3817
3818/// A5 step 3c.1d, design D37: remove the pending instances of `set` (ignored
3819/// signals Linux would not hold, `ignored_signals::removable`) from the
3820/// calling thread's queues, in its own turn, by repeated trusted zero-timeout
3821/// `rt_sigtimedwait` calls until `EAGAIN`. Each call dequeues one instance,
3822/// the thread's private queue first and then the shared one
3823/// (`dequeue_signal`, kernel/signal.c:626-639 at v6.12), and with a zero
3824/// timeout it never sleeps: no instance left gives `-EAGAIN`
3825/// (`do_sigtimedwait`, :3629-3676). SIGKILL and SIGSTOP are never in `set`
3826/// (they are never ignored), and the kernel drops them from it anyway
3827/// (:3648). Nothing is injected for an empty set. An error other than
3828/// `EAGAIN`, more instances than any queue can hold, or no scratch stack for
3829/// the call's two cells is Hermit's own failure (`Error::Tool`), never an
3830/// errno the guest's call could see.
3831pub(crate) async fn remove_ignored_signals<T, G>(guest: &mut G, set: u64) -> Result<(), Error>
3832where
3833    T: RecordOrReplay,
3834    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3835{
3836    if set == 0 {
3837        return Ok(());
3838    }
3839    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
3840    let set_cell = stack.push(set);
3841    let timeout = stack.push(Timespec {
3842        tv_sec: 0,
3843        tv_nsec: 0,
3844    });
3845    // A stack with no room for the two cells is Hermit's own failure too, never
3846    // an EFAULT of the guest's call (round-3 ruling 4).
3847    let _stack_guard = stack.commit().map_err(|errno| {
3848        Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
3849            "removing ignored signals {set:#x}: no scratch stack for the trusted \
3850             rt_sigtimedwait ({errno})"
3851        ))
3852    })?;
3853    // SAFETY: the kernel only reads the set; Reverie types the argument as
3854    // mutable.
3855    let set_cell = unsafe { set_cell.cast::<libc::sigset_t>().into_mut() };
3856    for _ in 0..MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS {
3857        let taken = guest
3858            .inject(
3859                syscalls::RtSigtimedwait::new()
3860                    .with_set(Some(set_cell))
3861                    .with_info(None)
3862                    .with_timeout(Some(timeout))
3863                    .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE),
3864            )
3865            .await;
3866        match taken {
3867            Ok(signal) => tracing::info!(
3868                "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, removed ignored signal {} that Linux \
3869                 would not hold (D37)",
3870                guest.thread_state().dettid,
3871                signal
3872            ),
3873            Err(Errno::EAGAIN) => return Ok(()),
3874            // Hermit's own failure, never the guest's result: the guest's call
3875            // (rt_sigaction, rt_sigsuspend, a masked wait) cannot return it.
3876            Err(errno) => {
3877                return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
3878                    "removing ignored signals {set:#x}: the trusted rt_sigtimedwait failed with \
3879                     {errno}"
3880                )));
3881            }
3882        }
3883    }
3884    Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
3885        "removing ignored signals {set:#x} dequeued {MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS} instances without \
3886         emptying the queues"
3887    )))
3888}
3889
3890/// Which of a thread's two queues [`remove_ignored_from_queue`] empties of a
3891/// signal.
3892#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
3893pub(crate) enum OneQueue {
3894    /// The thread's private queue (`SigPnd`).
3895    Private,
3896    /// Its thread group's shared queue (`ShdPnd`).
3897    Shared,
3898}
3899
3900/// A5 step 3c.1e A, D37's R2 per queue: remove every pending instance of the
3901/// ignored signal `signal` from `queue` only, leaving the other queue's
3902/// instances as they are, in the thread's own turn. `rt_sigtimedwait`
3903/// dequeues the private queue first (`dequeue_signal`, kernel/signal.c:
3904/// 626-639 at v6.12), so:
3905///
3906/// - `Private`: one trusted zero-timeout `rt_sigtimedwait` per instance, for
3907///   as long as the thread's `/proc` status shows `signal` in `SigPnd`.
3908/// - `Shared`: the private instances are dequeued first, each with its
3909///   siginfo, then the shared ones until `EAGAIN`, then the private ones are
3910///   queued again, in their order, with their own siginfo, by
3911///   `rt_tgsigqueueinfo` to the thread itself (`do_rt_tgsigqueueinfo` lets a
3912///   thread queue any siginfo to itself, kernel/signal.c:4112-4114; the
3913///   signal is blocked by the kernel's mask then, the guest's own mask, which
3914///   blocks it since Linux kept it, or the in-guest runtime's, so it is
3915///   queued and not discarded, `sig_ignored`, :104-120).
3916///
3917/// Nothing is injected when `signal` is not pending in `queue`. A failed
3918/// injection, more instances than any queue holds, or no scratch stack is
3919/// Hermit's own failure (`Error::Tool`), never an errno of the guest's call.
3920pub(crate) async fn remove_ignored_from_queue<T, G>(
3921    guest: &mut G,
3922    signal: i32,
3923    queue: OneQueue,
3924) -> Result<(), Error>
3925where
3926    T: RecordOrReplay,
3927    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
3928{
3929    let bit = crate::syscalls::kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
3930    let failed = |what: &str| {
3931        Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
3932            "removing ignored signal {signal} from the {queue:?} queue: {what}"
3933        ))
3934    };
3935    let state = read_thread_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())?;
3936    let in_queue = match queue {
3937        OneQueue::Private => state.thread_pending,
3938        OneQueue::Shared => state.shared_pending,
3939    };
3940    if in_queue & bit == 0 {
3941        return Ok(());
3942    }
3943    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
3944    let set_cell = stack.push(bit);
3945    let timeout = stack.push(Timespec {
3946        tv_sec: 0,
3947        tv_nsec: 0,
3948    });
3949    // A siginfo cell, kept as bytes: `siginfo_t` holds raw pointers, so an
3950    // address typed by it could not live across an await.
3951    let info = stack.reserve::<[u8; 128]>();
3952    let _stack_guard = stack
3953        .commit()
3954        .map_err(|errno| failed(&format!("no scratch stack ({errno})")))?;
3955    // SAFETY: the kernel only reads the set; Reverie types it as mutable.
3956    let set_cell = unsafe { set_cell.cast::<libc::sigset_t>().into_mut() };
3957    let dequeue = move |with_info: bool| {
3958        syscalls::RtSigtimedwait::new()
3959            .with_set(Some(set_cell))
3960            .with_info(with_info.then(|| info.cast()))
3961            .with_timeout(Some(timeout))
3962            .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE)
3963    };
3964    // The private instances, dequeued one at a time while `SigPnd` shows
3965    // them; their siginfo is kept to queue them again for `Shared`.
3966    let mut kept: Vec<[u8; 128]> = Vec::new();
3967    let mut removals = 0;
3968    while read_thread_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())?.thread_pending & bit != 0 {
3969        removals += 1;
3970        if removals > MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS {
3971            return Err(failed("too many instances"));
3972        }
3973        match guest.inject(dequeue(queue == OneQueue::Shared)).await {
3974            Ok(_) => {
3975                if queue == OneQueue::Shared {
3976                    kept.push(guest.memory().read_value(info)?);
3977                }
3978            }
3979            Err(errno) => return Err(failed(&format!("rt_sigtimedwait failed with {errno}"))),
3980        }
3981    }
3982    if queue == OneQueue::Private {
3983        tracing::info!(
3984            "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, removed ignored signal {} from the \
3985             private queue, which Linux discarded at send (D37)",
3986            guest.thread_state().dettid,
3987            signal
3988        );
3989        return Ok(());
3990    }
3991    loop {
3992        removals += 1;
3993        if removals > MAX_IGNORED_REMOVALS {
3994            return Err(failed("too many instances"));
3995        }
3996        match guest.inject(dequeue(false)).await {
3997            Ok(_) => {}
3998            Err(Errno::EAGAIN) => break,
3999            Err(errno) => return Err(failed(&format!("rt_sigtimedwait failed with {errno}"))),
4000        }
4001    }
4002    for siginfo in kept {
4003        guest.memory().write_value(info, &siginfo)?;
4004        let requeue = syscalls::RtTgsigqueueinfo::new()
4005            .with_tgid(guest.pid().as_raw())
4006            .with_tid(guest.tid().as_raw())
4007            .with_sig(signal)
4008            .with_siginfo(Some(info.cast()));
4009        if let Err(errno) = guest.inject(requeue).await {
4010            return Err(failed(&format!(
4011                "queueing a kept private instance again failed with {errno}"
4012            )));
4013        }
4014    }
4015    tracing::info!(
4016        "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, removed ignored signal {} from the shared \
4017         queue, which Linux discarded at send, keeping its private instances (D37)",
4018        guest.thread_state().dettid,
4019        signal
4020    );
4021    Ok(())
4022}
4023
4024/// What a temporary-mask wait's check finds under the in-guest delivery gate
4025/// ([`temporary_mask_check`]).
4026#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
4027pub(crate) enum TemporaryMaskCheck {
4028    /// Nothing ends the wait; the ignored signals Linux would not hold were
4029    /// removed (D37 rule (ii)).
4030    Waits,
4031    /// A default-fatal signal the temporary mask lets in ends it: the D40
4032    /// flag `Fatal` is recorded, and the call returns its restart code
4033    /// (`-ERESTARTNOHAND`; `-EINTR` for the `epoll` forms), which the restart
4034    /// checkpoint turns into `-EINTR` for the death path of step 3c.1e.
4035    Fatal,
4036    /// A masked `epoll_pwait` or `epoll_pwait2` at its park: an ignored signal
4037    /// pending at entry that only the temporary mask lets in, removed, and
4038    /// the call returns `EINTR` (D37's exception, IR-3).
4039    EpollInterrupted,
4040    /// A caught signal would end the wait (or be delivered first): its
4041    /// handler would run under the temporary mask, which step 3c.w owns and
4042    /// which 3c.1 never reaches (phase 1 refuses every temporary-mask call in
4043    /// a process that handles SIGALRM, F8). The stopping refusal
4044    /// HERMIT_TEMPORARY_MASK_CAUGHT_END was filed (D49); were the run to go
4045    /// on, the call returns `EINTR`.
4046    Refused,
4047}
4048
4049/// A5 step 3c.1d (design D37, D39, D50, IR-7): the check of a wait under a
4050/// temporary mask `m_temp` (`rt_sigsuspend`, a masked `pselect6`, `ppoll`,
4051/// `epoll_pwait` or `epoll_pwait2`), at the point where Linux tests for a
4052/// pending signal: the call would wait (nothing ready), in the thread's own
4053/// turn, from its `/proc` status (one read).
4054///
4055/// 1. The design's deliverable set under `m_temp` (`wait_signal_end`): a
4056///    default-fatal signal ends the wait (`Fatal`, the D40 flag recorded). A
4057///    caught one would run its handler under the temporary mask (step 3c.w,
4058///    unreachable in 3c.1): a named stopping refusal (`Refused`).
4059/// 2. D37 rule (ii) with IR-7's per-instance masks: the ignored signals `I`
4060///    pending now, less `I ∩ M_req ∩ M_next`, are removed, where `M_next` is
4061///    `m_temp` and `M_req` is the mask in force when the instance was
4062///    queued. `entry` is `Some(!0)` at the wait's first check, which every
4063///    form makes in the call's own turn, before any scheduler request, so
4064///    every instance pending then was pending at entry and was queued under
4065///    the guest's own mask ([`gated_own_mask`]); `None` at any later check,
4066///    where every instance kept from entry is in both masks, so `M_req` =
4067///    `m_temp` for all of them. (A narrower `entry` set limits the at-entry
4068///    rule to those bits.)
4069/// 3. `epoll` (a masked `epoll_pwait` or `epoll_pwait2`) at the first check:
4070///    an instance pending at entry in `I ∩ M_own ∖ M_temp` makes the call
4071///    return `EINTR` (`EpollInterrupted`), as `ep_poll` does
4072///    (`ignored_signals::epoll_interrupting`).
4073///
4074/// With the gate off it is never called.
4075pub(crate) async fn temporary_mask_check<T, G>(
4076    guest: &mut G,
4077    m_temp: KernelSigset,
4078    entry: Option<KernelSigset>,
4079    epoll: bool,
4080) -> Result<TemporaryMaskCheck, Error>
4081where
4082    T: RecordOrReplay,
4083    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4084{
4085    use crate::wait_signal_end::WaitSignalEnd;
4086    let state = read_thread_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())?;
4087    let reserved = guest.config().in_guest_reserved_signals;
4088    match crate::wait_signal_end::wait_end(&state, m_temp, reserved) {
4089        None => {}
4090        Some(end @ WaitSignalEnd::Fatal(_)) => {
4091            tracing::info!(
4092                "[dtid {}] under the in-guest delivery gate, {:?} ends the wait under its \
4093                 temporary mask {:#x}",
4094                guest.thread_state().dettid,
4095                end,
4096                m_temp
4097            );
4098            guest.thread_state_mut().wait_signal_end = Some(end);
4099            return Ok(TemporaryMaskCheck::Fatal);
4100        }
4101        Some(end) => {
4102            let signal = match end {
4103                WaitSignalEnd::Caught(signal) => signal,
4104                _ => {
4105                    (state.pending & !m_temp & state.caught & !reserved).trailing_zeros() as i32 + 1
4106                }
4107            };
4108            let reason = crate::refused_signal_controls::temporary_mask_caught_end_refusal(
4109                guest.thread_state().dettid.as_raw(),
4110                signal,
4111            );
4112            tracing::error!("{}", reason);
4113            crate::tool_global::stopping_refusal(guest, reason).await;
4114            return Ok(TemporaryMaskCheck::Refused);
4115        }
4116    }
4117    let own = gated_own_mask(guest, state.blocked);
4118    let now = crate::ignored_signals::pending_ignored(&state, reserved);
4119    let (removed, interrupted) = match entry {
4120        Some(entry) => {
4121            let at_entry = KernelSignalState {
4122                pending: state.pending & entry,
4123                ..state
4124            };
4125            let since = KernelSignalState {
4126                pending: state.pending & !entry,
4127                ..state
4128            };
4129            let interrupted = epoll
4130                && crate::ignored_signals::epoll_interrupting(&at_entry, own, m_temp, reserved)
4131                    != 0;
4132            (
4133                crate::ignored_signals::removable(&at_entry, own, m_temp, reserved)
4134                    | crate::ignored_signals::removable(&since, m_temp, m_temp, reserved),
4135                interrupted,
4136            )
4137        }
4138        None => (now & !m_temp, false),
4139    };
4140    remove_ignored_signals(guest, removed).await?;
4141    Ok(if interrupted {
4142        TemporaryMaskCheck::EpollInterrupted
4143    } else {
4144        TemporaryMaskCheck::Waits
4145    })
4146}
4147
4148/// The `sa_flags` of `signal`'s current action, as the guest set it, read in
4149/// this thread's turn with a query `rt_sigaction` (the in-guest runtime
4150/// answers it from the guest's action, phase 1's virtual SIGALRM included):
4151/// for the restart checkpoint's caught row (A5 design D40).
4152pub(crate) async fn caught_action_flags<T, G>(guest: &mut G, signal: i32) -> Result<u64, Error>
4153where
4154    T: RecordOrReplay,
4155    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4156{
4157    Ok(caught_action(guest, signal).await?.flags)
4158}
4159
4160/// The `sa_mask` and `sa_flags` of `signal`'s current action, as the guest set
4161/// it, read in this thread's turn with a query `rt_sigaction` (the in-guest
4162/// runtime answers it from the guest's action, phase 1's virtual SIGALRM
4163/// included): for the restart checkpoint's resolution of a
4164/// `WaitSignalEnd::BehindCaught` (A5 design D40) and its caught row. Called
4165/// only where the thread holds no committed scratch stack.
4166pub(crate) async fn caught_action<T, G>(
4167    guest: &mut G,
4168    signal: i32,
4169) -> Result<crate::wait_signal_end::CaughtAction, Error>
4170where
4171    T: RecordOrReplay,
4172    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4173{
4174    let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
4175    let action = stack.reserve::<KernelSigaction>();
4176    let _stack_guard = stack.commit()?;
4177    guest
4178        .inject_with_retry(
4179            syscalls::RtSigaction::new()
4180                .with_signum(signal)
4181                .with_action(None)
4182                .with_old_action(Some(action.cast()))
4183                .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE),
4184        )
4185        .await?;
4186    let action: KernelSigaction = guest.memory().read_value(action)?;
4187    Ok(crate::wait_signal_end::CaughtAction {
4188        mask: action.mask,
4189        flags: action.flags,
4190    })
4191}
4192
4193/// Whether the scheduler keeps a guest mask that differs from the kernel's
4194/// `SigBlk` (`Scheduler::saved_guest_sigmasks`) and reads it in its place, so
4195/// that a thread must publish it: under signal-target modelling
4196/// (`Config::models_signal_targets`, which is where the discarded-at-send
4197/// record is kept, `discarded_at_send::records`), and under the in-guest
4198/// delivery gate (`Config::in_guest_signal_delivery`; A5 step 3c.1b), where the
4199/// kernel's mask may be the in-guest runtime's. With both off, nothing is
4200/// published and every reader takes `SigBlk`, as before step 3c.1b.
4201pub(crate) fn publishes_guest_masks(cfg: &crate::Config) -> bool {
4202    crate::scheduler::discarded_at_send::records(cfg) || cfg.in_guest_signal_delivery
4203}
4204
4205/// The waiting thread's mask as last told to the scheduler
4206/// (`publish_wait_mask`). It is deliberately not `Copy`: a wait loop in an
4207/// `async move` block must reborrow it, or the block would publish into a
4208/// copy and the clear after the block would see nothing to clear.
4209#[derive(Debug, Default)]
4210pub(crate) struct PublishedWaitMask(Option<KernelSigset>);
4211
4212/// Tell the scheduler the waiting thread's effective mask
4213/// (`KernelSignalWait::effective_mask`, or `None` once the wait is over) if it
4214/// differs from `published`, the last one told. The scheduler reads it in
4215/// place of the thread's `SigBlk` (`set_saved_guest_sigmask`), for example to
4216/// decide whether a leader ignores an `ITIMER_REAL` expiry at generation
4217/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139). Only where the scheduler
4218/// reads it for a wait (`publishes_guest_masks`): under signal-target
4219/// modelling, or under the in-guest delivery gate.
4220pub(crate) async fn publish_wait_mask<T, G>(
4221    guest: &mut G,
4222    mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
4223    published: &mut PublishedWaitMask,
4224) where
4225    T: RecordOrReplay,
4226    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4227{
4228    if mask == published.0 || !publishes_guest_masks(guest.config()) {
4229        return;
4230    }
4231    crate::tool_global::set_saved_guest_sigmask(guest, mask).await;
4232    published.0 = mask;
4233}
4234
4235async fn retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state<T, G, C>(
4236    guest: &mut G,
4237    call0: C,
4238    rsrc: Resources,
4239    maybe_timeout: Option<(LogicalTime, Result<i64, Errno>)>,
4240) -> Result<i64, Error>
4241where
4242    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
4243    T: RecordOrReplay,
4244    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4245{
4246    retry_blocking_wait_under_mask(guest, call0, rsrc, maybe_timeout, None)
4247        .await
4248        .0
4249}
4250
4251/// `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state` for a call that sleeps under
4252/// `wait_mask` instead of the guest's own mask, when it is set: the temporary
4253/// mask of an `epoll_pwait` (`KernelSignalWait::with_wait_mask`). `call0`
4254/// carries no mask, so its probes run under the guest's own mask until every
4255/// blockable signal is blocked, as for any other wait. Also returns whether the
4256/// signal that ended the wait must still be delivered under `wait_mask`: one
4257/// that only `wait_mask` lets in, pending in the kernel under the guest's own
4258/// mask once it is put back, which the caller delivers with
4259/// `inject_signal_delivery`, as a masked pselect6 does.
4260pub(crate) async fn retry_blocking_wait_under_mask<T, G, C>(
4261    guest: &mut G,
4262    call0: C,
4263    rsrc: Resources,
4264    maybe_timeout: Option<(LogicalTime, Result<i64, Errno>)>,
4265    wait_mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
4266) -> (Result<i64, Error>, bool)
4267where
4268    C: NonblockableSyscall + Into<Syscall>,
4269    T: RecordOrReplay,
4270    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4271{
4272    let mut signals = KernelSignalWait::new(
4273        guest,
4274        call0.signals_consumed_by_wait(&guest.memory()),
4275        call0.restart_keeps_deadline(),
4276        call0.kernel_restart_errno(),
4277    )
4278    .with_deadline(maybe_timeout.is_some())
4279    .with_wait_mask(wait_mask);
4280    // Set when a signal that only `wait_mask` lets in ends the wait.
4281    let mut deliver_under_wait_mask = false;
4282    let mut published = PublishedWaitMask::default();
4283    publish_wait_mask(guest, signals.effective_mask(), &mut published).await;
4284    let mut rsrc = rsrc.clone();
4285    rsrc.poll_deadline = poll_deadline_for(guest, maybe_timeout.map(|(deadline, _)| deadline));
4286    let (mut call, mut guard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
4287    let mut first_turn = true;
4288    // Set when only a signal the scheduler committed in this turn ends the
4289    // wait: the turn's probe runs first, and the wait ends with the restart
4290    // errno only if the call has nothing to report.
4291    let mut interrupt_after_probe;
4292
4293    let result = loop {
4294        interrupt_after_probe = false;
4295        // A scheduler `Signaled` answer only says a signal may be pending. The kernel's
4296        // state below decides whether it ends the wait.
4297        let resumed = resource_request(guest, rsrc.clone()).await;
4298        // Read in this turn, before any injection: another thread may have
4299        // armed a host-timed source since the last turn, and none can until
4300        // this turn ends. The same round trip gives the `SIGCHLD` a guest sent
4301        // this thread that the schedule recorded in its private queue, which
4302        // an injection of this turn (the timerfd publication below) could
4303        // otherwise take into the backend's single held slot (R2b-2 stage 3,
4304        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273).
4305        let (host_timed, recorded) =
4306            crate::tool_global::host_timed_and_private_sigchld(guest).await;
4307        signals.hold_until_return(host_timed);
4308        // A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler committed to this thread in this turn, sent
4309        // at a commit point (a child's child-exit timer, or a POSIX timer whose
4310        // signal is `SIGCHLD`), ends the wait, as on Linux
4311        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005), and so does a
4312        // recorded private one: both are admitted (`KernelSignalWait::admit`).
4313        let committed = committed_signals(&resumed) & kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
4314        let private = match signals
4315            .admit_under_block(guest, committed, recorded, host_timed, &mut published)
4316            .await
4317        {
4318            Ok(private) => private,
4319            Err(error) => break Err(error),
4320        };
4321        signals.admit(committed, private);
4322        // As in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`: virtual timerfds first.
4323        // As in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`: release the nonblocking
4324        // form's scratch stack before publishing, and convert again after.
4325        let reconvert =
4326            guard.is_some() && crate::syscalls::timerfd::may_publish(guest, call.into());
4327        if reconvert {
4328            guard = None;
4329        }
4330        rsrc.poll_deadline = crate::syscalls::timerfd::publish_before_probe(
4331            guest,
4332            call.into(),
4333            maybe_timeout.map(|(deadline, _)| deadline),
4334        )
4335        .await;
4336        if reconvert {
4337            (call, guard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
4338        }
4339        // A pending real-time timer expiration that this wait would consume or
4340        // be ended by (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089).
4341        let pending = pending_real_time_among(guest, REAL_TIME_SIGNALS).await;
4342        if pending != 0 {
4343            match signals.observable_now() {
4344                Ok(observable) => act_on_pending_real_time(guest, pending, observable, 0).await,
4345                Err(error) => break Err(error),
4346            }
4347        }
4348        let first = std::mem::take(&mut first_turn);
4349        // Never `inject_with_retry`: see `KernelSignalWait`.
4350        let injected = if first {
4351            // The first probe runs before the check, so a source that was ready when
4352            // the call began, or an argument error, is reported as Linux reports it
4353            // whatever signal is pending (`inject_first_probe`).
4354            signals.inject_first_probe(guest, call).await
4355        } else {
4356            let state = match signals.interrupted_with_state() {
4357                Ok((false, state)) => state,
4358                // Linux takes a completion before it returns EINTR: a queued
4359                // signal of rt_sigtimedwait's set (`do_sigtimedwait` dequeues
4360                // first, and again after it sleeps), a ready descriptor of poll
4361                // or epoll_wait. A signal the scheduler committed in this turn
4362                // was sent at the same fixed point as any completion this turn
4363                // can see, so the completion wins, as on Linux (Codex review of
4364                // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4039).
4365                Ok((true, state)) if signals.interrupts_only_by_committed(&state) => {
4366                    interrupt_after_probe = true;
4367                    deliver_under_wait_mask = signals.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state);
4368                    state
4369                }
4370                Ok((true, state)) => {
4371                    deliver_under_wait_mask = signals.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state);
4372                    let errno = call0.kernel_restart_errno();
4373                    tracing::trace!(
4374                        "retry_nonblocking_syscall: pending signals interrupt {}: {:?}",
4375                        call.display(&guest.memory()),
4376                        errno
4377                    );
4378                    break Err(errno.into());
4379                }
4380                Err(error) => break Err(error),
4381            };
4382            signals.inject_absorbing_after(guest, call, state).await
4383        };
4384        let syscall_result = match injected {
4385            Ok(result) => result,
4386            Err(error) => {
4387                tracing::trace!(
4388                    "retry_nonblocking_syscall: a signal stop ends the wait in {}: {:?}",
4389                    call.display(&guest.memory()),
4390                    error
4391                );
4392                break Err(error);
4393            }
4394        };
4395        if !call.syscall_would_have_blocked(syscall_result) {
4396            let res = call
4397                .normalize_nonblocking_result(syscall_result, rsrc.poll_attempt > 0)
4398                .map_err(|e| e.into());
4399            tracing::trace!(
4400                "retry_nonblocking_syscall: syscall completed after {} retries: {} = {:?}",
4401                rsrc.poll_attempt,
4402                call.display(&guest.memory()),
4403                res
4404            );
4405            break res;
4406        }
4407        if interrupt_after_probe {
4408            let errno = call0.kernel_restart_errno();
4409            tracing::trace!(
4410                "retry_nonblocking_syscall: a committed signal interrupts {}: {:?}",
4411                call.display(&guest.memory()),
4412                errno
4413            );
4414            break Err(errno.into());
4415        }
4416        if first {
4417            // The first turn's check, after its probe found nothing to report.
4418            match signals.interrupted_with_state() {
4419                Ok((false, _)) => {}
4420                Ok((true, state)) => {
4421                    deliver_under_wait_mask = signals.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state);
4422                    let errno = call0.kernel_restart_errno();
4423                    tracing::trace!(
4424                        "retry_nonblocking_syscall: pending signals interrupt {}: {:?}",
4425                        call.display(&guest.memory()),
4426                        errno
4427                    );
4428                    break Err(errno.into());
4429                }
4430                Err(error) => break Err(error),
4431            }
4432        }
4433        if signals.needs_block() {
4434            // Only one scratch-stack guard may be live, so release the probe's, block
4435            // signals from a fresh one, and rebuild the probe.
4436            guard = None;
4437            if let Err(error) = signals.block(guest, None).await {
4438                break Err(error);
4439            }
4440            publish_wait_mask(guest, signals.effective_mask(), &mut published).await;
4441            (call, guard) = call0.into_nonblocking(guest).await;
4442        }
4443        rsrc.poll_attempt += 1;
4444        if let Some((timeout, timeout_result)) = maybe_timeout {
4445            let new_time = thread_observe_time(guest).await;
4446            if new_time >= timeout {
4447                tracing::trace!(
4448                    "Timing out syscall after #{} retries: {}",
4449                    rsrc.poll_attempt - 1,
4450                    call.display(&guest.memory())
4451                );
4452                break timeout_result.map_err(|e| e.into());
4453            }
4454            tracing::trace!(
4455                "Retry #{} for syscall due to result {:?}, {} from timeout: {}",
4456                rsrc.poll_attempt,
4457                syscall_result,
4458                timeout - new_time,
4459                call.display(&guest.memory())
4460            );
4461        } else {
4462            tracing::trace!(
4463                "Retry #{} for syscall due to result {:?}: {}",
4464                rsrc.poll_attempt,
4465                syscall_result,
4466                call.display(&guest.memory())
4467            );
4468        }
4469        record_retry_event(guest, call).await;
4470    };
4471
4472    drop(guard);
4473    let restored = signals.restore(guest, None).await;
4474    publish_wait_mask(guest, None, &mut published).await;
4475    let result = match result_after_restore(restored, result) {
4476        Ok(result) => result,
4477        Err(error) => return (Err(error), false),
4478    };
4479    // A signal the backend holds is delivered as the guest resumes, under the
4480    // guest's own mask (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1011).
4481    let deliver = deliver_under_wait_mask && !signals.holds_signal() && result.is_err();
4482    (
4483        refuse_held_signal_loss(guest, call0.number(), result).await,
4484        deliver,
4485    )
4486}
4487
4488/// The internal failure, if any, that `refusal` names, for thread `dettid`
4489/// handling the guest's `sysno`. `UnsupportedOperation::ToolDecided` is a
4490/// backend's statement that it left a call Detcore injected to the Tool,
4491/// because the Tool decides that call on every backend (the KVM executor's
4492/// CPU, scheduling, priority, id, getrandom, prlimit64, membarrier, seccomp
4493/// and getpgrp calls). Detcore answers every such call itself, except the
4494/// getpgrp that a clone3 race passes through to the backend
4495/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4531); so one that reached the
4496/// backend is a Detcore defect or that race, never an answer for the guest.
4497/// Every other refusal belongs to the call site that injected it and is not
4498/// judged here.
4499pub(crate) fn tool_decided_injection_failure(
4500    refusal: Option<reverie::UnsupportedRefusal>,
4501    dettid: DetTid,
4502    sysno: Sysno,
4503) -> Option<String> {
4504    refusal
4505        .filter(|refusal| refusal.operation == reverie::UnsupportedOperation::ToolDecided)
4506        .map(|refusal| {
4507            format!(
4508                "HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=tool-decided-injection dtid={dettid} \
4509                 syscall={sysno}: the backend refused a call Detcore injected, as one the Tool \
4510                 decides on every backend ({}); Detcore must answer it itself",
4511                refusal.diagnostic
4512            )
4513        })
4514}
4515
4516/// Ends the run as an internal failure when the last call Detcore injected
4517/// while handling the guest's `sysno` came back with a `ToolDecided` refusal
4518/// ([`tool_decided_injection_failure`]), instead of letting its ENOSYS reach
4519/// the guest. The panic text and the error log carry
4520/// `HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=tool-decided-injection`; the CLI's own
4521/// summary line classifies the run as `class=container-child-panic`.
4522///
4523/// This is not a general guard. That no Detcore path injects one of these
4524/// calls on KVM rests on an audit of Detcore's handlers. The one known
4525/// exception is a race: under --no-sequentialize-threads a sibling can
4526/// rewrite clone3's argument struct between Detcore's read and the KVM
4527/// executor's, so a child Detcore marks as in a nested PID namespace passes
4528/// its getpgrp through to the backend (tracked in
4529/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4531). This check mitigates
4530/// that path: it runs once per syscall event, after Detcore's handler
4531/// returns and before the result is used, and a backend's refusal describes
4532/// only the latest injection, so it sees a handler's pass-through when that
4533/// is the event's last injection. It does not see:
4534/// - an injection of one of these calls followed by another injection in the
4535///   same event, which clears the first one's refusal;
4536/// - a refusal that a consumer takes and filters first, such as
4537///   `report_backend_signal_refusal` (signal.rs), behind the
4538///   thread-directed process signal capability that is false on KVM;
4539/// - injections from Tool callbacks other than the syscall handler (signal
4540///   events, thread start, post-exec, exit, timers);
4541/// - `tail_inject`, whose result goes straight to the guest.
4542///
4543/// A general guard needs a Reverie API hook and is not part of this change.
4544///
4545/// Any other refusal it takes counts the call as refused in the syscall
4546/// histogram (`crate::syscall_histogram`). A signalfd operation the backend
4547/// does not model (`UnsupportedOperation::Signalfd`: a read that would wait,
4548/// an epoll registration, a process created while one is open) is named in a
4549/// warning as well: no handler takes that refusal, and its ENOSYS reaches the
4550/// guest as the backend answered.
4551pub(crate) fn fail_on_tool_decided_injection<T, G>(guest: &mut G, sysno: Sysno)
4552where
4553    T: RecordOrReplay,
4554    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4555{
4556    let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
4557    let refusal = guest.take_unsupported_refusal();
4558    if refusal.is_some() {
4559        crate::syscall_histogram::mark_refused::<T, G>(guest);
4560    }
4561    if let Some(refusal) =
4562        refusal.filter(|refusal| refusal.operation == reverie::UnsupportedOperation::Signalfd)
4563    {
4564        tracing::warn!(
4565            "[dtid {dettid}] {sysno} refused by the backend: {}",
4566            refusal.diagnostic
4567        );
4568    }
4569    if let Some(failure) = tool_decided_injection_failure(refusal, dettid, sysno) {
4570        tracing::error!("{failure}");
4571        panic!("{failure}");
4572    }
4573}
4574
4575/// The policy of `Detcore::refuse_unserviceable_operation`, for a caller that
4576/// holds the guest but not the tool. `panic_on_unsupported_syscalls` is the
4577/// setting of that name: the tool's own copy in the method, the guest's
4578/// configuration in `refuse_held_signal_loss`.
4579pub(crate) async fn refuse_unserviceable_operation_with<T, G>(
4580    guest: &mut G,
4581    panic_on_unsupported_syscalls: bool,
4582    sysno: Sysno,
4583    fallback: Errno,
4584    reason: Option<&str>,
4585) -> Result<i64, Error>
4586where
4587    T: RecordOrReplay,
4588    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4589{
4590    crate::syscall_histogram::mark_refused::<T, G>(guest);
4591    if !panic_on_unsupported_syscalls {
4592        return Err(fallback.into());
4593    }
4594    if guest.config().shutdown_on_unsupported_syscall {
4595        // Fail-closed policy: the operation is unserviceable and the config
4596        // forbids passing it through. Say why first: on an in-guest backend
4597        // the exit below ends only the guest process, and the launcher learns
4598        // the reason from the coordinator.
4599        let reason = match reason {
4600            Some(reason) => format!("{sysno}: {reason}"),
4601            None => format!(
4602                "{sysno} cannot be serviced on this backend (with \
4603                 --allow-unsupported-syscalls the guest would see {fallback})"
4604            ),
4605        };
4606        crate::tool_global::report_policy_refusal(guest, reason).await;
4607        crate::tool_global::unrecoverable_shutdown(
4608            guest,
4609            detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT,
4610        )
4611        .await;
4612    }
4613    if guest.config().exit_on_unsupported_syscall {
4614        return Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(
4615            crate::UnsupportedSyscallError(sysno),
4616        )));
4617    }
4618    panic!("unserviceable operation on syscall: {sysno:?}");
4619}
4620
4621/// The signals the guest ignores, blocked for one wait that Detcore runs in the
4622/// kernel under the thread's own mask: the `epoll_wait` family (`ep_poll`), and
4623/// `poll`, `select`, and `ppoll` and `pselect6` naming no mask (`do_sys_poll`,
4624/// `core_sys_select`). Linux discards a signal the process ignores when it is
4625/// generated (`sig_ignored`), so it never ends such a wait, but it queues one
4626/// for a traced thread. An epoll wait then returned `EINTR` to the guest. A
4627/// poll-family wait ended with a restart code instead: a `poll` restarts
4628/// through `restart_syscall`, which Detcore refuses, and a `select`,
4629/// `pselect6` or `ppoll` runs again in place, or returns `EINTR` when Linux
4630/// cannot write back its time left (`poll_select_finish`). Blocked for the
4631/// wait, such a signal stays pending without ending it; once the guest's mask
4632/// is back it is delivered and ignored, as it was before.
4633/// The mask changes through the backend (`Guest::set_blocked_signals`, on
4634/// ptrace `PTRACE_SETSIGMASK`), so no syscall the guest or the recorder sees is
4635/// added. Replay, which serves the wait from the recording, raises the same
4636/// shield: the scheduler reads the thread's mask when it commits the wait's
4637/// request (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask`), and record and replay must
4638/// present the same one.
4639#[must_use]
4640pub(crate) struct IgnoredSignalShield {
4641    /// The guest's mask to put back, when the shield is up.
4642    guest_mask: Option<u64>,
4643}
4644
4645impl IgnoredSignalShield {
4646    /// No shield: the wait cannot block, or runs under its own temporary mask
4647    /// (or one the tracer cannot read).
4648    pub(crate) fn none() -> Self {
4649        Self { guest_mask: None }
4650    }
4651
4652    /// Blocks the signals the guest ignores and does not block, read from the
4653    /// kernel (`KernelSignalState::discarded_at_generation`). If the state
4654    /// cannot be read or the backend refuses the change and left the mask as
4655    /// it was, the wait runs under the guest's own mask, as it did before. A
4656    /// change that may have been written without being confirmed ends the
4657    /// run: the guest must not resume as if its mask were known
4658    /// (`MaskChangeRefused::Failed`).
4659    pub(crate) async fn raise<T, G>(guest: &mut G) -> Result<Self, Error>
4660    where
4661        T: RecordOrReplay,
4662        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4663    {
4664        let state = match crate::syscalls::read_thread_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid()) {
4665            Ok(state) => state,
4666            Err(errno) => {
4667                tracing::debug!("[tid {}] no ignored-signal shield: {errno}", guest.tid());
4668                return Ok(Self::none());
4669            }
4670        };
4671        let Some(mask) = ignored_signal_shield_mask(&state) else {
4672            return Ok(Self::none());
4673        };
4674        match guest.set_blocked_signals(mask).await {
4675            Ok(guest_mask) => Ok(Self {
4676                guest_mask: Some(guest_mask),
4677            }),
4678            Err(refused) if shield_refusal_leaves_the_mask_known(&refused) => {
4679                tracing::debug!("[tid {}] no ignored-signal shield: {refused}", guest.tid());
4680                Ok(Self::none())
4681            }
4682            Err(refused) => Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
4683                "[tid {}] could not block the signals the guest ignores ({mask:#x}) for a wait, \
4684                 and its signal mask is unknown: {refused}",
4685                guest.tid()
4686            ))),
4687        }
4688    }
4689
4690    /// Puts the guest's mask back. The guest must not resume under the
4691    /// shield, so a mask that cannot be put back ends the run.
4692    pub(crate) async fn lower<T, G>(mut self, guest: &mut G) -> Result<(), Error>
4693    where
4694        T: RecordOrReplay,
4695        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4696    {
4697        let Some(guest_mask) = self.guest_mask.take() else {
4698            return Ok(());
4699        };
4700        match guest.set_blocked_signals(guest_mask).await {
4701            Ok(_) | Err(MaskChangeRefused::Gone) => Ok(()),
4702            Err(refused) => Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::anyhow!(
4703                "[tid {}] could not put back the guest's signal mask {guest_mask:#x} after a \
4704                 wait that blocked the signals it ignores: {refused}",
4705                guest.tid()
4706            ))),
4707        }
4708    }
4709}
4710
4711/// A shield is dropped with its mask still to put back only when the
4712/// backend cancelled the handler around it, which it does when the thread
4713/// dies during the wait or an injection (a sibling's `exit_group` or
4714/// `execve`, a SIGKILL), or when a backend error is ending the run. Drop
4715/// cannot tell those apart, so its log claims neither: it says only that
4716/// the handler ended with the mask unrestored.
4717/// The log line for a shield dropped with its mask still to put back.
4718/// It must not claim the thread is gone: Drop cannot prove that (the
4719/// handler may also be cancelled by a backend error ending the run).
4720fn shield_drop_message(guest_mask: u64) -> String {
4721    format!(
4722        "an ignored-signal shield ended with its handler, leaving the guest's mask \
4723         {guest_mask:#x} unrestored; the handler ended before the mask could be put \
4724         back (the thread may have died, or the run may be ending)"
4725    )
4726}
4727
4728impl Drop for IgnoredSignalShield {
4729    fn drop(&mut self) {
4730        if let Some(guest_mask) = self.guest_mask {
4731            tracing::debug!("{}", shield_drop_message(guest_mask));
4732        }
4733    }
4734}
4735
4736/// Whether a refused shield change left the thread's mask as it was, so the
4737/// wait can run under it: every refusal but a failure after which the backend
4738/// could not confirm the mask (`MaskChangeRefused::Failed`'s `mask_unknown`).
4739fn shield_refusal_leaves_the_mask_known(refused: &MaskChangeRefused) -> bool {
4740    !matches!(
4741        refused,
4742        MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
4743            mask_unknown: true,
4744            ..
4745        }
4746    )
4747}
4748
4749/// The mask an ignored-signal shield sets over `state`: the thread's mask and
4750/// the signals it would discard at generation, or `None` when there are none
4751/// (`IgnoredSignalShield`).
4752fn ignored_signal_shield_mask(state: &KernelSignalState) -> Option<KernelSigset> {
4753    let ignored = state.discarded_at_generation();
4754    (ignored != 0).then_some(state.blocked | ignored)
4755}
4756
4757/// Refuse the guest's `sysno` call when its wait ended with a
4758/// [`HeldSignalRefusal`], through the unsupported-operation policy
4759/// (`refuse_unserviceable_operation_with`): a fail-closed run, which ordinary
4760/// `hermit run` is, ends with the policy's exit, and a run started with
4761/// `--allow-unsupported-syscalls` gets `ERESTARTNOINTR`, the transparent
4762/// restart that such a wait returned before (round-10 High 1 on
4763/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361). The message names the call,
4764/// the signals and that pull request. Callers pass the wait's result after the
4765/// wait has put the guest's mask back. Every other result passes through.
4766///
4767/// Whether a wait meets such a stop can depend on host timing, as a signal
4768/// sent from outside the guest does, so a refusal can be host-timed: it
4769/// replaces a run that would have gone on to depend on that timing.
4770pub(crate) async fn refuse_held_signal_loss<T, G>(
4771    guest: &mut G,
4772    sysno: Sysno,
4773    result: Result<i64, Error>,
4774) -> Result<i64, Error>
4775where
4776    T: RecordOrReplay,
4777    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4778{
4779    use std::io::Write as _;
4780    let refusal = match &result {
4781        Err(Error::Tool(error)) => match error.downcast_ref::<HeldSignalRefusal>() {
4782            Some(refusal) => HeldSignalRefusal {
4783                wait: Some(sysno),
4784                ..*refusal
4785            },
4786            None => return result,
4787        },
4788        _ => return result,
4789    };
4790    let panic_on_unsupported_syscalls = guest.config().panic_on_unsupported_syscalls;
4791    tracing::error!("[tid {}] {}", guest.tid(), refusal);
4792    if panic_on_unsupported_syscalls {
4793        // The run ends: report why even when logging is disabled or redirected,
4794        // as the refusal of a nonleader exec does.
4795        let _ = writeln!(crate::util::RetryingStderr, "{refusal}");
4796    }
4797    refuse_unserviceable_operation_with(
4798        guest,
4799        panic_on_unsupported_syscalls,
4800        sysno,
4801        Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR,
4802        None,
4803    )
4804    .await
4805}
4806
4807/// Signal handling for one blocking wait whose interruption is decided from the
4808/// kernel's signal state (`supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`).
4809///
4810/// A wait ends early only for a signal that would end it natively: one the guest
4811/// does not block and that is caught, or whose default action terminates or stops
4812/// the process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Blocked,
4813/// ignored, and default-ignored signals do not end it, and neither does a default
4814/// job-control stop when `defers_default_stops` is set
4815/// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting_wait`), apart from the stops that
4816/// `inject_absorbing` cannot absorb safely, which end it with a restart.
4817///
4818/// The first probe runs under the guest's own mask. If it would block, `block`
4819/// blocks every blockable signal for the rest of the wait, so later probes cannot
4820/// be stopped by one and every signal that arrives stays pending in the kernel,
4821/// where `/proc` reports it. `interrupted_with_state` classifies the pending set
4822/// against the guest's mask and dispositions each turn, and `restore` puts the
4823/// guest's mask back before the call returns, so a pending interrupting signal
4824/// is delivered as the call returns its restart errno.
4825///
4826/// Probes and the mask change go through `inject_absorbing`, never
4827/// `inject_with_retry`. A signal that stops the guest around an injection is
4828/// dequeued from the kernel and held by the backend in a single slot, so a blind
4829/// retry that is stopped again would replace it. `inject_absorbing` works out
4830/// from `/proc` which signal the backend holds and injects again only when that
4831/// signal would not end the wait natively. Before the mask is set, a signal
4832/// pending at the turn's `/proc` read that would end the wait is reported by
4833/// `interrupted_with_state`, and any other unblocked one stops the next
4834/// injection and is absorbed; a signal that arrives after the read can stop an
4835/// injection in a way that cannot be identified, and is held without ending the
4836/// wait, so the wait keeps its deadline and its checks, unless the backend held
4837/// a signal whose loss matters, which ends the wait with a
4838/// [`HeldSignalRefusal`] (`inject_absorbing`).
4839/// Afterwards only a signal that cannot be blocked can stop an injection. A stop
4840/// after a probe ran replaces its result, so a probe that consumed something (an
4841/// edge-triggered event, a dequeued signal) loses it; that remains a known gap.
4842///
4843/// No failure of this machinery reaches the guest as an errno the wait call
4844/// cannot return. A `/proc` read that fails for a thread that still exists, or a
4845/// guest mask that cannot be put back, ends the run with a
4846/// [`BlockedWaitSignalError`]; a thread that no longer exists gets
4847/// `ERESTARTNOINTR`, which nothing observes (`read_wait_signal_state`). If the
4848/// mask cannot be changed at all (no scratch room below the guest's stack
4849/// pointer, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3328), `block` leaves the
4850/// guest's own mask in place and every later probe runs under it, as the first
4851/// probe does.
4852/// The real-time signals, 32 to 64, as kernel sigset bits.
4853pub(crate) const REAL_TIME_SIGNALS: KernelSigset = !0 << 31;
4854
4855/// The signals a thread whose mask becomes `mask` lets the kernel take from
4856/// its queues: those `mask` does not block, split into the ones whose delivery
4857/// the guest observes and the ones Linux discards on delivery because their
4858/// disposition is `SIG_IGN`.
4859pub(crate) fn unblocked_by(
4860    state: &KernelSignalState,
4861    mask: KernelSigset,
4862) -> (KernelSigset, KernelSigset) {
4863    unblocked_by_ignored(state.ignored, mask)
4864}
4865
4866/// [`unblocked_by`] given only the thread's ignored set, from wherever it
4867/// comes (the kernel's `/proc` view or Detcore's copy).
4868pub(crate) fn unblocked_by_ignored(
4869    ignored: KernelSigset,
4870    mask: KernelSigset,
4871) -> (KernelSigset, KernelSigset) {
4872    let unblocked = !mask;
4873    (unblocked & !ignored, unblocked & ignored)
4874}
4875
4876/// The real-time timer expirations among `candidates` (a kernel sigset) that
4877/// are pending for the calling thread's process because every thread blocked
4878/// them when they expired (`Scheduler::pending_real_time_expirations`,
4879/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089). 0 without asking the
4880/// scheduler until one has been kept pending in this run
4881/// (`scheduler::real_time_expiration_kept_pending`), or when `candidates`
4882/// holds no real-time signal. Asked in the calling thread's turn.
4883pub(crate) async fn pending_real_time_among<T, G>(guest: &mut G, candidates: KernelSigset) -> u64
4884where
4885    T: RecordOrReplay,
4886    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4887{
4888    let candidates = candidates & REAL_TIME_SIGNALS;
4889    if candidates == 0 || !crate::scheduler::real_time_expiration_kept_pending() {
4890        return 0;
4891    }
4892    let Some(detpid) = guest.thread_state().detpid else {
4893        return 0;
4894    };
4895    crate::tool_global::pending_real_time_expirations(guest, detpid).await & candidates
4896}
4897
4898/// Where a call lets the guest observe the signals in `observable` (deliver,
4899/// dequeue or report them), refuse the run by name if one of the `pending`
4900/// real-time timer expirations (`pending_real_time_among`) is among them, and
4901/// discard the pending ones in `discarded`, which Linux discards there.
4902pub(crate) async fn act_on_pending_real_time<T, G>(
4903    guest: &mut G,
4904    pending: KernelSigset,
4905    observable: KernelSigset,
4906    discarded: KernelSigset,
4907) where
4908    T: RecordOrReplay,
4909    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4910{
4911    let observed = pending & observable;
4912    if observed != 0 {
4913        crate::scheduler::refuse_real_time_expiration(observed.trailing_zeros() as i32 + 1);
4914    }
4915    if pending & discarded != 0
4916        && let Some(detpid) = guest.thread_state().detpid
4917    {
4918        crate::tool_global::discard_pending_real_time_expirations(
4919            guest,
4920            detpid,
4921            pending & discarded,
4922        )
4923        .await;
4924    }
4925}
4926
4927/// For a call that runs under the temporary mask `mask`: refuse by name for a
4928/// pending real-time timer expiration the mask lets the kernel deliver, and
4929/// discard one it lets the kernel discard. Reads the thread's dispositions
4930/// only when one is pending.
4931pub(crate) async fn observe_under_mask<T, G>(guest: &mut G, mask: KernelSigset) -> Result<(), Error>
4932where
4933    T: RecordOrReplay,
4934    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
4935{
4936    let pending = pending_real_time_among(guest, !mask).await;
4937    if pending != 0 {
4938        let ignored = match crate::syscalls::signal_shadow::copied_dispositions(guest) {
4939            Some(copied) => copied.ignored,
4940            None => read_thread_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid())?.ignored,
4941        };
4942        let (observable, discarded) = unblocked_by_ignored(ignored, mask);
4943        act_on_pending_real_time(guest, pending, observable, discarded).await;
4944    }
4945    Ok(())
4946}
4947
4948pub(crate) struct KernelSignalWait {
4949    pid: reverie::Pid,
4950    tid: reverie::Pid,
4951    /// Signals the wait itself consumes (rt_sigtimedwait's set), which never
4952    /// interrupt it.
4953    consumed: KernelSigset,
4954    /// Whether a default job-control stop leaves the wait running, because Linux's
4955    /// restart of the call keeps its deadline
4956    /// (`NonblockableSyscall::restart_keeps_deadline`).
4957    defers_default_stops: bool,
4958    /// The errno that ends the wait for an interrupting signal: the restart code
4959    /// Linux uses for the call (`NonblockableSyscall::kernel_restart_errno`). A
4960    /// signal the backend holds turns `ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK` into `ERESTARTNOHAND`
4961    /// (`held_signal_restart_errno`).
4962    restart_errno: Errno,
4963    /// Signals that never end the wait, even ones that would end it natively.
4964    /// They stay pending in the kernel, or held by the backend, and are
4965    /// delivered as the call returns, once the guest's mask is put back. In
4966    /// every wait but `select`'s and `pselect6`'s (`for_select`) this is
4967    /// `SIGCHLD`, whichever process sent it: the kernel also posts one for a
4968    /// child's exit, stop or continue at a moment set by host timing, and
4969    /// `/proc` shows no siginfo that would tell the two apart
4970    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). The scheduler's own
4971    /// send of a `SIGCHLD` to this thread at a commit point lifts the hold for the
4972    /// turn whose resume names it (`admit`,
4973    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005). The gated loop adds,
4974    /// in each of its turns, every signal a host-timed source armed by a guest
4975    /// can post to this process (`hold_until_return`).
4976    held_until_return: KernelSigset,
4977    /// Whether the wait has a finite deadline (`with_deadline`). Hermit cannot
4978    /// install the restart block with which Linux keeps the absolute deadline
4979    /// of a restarted `poll` or timed futex wait, and a restarted `ppoll`,
4980    /// `epoll_wait`, `epoll_pwait` or `rt_sigtimedwait` runs again with the
4981    /// guest's unchanged timeout. So a transparent restart would start the
4982    /// timeout again, and such a wait never ends with `ERESTARTNOINTR`
4983    /// (`inject_absorbing`).
4984    deadline: bool,
4985    /// The guest's own mask while the wait runs with every signal blocked.
4986    saved_mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
4987    /// `block` could not change the mask, so probes run under the guest's own.
4988    unblockable: bool,
4989    /// `saved_mask` was installed by `block_in_place`, through
4990    /// `Guest::set_blocked_signals`, so `restore` puts it back the same way,
4991    /// with no injection and no scratch memory.
4992    blocked_in_place: bool,
4993    /// The signal the backend holds since `inject_absorbing` absorbed a stop;
4994    /// `None` also after a stop it could not identify (`held_unidentified`).
4995    held: Option<HeldSignal>,
4996    /// The backend holds a signal from a stop that `inject_absorbing` could not
4997    /// identify, which may be one whose loss matters, so no later stop may
4998    /// replace it (`would_replace_precious`).
4999    held_unidentified: bool,
5000    /// The signals `hold_until_return` added because a host-timed source armed
5001    /// by a guest can post them; a committed signal never lifts these
5002    /// (`admit`).
5003    host_timed: KernelSigset,
5004    /// Signals the scheduler committed to this thread in the current turn,
5005    /// which end the wait even though it holds them (`admit`).
5006    committed: KernelSigset,
5007    /// The `SIGCHLD` a guest sent this thread, which the schedule recorded in
5008    /// its private queue, admitted in the current turn (`admit_under_block`):
5009    /// it ends the wait from the thread's own queue only, even though the
5010    /// wait holds it (R2b-2 stage 3,
5011    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273).
5012    private: KernelSigset,
5013    /// The mask the wait sleeps under, when it is not the guest's own: the
5014    /// temporary mask of a `pselect6` (`with_wait_mask`). A signal decides
5015    /// against it whether it ends the wait; `restore` still puts back the
5016    /// guest's own mask (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3991).
5017    wait_mask: Option<KernelSigset>,
5018}
5019
5020/// A signal that stopped one of a wait's injections and that the backend holds
5021/// for delivery when the guest resumes (`KernelSignalWait::inject_absorbing`).
5022#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
5023struct HeldSignal {
5024    signal: i32,
5025    queue: SignalQueue,
5026    kind: HeldKind,
5027}
5028
5029/// Whether losing a held signal, which a later stop would replace, changes what
5030/// the guest or the scheduler observes.
5031#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd)]
5032enum HeldKind {
5033    /// Its delivery does nothing: it is ignored, or default-ignored and not
5034    /// `SIGCHLD`.
5035    Harmless,
5036    /// Its delivery matters, or is kept as if it did: a signal the wait holds
5037    /// until the call returns (`held_until_return`), which may run a handler
5038    /// then, any other `SIGCHLD`, or a default job-control stop that the wait
5039    /// defers.
5040    Precious,
5041}
5042
5043/// How a wait would lose a signal that the backend holds, or deliver it in
5044/// place of the result Linux gives (`HeldSignalRefusal`).
5045#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
5046pub(crate) enum HeldSignalLoss {
5047    /// Another pending signal would stop the next injection, and the backend,
5048    /// which has one slot for a held signal, would drop the held one for it.
5049    Replaced,
5050    /// A stop that `/proc` cannot identify replaced a held signal whose loss
5051    /// matters (`HeldKind::Precious`), or one that could not be identified
5052    /// either and so may matter.
5053    UnidentifiedStop,
5054    /// The wait reached `MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS` absorbed stops while the backend
5055    /// held a signal whose loss matters or that could not be identified.
5056    StopBound,
5057    /// A signal that a wait without a deadline consumes stopped an injection,
5058    /// so the backend holds it and delivers it rather than the wait returning
5059    /// it, and either it is one the wait holds until the call returns
5060    /// (`held_until_return`) or it replaced a held signal whose loss matters.
5061    Consumed,
5062    /// A signal stopped an injection of `restore`, which puts the guest's mask
5063    /// back and so must run whatever is pending, and the backend dropped a held
5064    /// signal whose loss matters, or one that could not be identified, for it.
5065    Restoration,
5066}
5067
5068/// A wait that ends because going on, or restarting the call, would lose a
5069/// signal the backend holds, or deliver it in place of the result Linux gives.
5070///
5071/// Every path that used to end such a wait with a fallback that returns
5072/// success (a transparent `ERESTARTNOINTR` restart, or a wait that went on and
5073/// let a stop replace the held signal) returns this instead (round-10 High 1 on
5074/// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361). The wait puts the guest's mask
5075/// back, and its caller then applies the unsupported-operation policy
5076/// (`refuse_held_signal_loss`). A complete successful repair preserving signal
5077/// information needs additional framework support with the current generic
5078/// API: the backend holds one signal, does not say which, and delivers it
5079/// without the tool. A Detcore-only refusal or capability withdrawal can
5080/// prevent the determinism regression.
5081#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
5082pub(crate) struct HeldSignalRefusal {
5083    /// The guest call whose wait ends, once the caller names it
5084    /// (`refuse_held_signal_loss`).
5085    pub(crate) wait: Option<Sysno>,
5086    /// The signal the backend holds that would be lost or delivered wrongly;
5087    /// `None` when it could not be identified.
5088    pub(crate) held: Option<i32>,
5089    /// The signal that would replace it, or that stopped the injection, when
5090    /// known.
5091    pub(crate) replacing: Option<i32>,
5092    /// How it would be lost.
5093    pub(crate) loss: HeldSignalLoss,
5094}
5095
5096/// A signal's name, such as `SIGCHLD`, or its number for a real-time signal.
5097fn signal_label(signal: Option<i32>) -> String {
5098    match signal {
5099        Some(signal) => match nix::sys::signal::Signal::try_from(signal) {
5100            Ok(named) => named.as_str().to_string(),
5101            Err(_) => format!("signal {signal}"),
5102        },
5103        None => "a signal that could not be identified".to_string(),
5104    }
5105}
5106
5107impl std::fmt::Display for HeldSignalRefusal {
5108    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
5109        let wait = self
5110            .wait
5111            .map_or_else(|| "a blocking".to_string(), |sysno| sysno.to_string());
5112        let held = match self.held {
5113            Some(_) => format!("the held signal {}", signal_label(self.held)),
5114            None => "a held signal that could not be identified".to_string(),
5115        };
5116        let replacing = signal_label(self.replacing);
5117        match self.loss {
5118            HeldSignalLoss::Replaced => write!(
5119                f,
5120                "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot keep {held}: the pending {replacing} \
5121                 would stop the next injection and replace it"
5122            )?,
5123            HeldSignalLoss::UnidentifiedStop => write!(
5124                f,
5125                "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot keep {held}: a signal stop that /proc \
5126                 cannot identify replaced it"
5127            )?,
5128            HeldSignalLoss::StopBound => write!(
5129                f,
5130                "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot keep {held}: the wait absorbed the \
5131                 maximum number of signal stops"
5132            )?,
5133            HeldSignalLoss::Consumed => {
5134                write!(
5135                    f,
5136                    "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot return {replacing}, which it consumes: \
5137                     the signal stopped an injection, so the backend would deliver it instead"
5138                )?;
5139                if self.held.is_some() {
5140                    write!(f, ", in place of {held}")?;
5141                }
5142            }
5143            HeldSignalLoss::Restoration => write!(
5144                f,
5145                "unsupported: the {wait} wait cannot keep {held}: {replacing} stopped the \
5146                 injection that puts the guest's signal mask back and replaced it"
5147            )?,
5148        }
5149        write!(
5150            f,
5151            " (scope reduction of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361; rerun with \
5152             --allow-unsupported-syscalls to restart the call instead)"
5153        )
5154    }
5155}
5156
5157impl std::error::Error for HeldSignalRefusal {}
5158
5159/// What a signal that stopped one of a wait's injections means for the wait.
5160#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
5161enum StopVerdict {
5162    /// The wait goes on; the backend holds the signal.
5163    Absorb(HeldKind),
5164    /// The wait ends with this errno.
5165    End(Errno),
5166}
5167
5168/// The first real-time signal number in the kernel. A standard signal below it
5169/// is pending at most once; a second one sent while it is pending is merged.
5170const KERNEL_SIGRTMIN: i32 = 32;
5171
5172impl KernelSignalWait {
5173    pub(crate) fn new<T, G>(
5174        guest: &G,
5175        consumed: KernelSigset,
5176        defers_default_stops: bool,
5177        restart_errno: Errno,
5178    ) -> Self
5179    where
5180        T: RecordOrReplay,
5181        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5182    {
5183        Self {
5184            pid: guest.pid(),
5185            tid: guest.tid(),
5186            consumed,
5187            defers_default_stops,
5188            restart_errno,
5189            held_until_return: kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD),
5190            deadline: false,
5191            saved_mask: None,
5192            unblockable: false,
5193            blocked_in_place: false,
5194            held: None,
5195            held_unidentified: false,
5196            host_timed: 0,
5197            committed: 0,
5198            private: 0,
5199            wait_mask: None,
5200        }
5201    }
5202
5203    /// This wait, with a finite deadline when `deadline` is set (the `deadline`
5204    /// field): no fallback of `inject_absorbing` then ends it with
5205    /// `ERESTARTNOINTR`, which would start the guest's timeout again.
5206    pub(crate) fn with_deadline(self, deadline: bool) -> Self {
5207        Self { deadline, ..self }
5208    }
5209
5210    /// The wait of `select` and of `pselect6`, which holds no signal until the
5211    /// call returns (`held_until_return` is empty); a `pselect6` with a
5212    /// temporary mask adds it with `with_wait_mask`:
5213    /// any pending signal that could interrupt it ends it, `SIGCHLD` included.
5214    ///
5215    /// Linux ends these calls with `ERESTARTNOHAND` whenever no descriptor is
5216    /// ready and a signal is pending (`core_sys_select`), so a caught `SIGCHLD`
5217    /// ends them whoever sent it. Detcore's select and pselect6 waits did the
5218    /// same before this machinery existed: their probes ran under the guest's
5219    /// own mask, and a pending caught signal stopped one.
5220    ///
5221    /// This is a known gap that these waits had before, and it is left as it
5222    /// was: the `SIGCHLD` the kernel posts for a child's exit, stop or continue
5223    /// ends the wait at the first turn whose read sees it, and host timing
5224    /// decides which turn that is (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
5225    /// Every other wait holds `SIGCHLD` until it returns, unless the scheduler
5226    /// commits it to the thread in that turn (`admit`).
5227    pub(crate) fn for_select<T, G>(guest: &G) -> Self
5228    where
5229        T: RecordOrReplay,
5230        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5231    {
5232        Self {
5233            held_until_return: 0,
5234            ..Self::new(guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND)
5235        }
5236    }
5237
5238    /// This wait, sleeping under `mask` instead of the guest's own (`wait_mask`):
5239    /// a `pselect6` with a temporary mask. Linux installs that mask for the
5240    /// whole call, so a signal it blocks never ends the call, even one the
5241    /// guest's own mask leaves unblocked, and one it leaves unblocked ends the
5242    /// call although the guest's own mask blocks it.
5243    pub(crate) fn with_wait_mask(self, mask: Option<KernelSigset>) -> Self {
5244        Self {
5245            wait_mask: mask,
5246            ..self
5247        }
5248    }
5249
5250    /// The mask Linux's `blocked` holds for the waiting thread when the
5251    /// kernel's `SigBlk` does not show it: the wait's temporary mask
5252    /// (`wait_mask`), or else the guest's own mask once `block` has replaced
5253    /// it (`saved_mask`). `None` while `SigBlk` is the guest's own mask.
5254    pub(crate) fn effective_mask(&self) -> Option<KernelSigset> {
5255        self.wait_mask.or(self.saved_mask)
5256    }
5257
5258    /// Whether the backend holds a signal from a stop of one of this wait's
5259    /// injections (`held`, `held_unidentified`), which it delivers when the
5260    /// guest resumes.
5261    pub(crate) fn holds_signal(&self) -> bool {
5262        self.held.is_some() || self.held_unidentified
5263    }
5264
5265    /// Whether a signal that ends the wait, pending in the kernel per `state`,
5266    /// is one the guest's own mask blocks: it ends the wait only because the
5267    /// wait mask (`with_wait_mask`) leaves it unblocked, and it stays pending
5268    /// when the guest's own mask is put back. A signal the wait holds until
5269    /// the call returns counts once the scheduler committed it in this turn
5270    /// (`admit`), as in `interrupted_with_state`: otherwise a
5271    /// committed `SIGCHLD` that only the wait mask lets in ended the call
5272    /// without its handler (Claude review of
5273    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4217).
5274    pub(crate) fn interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&self, state: &KernelSignalState) -> bool {
5275        let own_mask = self.saved_mask.unwrap_or(state.blocked);
5276        let held_until_return = self.held_until_return & !self.committed;
5277        let could_interrupt = self.could_interrupt(state);
5278        let interrupting = (state.pending & !held_until_return
5279            | state.thread_pending & self.private)
5280            & could_interrupt;
5281        self.wait_mask.is_some() && interrupting & own_mask != 0
5282    }
5283
5284    /// Adds `signals` to the ones this wait holds until the call returns
5285    /// (`held_until_return`). The gated loop passes, in each of its turns, the
5286    /// signals that a host-timed source armed by a guest can post to this
5287    /// process, such as a parent-death signal (`tool_global::host_timed_signals`):
5288    /// the kernel posts those at a moment set by host timing, so ending the wait
5289    /// for one would make the run depend on host timing. Never called for a
5290    /// `select` wait (`for_select`), which holds nothing.
5291    pub(crate) fn hold_until_return(&mut self, signals: KernelSigset) {
5292        self.held_until_return |= signals;
5293        self.host_timed |= signals;
5294    }
5295
5296    /// Sets the signals the scheduler committed to this thread in this turn
5297    /// (`committed`): its resume named them (`ResumeStatus::Signaled`). Such a
5298    /// signal was sent at a fixed point of the schedule, so a wait may end for
5299    /// it although the wait holds it, unless a host-timed source can post it
5300    /// too (`host_timed`). The loop passes a committed `SIGCHLD`, which the
5301    /// scheduler sends at a commit point (a child's child-exit timer, or a
5302    /// POSIX timer whose signal is `SIGCHLD`); the kernel's
5303    /// own copy of it, posted at a host-timed moment, decides nothing, since
5304    /// only the resume that names it lifts the hold, for that turn alone
5305    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
5306    ///
5307    /// `private` is the `SIGCHLD` a guest sent this thread, recorded in its
5308    /// private queue, that the turn admits (`admit_under_block`): it lifts the
5309    /// hold only against the thread's own queue, for this turn alone.
5310    pub(crate) fn admit(&mut self, committed: KernelSigset, private: KernelSigset) {
5311        self.committed = committed & !self.host_timed;
5312        self.private = private & !self.host_timed;
5313    }
5314
5315    /// The private `SIGCHLD` this turn admits (`admit`), from `recorded`, the
5316    /// schedule's record (`Scheduler::private_sigchld`). A turn that admits a
5317    /// `SIGCHLD`, committed or recorded, first blocks every blockable signal
5318    /// in place, before any injection of the turn, and publishes the guest's
5319    /// mask while it holds (`block_in_place`, `publish_wait_mask`). The
5320    /// recorded one is then kept only while that block holds (`saved_mask`;
5321    /// an earlier injected `block` that failed leaves none), and only if the
5322    /// thread's own queue holds `SIGCHLD`, read after the block: only this
5323    /// stopped thread can take it from there, and no injection can now. If
5324    /// the setter refuses, the wait keeps its fallback, the injected `block`
5325    /// after the first probe (rev4 1f), and holds the recorded `SIGCHLD` as
5326    /// before.
5327    pub(crate) async fn admit_under_block<T, G>(
5328        &mut self,
5329        guest: &mut G,
5330        committed: KernelSigset,
5331        recorded: KernelSigset,
5332        host_timed: KernelSigset,
5333        published: &mut PublishedWaitMask,
5334    ) -> Result<KernelSigset, Error>
5335    where
5336        T: RecordOrReplay,
5337        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5338    {
5339        if (committed | recorded) & !host_timed == 0 {
5340            return Ok(0);
5341        }
5342        if self.needs_block() {
5343            if self.block_in_place(guest, host_timed).await? {
5344                publish_wait_mask(guest, self.effective_mask(), published).await;
5345            } else {
5346                // Keep today's fallback for this wait.
5347                self.unblockable = false;
5348            }
5349        }
5350        if recorded == 0 || self.saved_mask.is_none() {
5351            return Ok(0);
5352        }
5353        let state = read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?;
5354        Ok(recorded & state.thread_pending)
5355    }
5356
5357    /// Whether, of the signals that end the wait per `state`, only signals the
5358    /// scheduler committed in this turn do (`admit`): without them
5359    /// the wait would go on.
5360    pub(crate) fn interrupts_only_by_committed(&self, state: &KernelSignalState) -> bool {
5361        let held = self.held.map_or(0, |held| kernel_sigset_bit(held.signal));
5362        let interrupting = (state.pending | held) & self.could_interrupt(state);
5363        (self.committed | self.private) != 0 && interrupting & !self.held_until_return == 0
5364    }
5365
5366    /// Whether the caller should still call `block`: it has neither blocked the
5367    /// guest's signals nor found that it cannot.
5368    pub(crate) fn needs_block(&self) -> bool {
5369        self.saved_mask.is_none() && !self.unblockable
5370    }
5371
5372    /// The signals that would end the wait natively under the guest's mask, given
5373    /// the kernel's `state`.
5374    /// The signals whose pending presence this wait would observe now: those
5375    /// it consumes, and those that would end it under the guest's mask, or
5376    /// the wait mask when it has one (`could_interrupt`). Read from the kernel's state in this turn.
5377    pub(crate) fn observable_now(&self) -> Result<KernelSigset, Error> {
5378        let state = read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?;
5379        Ok(self.consumed | self.could_interrupt(&state))
5380    }
5381
5382    fn could_interrupt(&self, state: &KernelSignalState) -> KernelSigset {
5383        let guest_mask = self.wait_mask.or(self.saved_mask).unwrap_or(state.blocked);
5384        state.interrupting_wait(guest_mask, self.defers_default_stops) & !self.consumed
5385    }
5386
5387    /// `interrupted_with_state` without the state, for the tests.
5388    #[cfg(test)]
5389    pub(crate) fn interrupted(&self) -> Result<bool, Error> {
5390        Ok(self.interrupted_with_state()?.0)
5391    }
5392
5393    /// Whether a signal that would end the wait natively is pending, in which case
