5394    /// the caller returns the call's restart errno, with the kernel's state that
5395    /// this read, which `inject_absorbing_after` takes as its first read in the same
5396    /// turn. The guest thread has been stopped inside the call since it was
5397    /// intercepted, so such a signal arrived while the call was waiting, and Linux
5398    /// returns the restart errno for that. Linux reports a source that was ready
5399    /// when the call began, or an argument error, before any pending signal, so
5400    /// `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state` runs its first probe before
5401    /// this check (`inject_first_probe`). There, a source that becomes ready in a
5402    /// later turn in which a signal is also pending is put behind the signal,
5403    /// because the turn cannot tell which came first. The waits of `select` and
5404    /// `pselect6` run every probe before this check, as Linux's do_select polls
5405    /// every descriptor on each pass before it tests for a pending signal. A
5406    /// signal the wait holds until the call returns (`held_until_return`) never
5407    /// counts. A signal that the backend holds since `inject_absorbing` absorbed
5408    /// it counts as pending. A failed read is never returned as the call's errno
5409    /// (`read_wait_signal_state`).
5410    pub(crate) fn interrupted_with_state(&self) -> Result<(bool, KernelSignalState), Error> {
5411        let state = read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?;
5412        let could_interrupt = self.could_interrupt(&state);
5413        let held = self.held.map_or(0, |held| kernel_sigset_bit(held.signal));
5414        let held_until_return = self.held_until_return & !self.committed;
5415        // An admitted private `SIGCHLD` counts against the thread's own queue
5416        // only (`admit`).
5417        let interrupting = ((state.pending | held) & !held_until_return
5418            | state.thread_pending & self.private)
5419            & could_interrupt;
5420        if interrupting != 0 {
5421            tracing::trace!(
5422                "[tid {}] pending signals {:#x} interrupt a blocking wait",
5423                self.tid,
5424                interrupting
5425            );
5426        }
5427        Ok((interrupting != 0, state))
5428    }
5429
5430    /// Inject `call`, a probe or a mask change, absorbing the signal stops that do
5431    /// not end the wait. `Ok` carries the call's own result; `Err` ends the wait.
5432    ///
5433    /// A signal that stops the guest around an injection is dequeued from the
5434    /// kernel and held by the backend, which delivers it when the guest resumes,
5435    /// and the injection returns a restart errno instead of the call's result.
5436    /// The backend does not say which signal it holds, so the kernel's state is
5437    /// read before each injection (in a polling turn of
5438    /// `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state` under the full mask, the
5439    /// turn's own read: `inject_absorbing_after`), which names the signal the
5440    /// kernel dequeues next (`KernelSignalState::next_dequeued`), and again
5441    /// after a stop. The stop is identified only if exactly that signal left its queue
5442    /// and the mask and dispositions did not change; it then decides:
5443    ///
5444    /// - A signal the wait consumes (`consumed`) is delivered rather than
5445    ///   consumed. In a wait without a deadline it ends the wait with
5446    ///   `ERESTARTNOINTR`, and the call runs again, unless the wait holds it
5447    ///   until the call returns (`held_until_return`), so that its delivery now
5448    ///   could follow host timing: then the wait ends with a
5449    ///   [`HeldSignalRefusal`]. In a wait with a deadline (`deadline`) it is
5450    ///   classified as if the wait did not consume it, by the rules below.
5451    /// - A signal that would end the wait natively ends it with the restart
5452    ///   errno, except a signal the wait holds until the call returns
5453    ///   (`held_until_return`), which is held.
5454    /// - Any other `SIGCHLD`, and a default job-control stop that the wait
5455    ///   defers, are held, and so are an ignored signal and a default-ignored
5456    ///   one. The injection runs again.
5457    /// - A signal that the wait mask (`with_wait_mask`) blocks is held: Linux
5458    ///   keeps it pending until the call returns.
5459    /// - Anything else, which is the backend's own preemption signal, ends the
5460    ///   wait with `ERESTARTNOINTR`, or is held in a wait with a deadline.
5461    ///
5462    /// A pending signal that would end the wait ends it before the injection,
5463    /// with the restart errno, so it is never held, except by a probe made by
5464    /// `inject_first_probe`: the first probe of a wait, and every probe of the
5465    /// waits of `select` and `pselect6`. A stop that cannot be identified, by a
5466    /// signal that arrived after the read, does not end the wait while the
5467    /// backend held nothing whose loss matters: the backend holds that signal
5468    /// in place of any held one and the injection runs again, as the blind
5469    /// retry before this machinery did, so the wait keeps its deadline and
5470    /// every check that ends it. Which signal it was would need the backend to
5471    /// say, so it is recorded only as unidentified (`held_unidentified`), and
5472    /// it is delivered as the call returns.
5473    ///
5474    /// The backend has one slot for a held signal, and a stop replaces what it
5475    /// holds. A held signal whose loss matters (`HeldKind::Precious`), or one
5476    /// that could not be identified and so may matter, is never given up for a
5477    /// result that reads as success, with or without a deadline:
5478    ///
5479    /// - An injection that another pending signal would stop is not made. If
5480    ///   the held signal would end the wait natively, the wait ends with the
5481    ///   restart errno, as Linux ends it for that signal; otherwise it ends
5482    ///   with a `HeldSignalRefusal`. The same standard signal on the same queue
5483    ///   is the exception, because Linux merges the two.
5484    /// - A stop that cannot be identified, which has already replaced such a
5485    ///   signal, ends the wait with a `HeldSignalRefusal`.
5486    /// - After `MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS` absorbed stops, a wait without a deadline
5487    ///   ends with a `HeldSignalRefusal`, or with `ERESTARTNOINTR` when the
5488    ///   backend holds nothing whose loss matters. A wait with a deadline,
5489    ///   whose restart would start the guest's timeout again, absorbs stops
5490    ///   without a bound.
5491    ///
5492    /// Each refusal is a scope reduction. It replaces a transparent
5493    /// `ERESTARTNOINTR` restart, or, in a wait with a deadline, an injection
5494    /// that went on and let a stop replace the held signal (round-10 High 1 on
5495    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361): the restart made the
5496    /// backend deliver the held signal before the wait completed, at a moment
5497    /// host timing could set. A complete successful repair preserving signal
5498    /// information needs additional framework support with the current generic
5499    /// API. A Detcore-only refusal or capability withdrawal can prevent the
5500    /// determinism regression.
5501    ///
5502    /// In a probe made by `inject_first_probe` that two pending signals would
5503    /// stop in turn, the first of which would end the wait, the wait ends with
5504    /// the restart errno before the probe has run, so a ready source, or an
5505    /// argument error, is reported behind the signal: the order compromise that
5506    /// a later turn of `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state` already
5507    /// makes (`interrupted_with_state`).
5508    pub(crate) async fn inject_absorbing<T, G, S>(
5509        &mut self,
5510        guest: &mut G,
5511        call: S,
5512    ) -> Result<Result<i64, Errno>, Error>
5513    where
5514        T: RecordOrReplay,
5515        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5516        S: SyscallInfo,
5517    {
5518        self.inject_absorbing_from(guest, call, None, false).await
5519    }
5520
5521    /// The first probe of a wait, and every probe of the waits of `select` and
5522    /// `pselect6`, which runs before the turn's `interrupted_with_state` check:
5523    /// `inject_absorbing`, except that a signal that would end the wait neither
5524    /// ends it before the injection nor when it stops the injection.
5525    ///
5526    /// Linux reports a descriptor that is ready when the call begins, a queued
5527    /// event, and an argument error before it looks at pending signals:
5528    /// `do_poll` tests `signal_pending` only when no descriptor is ready, and so
5529    /// does `core_sys_select`, whose `max_select_fd` first returns `EBADF` for a
5530    /// descriptor in the sets that is not open; `ep_poll` sends queued events
5531    /// before it tests it, `do_epoll_wait` rejects a bad descriptor or
5532    /// `maxevents` first, and `do_sigtimedwait` copies its set first. So the
5533    /// probe runs even when such a signal is pending. `do_select` also polls
5534    /// every descriptor on each pass before it tests `signal_pending`, so the
5535    /// waits of `select` and `pselect6` make every probe this way; once `block`
5536    /// has blocked every blockable signal, a pending one cannot stop a probe
5537    /// there, and the check that follows a probe that would block counts it.
5538    /// A pending signal that the guest does not block stops the injection
5539    /// before the probe runs; when the stop is identified, the signal is held
5540    /// as a precious one (`HeldKind::Precious`) and the probe runs again, so
5541    /// its result stands, and the backend delivers the signal as the call
5542    /// returns. If the probe would block, the caller's check that follows
5543    /// counts the held signal (`interrupted_with_state`) and ends the wait with
5544    /// the restart errno. A stop that cannot be identified is held, as
5545    /// `inject_absorbing` describes.
5546    pub(crate) async fn inject_first_probe<T, G, S>(
5547        &mut self,
5548        guest: &mut G,
5549        call: S,
5550    ) -> Result<Result<i64, Errno>, Error>
5551    where
5552        T: RecordOrReplay,
5553        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5554        S: SyscallInfo,
5555    {
5556        self.inject_absorbing_from(guest, call, None, true).await
5557    }
5558
5559    /// `inject_absorbing` in a turn whose `interrupted_with_state` read `state`
5560    /// and found no signal that ends the wait.
5561    ///
5562    /// Once `block` has blocked every blockable signal (`saved_mask`), `state`
5563    /// serves as the first read before the injection, so a polling turn reads
5564    /// `/proc` once, as it did before injections absorbed stops. The caller must
5565    /// run nothing between the two that resumes the guest thread or changes its
5566    /// signal state. `retry_blocking_wait_with_kernel_signal_state`, which serves
5567    /// ppoll, poll, epoll_pwait, epoll_wait, rt_sigtimedwait and polling futex
5568    /// waits and is the only caller, runs nothing there. So between the two reads
5569    /// the guest thread stays stopped and only it can change its own mask, and
5570    /// with threads sequentialized no other guest thread runs in its turn, so a
5571    /// signal that arrives meanwhile arrives at a
5572    /// host-timed moment: sent from outside the guest, or posted by the kernel.
5573    /// A signal that the full mask blocks stays pending, cannot stop the
5574    /// injection, and is classified at the next turn's read, as one that arrives
5575    /// just after a fresh read is. One that the full mask leaves unblocked
5576    /// (`SIGKILL`, `SIGSTOP`, glibc's two reserved signals, `PERF_EVENT_SIGNAL`)
5577    /// and that stops the injection is not named by `state`, so the stop is not
5578    /// identified and is handled as a stop by a signal that arrives just after a
5579    /// fresh read is. `interrupted_with_state` found
5580    /// no signal in `state` that ends the wait, so the check before the injection
5581    /// does not end it either.
5582    ///
5583    /// Before `block` takes effect, or when it cannot, the probe runs under the
5584    /// guest's own mask and a fresh read is taken, so a signal that arrived
5585    /// after `state` is still identified or ends the wait before the injection.
5586    pub(crate) async fn inject_absorbing_after<T, G, S>(
5587        &mut self,
5588        guest: &mut G,
5589        call: S,
5590        state: KernelSignalState,
5591    ) -> Result<Result<i64, Errno>, Error>
5592    where
5593        T: RecordOrReplay,
5594        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5595        S: SyscallInfo,
5596    {
5597        let first = self.saved_mask.is_some().then_some(state);
5598        self.inject_absorbing_from(guest, call, first, false).await
5599    }
5600
5601    /// `inject_absorbing`, taking `first`, if any, as the state read before the
5602    /// first injection. For `first_probe`, a signal that would end the wait does
5603    /// not end it, and one that stops the injection is held
5604    /// (`inject_first_probe`).
5605    async fn inject_absorbing_from<T, G, S>(
5606        &mut self,
5607        guest: &mut G,
5608        call: S,
5609        mut first: Option<KernelSignalState>,
5610        first_probe: bool,
5611    ) -> Result<Result<i64, Errno>, Error>
5612    where
5613        T: RecordOrReplay,
5614        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5615        S: SyscallInfo,
5616    {
5617        // Each absorbed stop takes one signal off a kernel queue, so only signals
5618        // sent faster than the injections run can reach this. A wait with a
5619        // deadline has no bound, as the blind retry before this machinery had
5620        // none: ending it would start its timeout again (`deadline`).
5621        const MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS: usize = 64;
5622        let mut absorbed = 0;
5623        loop {
5624            let before = match first.take() {
5625                Some(state) => state,
5626                None => read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?,
5627            };
5628            let ends_wait = self.could_interrupt(&before) & !self.held_until_return;
5629            if !first_probe && before.pending & ends_wait != 0 {
5630                return Err(self.restart_errno.into());
5631            }
5632            let next = before.next_dequeued(before.blocked);
5633            if let Some((signal, queue)) = next
5634                && self.would_replace_precious(signal, queue)
5635            {
5636                if let Some(held) = self.held
5637                    && self.held_ends_wait(&before, held.signal)
5638                {
5639                    tracing::trace!(
5640                        "[tid {}] signal {} would replace the held signal {}, which ends the wait",
5641                        self.tid,
5642                        signal,
5643                        held.signal
5644                    );
5645                    return Err(held_signal_restart_errno(self.restart_errno, held.signal).into());
5646                }
5647                // Round-10 High 1 on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361:
5648                // this used to end a wait without a deadline with ERESTARTNOINTR,
5649                // and let a wait with one go on and lose the held signal.
5650                tracing::trace!(
5651                    "[tid {}] signal {} would replace the held signal {:?}; the wait is refused",
5652                    self.tid,
5653                    signal,
5654                    self.held
5655                );
5656                return Err(self.refusal(Some(signal), HeldSignalLoss::Replaced));
5657            }
5658            let result = guest.inject(call).await;
5659            let Err(errno) = result else {
5660                return Ok(result);
5661            };
5662            if !probe_was_interrupted_by_signal(errno) {
5663                return Ok(result);
5664            }
5665            let after = read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?;
5666            // A probe that carries the call's temporary mask, as a masked
5667            // ppoll's does (`with_wait_mask`), and that the kernel itself
5668            // ended, for a pending signal the mask lets in, leaves that mask
5669            // installed with its restore pending until the signal is delivered
5670            // as the guest resumes, so `/proc` reports a mask other than the one
5671            // before the injection. That ERESTARTNOHAND is the call's own
5672            // result, not a stop, and no injection may follow it: a repeated
5673            // probe would save the temporary mask as the guest's
5674            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1003). A pselect6
5675            // wait's probes carry no mask, so this never holds for one.
5676            if self.wait_mask.is_some()
5677                && errno == Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
5678                && after.blocked != before.blocked
5679            {
5680                return Ok(result);
5681            }
5682            let identified =
5683                next.filter(|&(signal, queue)| stop_took_only(&before, &after, signal, queue));
5684            let Some((signal, queue)) = identified else {
5685                // A signal that `before` did not show stopped the injection. The
5686                // backend holds it in place of any held one and delivers it when
5687                // the guest resumes, but `/proc` cannot name it. If the backend
5688                // held a signal whose loss matters, or one it could not identify
5689                // either, that signal is gone, and the wait is refused. Otherwise
5690                // the wait goes on and the injection runs again, as the blind
5691                // retry before this machinery did, so the wait keeps its
5692                // deadline; the signals that `/proc` still shows are classified
5693                // as before, and every check that ends the wait still runs at
5694                // the read before the injection and at each turn's
5695                // `interrupted_with_state`.
5696                if self.holds_precious() {
5697                    tracing::trace!(
5698                        "[tid {}] a signal stop that cannot be identified replaced the held signal {:?}; the wait is refused",
5699                        self.tid,
5700                        self.held
5701                    );
5702                    return Err(self.refusal(None, HeldSignalLoss::UnidentifiedStop));
5703                }
5704                if !self.deadline && absorbed >= MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS {
5705                    // The backend now holds the unidentified signal.
5706                    self.held = None;
5707                    self.held_unidentified = true;
5708                    return Err(self.refusal(None, HeldSignalLoss::StopBound));
5709                }
5710                absorbed += 1;
5711                tracing::trace!(
5712                    "[tid {}] a signal stop that cannot be identified is held; the injection runs again",
5713                    self.tid
5714                );
5715                self.held = None;
5716                self.held_unidentified = true;
5717                continue;
5718            };
5719            let bit = kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
5720            let verdict = match self.stop_verdict(&before, signal) {
5721                // A probe made by `inject_first_probe` holds a signal that would
5722                // end the wait and runs again.
5723                StopVerdict::End(_)
5724                    if first_probe
5725                        && self.consumed & bit == 0
5726                        && self.could_interrupt(&before) & bit != 0 =>
5727                {
5728                    StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious)
5729                }
5730                verdict => verdict,
5731            };
5732            match verdict {
5733                StopVerdict::Absorb(kind) => {
5734                    let kind = self.held.map_or(kind, |held| held.kind.max(kind));
5735                    let unidentified = self.held_unidentified;
5736                    self.held = Some(HeldSignal {
5737                        signal,
5738                        queue,
5739                        kind,
5740                    });
5741                    self.held_unidentified = false;
5742                    if !self.deadline && absorbed >= MAX_ABSORBED_STOPS {
5743                        if kind == HeldKind::Precious || unidentified {
5744                            return Err(self.refusal(None, HeldSignalLoss::StopBound));
5745                        }
5746                        return Err(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR.into());
5747                    }
5748                    absorbed += 1;
5749                    tracing::trace!(
5750                        "[tid {}] signal {} stopped an injection and is held ({:?})",
5751                        self.tid,
5752                        signal,
5753                        kind
5754                    );
5755                }
5756                // A signal that a wait without a deadline consumes, delivered
5757                // rather than returned: refused when the wait holds it until the
5758                // call returns, or when it replaced a held signal whose loss
5759                // matters, and otherwise ended with ERESTARTNOINTR (stop_verdict).
5760                StopVerdict::End(_)
5761                    if !self.deadline
5762                        && self.consumed & bit != 0
5763                        && (self.held_until_return & bit != 0 || self.holds_precious()) =>
5764                {
5765                    tracing::trace!(
5766                        "[tid {}] consumed signal {} stopped an injection; the wait is refused",
5767                        self.tid,
5768                        signal
5769                    );
5770                    return Err(self.refusal(Some(signal), HeldSignalLoss::Consumed));
5771                }
5772                // The backend holds `signal`, which stopped the injection.
5773                StopVerdict::End(errno) => {
5774                    return Err(held_signal_restart_errno(errno, signal).into());
5775                }
5776            }
5777        }
5778    }
5779
5780    /// What a stop by `signal` means for the wait, given the kernel's state
5781    /// `before` the injection (see `inject_absorbing`).
5782    fn stop_verdict(&self, before: &KernelSignalState, signal: i32) -> StopVerdict {
5783        let bit = kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
5784        let interrupts = if self.consumed & bit != 0 {
5785            if !self.deadline {
5786                return StopVerdict::End(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR);
5787            }
5788            // The backend delivers the signal rather than the wait consuming it,
5789            // as Linux does for one the guest does not block, so it is classified
5790            // as if the wait did not consume it.
5791            let guest_mask = self.wait_mask.or(self.saved_mask).unwrap_or(before.blocked);
5792            before.interrupting_wait(guest_mask, self.defers_default_stops) & bit != 0
5793        } else {
5794            self.could_interrupt(before) & bit != 0
5795        };
5796        if interrupts {
5797            return if self.held_until_return & bit != 0 {
5798                StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious)
5799            } else {
5800                StopVerdict::End(self.restart_errno)
5801            };
5802        }
5803        if signal == libc::SIGCHLD
5804            || (self.defers_default_stops && before.default_job_control_stops() & bit != 0)
5805        {
5806            return StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious);
5807        }
5808        let default_ignored = [libc::SIGCONT, libc::SIGURG, libc::SIGWINCH]
5809            .into_iter()
5810            .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_sigset_bit(signal));
5811        if (before.ignored | (default_ignored & !before.caught)) & bit != 0 {
5812            return StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Harmless);
5813        }
5814        // A signal that the wait mask blocks, and the guest's own mask does
5815        // not, can stop an injection that runs before `block` takes effect.
5816        // Linux keeps it pending for the whole call, under the temporary mask,
5817        // and delivers it as the call returns, so it is held and never ends
5818        // the wait (review of
5819        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4051).
5820        if self.deadline || self.wait_mask.is_some_and(|mask| mask & bit != 0) {
5821            StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious)
5822        } else {
5823            StopVerdict::End(Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR)
5824        }
5825    }
5826
5827    /// Whether an injection that `signal`, pending on `queue`, stops would make
5828    /// the backend drop a held signal whose delivery matters
5829    /// (`HeldKind::Precious`), or one it could not identify, which may matter
5830    /// (`held_unidentified`). Linux merges a standard signal into the same one
5831    /// pending on the same queue, so that one replaces nothing.
5832    fn would_replace_precious(&self, signal: i32, queue: SignalQueue) -> bool {
5833        self.held_unidentified
5834            || self.held.is_some_and(|held| {
5835                held.kind == HeldKind::Precious
5836                    && !(signal == held.signal && queue == held.queue && signal < KERNEL_SIGRTMIN)
5837            })
5838    }
5839
5840    /// Whether the backend holds a signal whose loss matters
5841    /// (`HeldKind::Precious`), or one it could not identify, which may matter.
5842    fn holds_precious(&self) -> bool {
5843        self.held_unidentified
5844            || self
5845                .held
5846                .is_some_and(|held| held.kind == HeldKind::Precious)
5847    }
5848
5849    /// The `HeldSignalRefusal` that ends the wait, naming the signal the backend
5850    /// holds, if known, and `replacing`, the one that would replace it or that
5851    /// stopped the injection.
5852    fn refusal(&self, replacing: Option<i32>, loss: HeldSignalLoss) -> Error {
5853        Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(HeldSignalRefusal {
5854            wait: None,
5855            held: self.held.map(|held| held.signal),
5856            replacing,
5857            loss,
5858        }))
5859    }
5860
5861    /// Whether a held `signal` would end the wait natively, given the kernel's
5862    /// state `before` an injection: it could interrupt the wait, and the wait
5863    /// does not hold it until the call returns (`held_until_return`).
5864    fn held_ends_wait(&self, before: &KernelSignalState, signal: i32) -> bool {
5865        self.could_interrupt(before) & !self.held_until_return & kernel_sigset_bit(signal) != 0
5866    }
5867
5868    /// Block every blockable signal for the rest of the wait, and keep blocked the
5869    /// signals the guest blocks itself, which the blockable set leaves out (the C
5870    /// library's reserved signals). `scratch` is a guest cell for the mask when
5871    /// the caller holds the only scratch-stack guard; otherwise a fresh guard is
5872    /// taken. The change goes through `inject_absorbing`, so a signal that stops
5873    /// it is handled as one that stops a probe. If that ends the wait, the guest's
5874    /// mask is still recorded, and the caller's final `restore` reads the
5875    /// kernel's mask and puts the guest's back if the change took effect.
5876    ///
5877    /// If the mask cannot be changed for another reason, the guest's mask is
5878    /// unchanged and no wait call can return that error, so the wait continues
5879    /// with every probe under the guest's own mask, as the first probe runs, and
5880    /// `block` is not tried again (`needs_block`). `interrupted_with_state` reads
5881    /// that mask from the kernel each turn. The scratch-stack commit fails this
5882    /// way on a guest stack with no room below its stack pointer
5883    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3328); poll and epoll_wait
5884    /// probes need no scratch of their own, so for them this is the first need.
5885    pub(crate) async fn block<'a, T, G>(
5886        &mut self,
5887        guest: &mut G,
5888        scratch: Option<AddrMut<'a, KernelSigset>>,
5889    ) -> Result<(), Error>
5890    where
5891        T: RecordOrReplay,
5892        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5893    {
5894        let guest_mask = read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?.blocked;
5895        let mask = blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask;
5896        let result = match scratch {
5897            Some(cell) => match guest.memory().write_value(cell, &mask) {
5898                Ok(()) => {
5899                    self.inject_absorbing(guest, set_signal_mask_call(cell.into()))
5900                        .await
5901                }
5902                Err(errno) => Ok(Err(errno)),
5903            },
5904            None => {
5905                let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
5906                let cell = stack.push(mask);
5907                match stack.commit() {
5908                    Ok(_guard) => {
5909                        self.inject_absorbing(guest, set_signal_mask_call(cell))
5910                            .await
5911                    }
5912                    Err(_) => Ok(Err(Errno::EFAULT)),
5913                }
5914            }
5915        };
5916        match result {
5917            Ok(Ok(_)) => {
5918                self.saved_mask = Some(guest_mask);
5919                Ok(())
5920            }
5921            Ok(Err(errno)) => {
5922                tracing::debug!(
5923                    "[tid {}] cannot block signals for a wait ({}); its probes run under the \
5924                     guest's mask",
5925                    self.tid,
5926                    errno
5927                );
5928                self.unblockable = true;
5929                Ok(())
5930            }
5931            Err(error) => {
5932                self.saved_mask = Some(guest_mask);
5933                Err(error)
5934            }
5935        }
5936    }
5937
5938    /// Block every blockable signal for the rest of the wait, as `block` does,
5939    /// but through `Guest::set_blocked_signals`: no guest code runs, so no
5940    /// pending signal is taken from the kernel's queues, and every one stays
5941    /// there for the kernel to deliver, in its own order, once `restore` puts
5942    /// the guest's mask back. `block` instead injects `rt_sigprocmask`, which a
5943    /// pending signal can stop before it runs, moving that signal into the
5944    /// backend's single held slot, where a second one replaces it
5945    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, stage 2). No scratch
5946    /// memory is needed, here or in `restore` (the Claude review of the R2b-2
5947    /// design, M1).
5948    ///
5949    /// `host_timed` is the turn's host-timed signals, held until the call
5950    /// returns as `hold_until_return` holds them.
5951    ///
5952    /// Returns whether the mask is now blocked. A refusal changes nothing
5953    /// (`MaskChangeRefused::Unsupported`, `RestorePending`), and neither does a
5954    /// failure that put the old mask back, so the wait goes on under the
5955    /// guest's own mask, as before this existed. A failure that leaves the mask
5956    /// unknown ends the run before the guest resumes
5957    /// ([`BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored`]).
5958    pub(crate) async fn block_in_place<T, G>(
5959        &mut self,
5960        guest: &mut G,
5961        host_timed: KernelSigset,
5962    ) -> Result<bool, Error>
5963    where
5964        T: RecordOrReplay,
5965        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
5966    {
5967        // As `install_turn_mask` does for `writev`: the signals a host-timed
5968        // source can post (`host_timed`) are held until the call returns, so a
5969        // fallback injected restoration holds one that stops it
5970        // (`absorb_restoration_stop`) rather than counting it lost.
5971        self.hold_until_return(host_timed);
5972        let guest_mask = read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?.blocked;
5973        match guest
5974            .set_blocked_signals(blocked_signal_mask() | guest_mask)
5975            .await
5976        {
5977            Ok(old) => {
5978                self.saved_mask = Some(old);
5979                self.blocked_in_place = true;
5980                Ok(true)
5981            }
5982            Err(MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
5983                errno,
5984                mask_unknown: true,
5985            }) => Err(self.mask_not_restored(1, Some(errno))),
5986            Err(refused) => {
5987                tracing::debug!(
5988                    "[tid {}] cannot block signals in place for a wait ({}); its attempts run \
5989                     under the guest's mask",
5990                    self.tid,
5991                    refused
5992                );
5993                // Not tried again for this wait (`needs_block`).
5994                self.unblockable = true;
5995                Ok(false)
5996            }
5997        }
5998    }
5999
6000    /// The error that ends the run when the guest's mask cannot be put back.
6001    fn mask_not_restored(&self, attempts: usize, last_error: Option<Errno>) -> Error {
6002        Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(
6003            BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored {
6004                pid: self.pid,
6005                tid: self.tid,
6006                attempts,
6007                last_error,
6008            },
6009        ))
6010    }
6011
6012    /// Put back the guest's mask, if `block` replaced it. A signal can stop the guest
6013    /// around the call, before or after it takes effect, so success is read back
6014    /// from the kernel and the call is repeated until the kernel reports the
6015    /// guest's mask. The guest never resumes with every signal blocked: if the
6016    /// mask cannot be put back, the run ends with
6017    /// [`BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored`].
6018    ///
6019    /// The backend holds the signal that stops one of these injections, in place
6020    /// of any it held, as it does for a probe (`inject_absorbing`). Each such
6021    /// stop is recorded from the read before the injection and the read after it
6022    /// (`absorb_restoration_stop`). If one replaced a held signal whose loss
6023    /// matters, or one that could not be identified, the mask is still put back
6024    /// and then the first such loss is returned as a [`HeldSignalRefusal`]
6025    /// (`HeldSignalLoss::Restoration`), which the caller turns into the wait's
6026    /// result (`result_after_restore`). Round-11 High F1 on
6027    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361: these stops used to be
6028    /// retried without that check, so the held signal was lost silently.
6029    pub(crate) async fn restore<'a, T, G>(
6030        &mut self,
6031        guest: &mut G,
6032        scratch: Option<AddrMut<'a, KernelSigset>>,
6033    ) -> Result<(), Error>
6034    where
6035        T: RecordOrReplay,
6036        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6037    {
6038        let Some(guest_mask) = self.saved_mask else {
6039            return Ok(());
6040        };
6041        // A mask `block_in_place` installed goes back the same way, with no
6042        // injection, so no signal can stop the restoration and none is held.
6043        // That call is refused under the same rules as the block; a refusal
6044        // or a failure that left the mask as it was falls back to the
6045        // injected restoration below, which needs scratch memory (the Codex
6046        // and Claude reviews of https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/1083,
6047        // F4).
6048        if std::mem::take(&mut self.blocked_in_place) {
6049            match guest.set_blocked_signals(guest_mask).await {
6050                Ok(_) | Err(MaskChangeRefused::Gone) => {
6051                    self.saved_mask = None;
6052                    return Ok(());
6053                }
6054                Err(MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
6055                    errno,
6056                    mask_unknown: true,
6057                }) => {
6058                    self.saved_mask = None;
6059                    return Err(self.mask_not_restored(1, Some(errno)));
6060                }
6061                Err(refused) => {
6062                    tracing::debug!(
6063                        "[tid {}] cannot restore the mask in place ({}); injecting it",
6064                        self.tid,
6065                        refused
6066                    );
6067                }
6068            }
6069        }
6070        // `stop_verdict` reads the guest's mask from `saved_mask`, so it is cleared
6071        // only once the restoration has ended.
6072        let restored = self.restore_mask(guest, guest_mask, scratch).await;
6073        self.saved_mask = None;
6074        restored
6075    }
6076
6077    /// `restore`, for a wait whose guest mask is `guest_mask`.
6078    async fn restore_mask<'a, T, G>(
6079        &mut self,
6080        guest: &mut G,
6081        guest_mask: KernelSigset,
6082        scratch: Option<AddrMut<'a, KernelSigset>>,
6083    ) -> Result<(), Error>
6084    where
6085        T: RecordOrReplay,
6086        G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6087    {
6088        // Under the all-blocked mask only a signal that cannot be blocked (SIGKILL,
6089        // SIGSTOP) can stop the call before it takes effect, and each such stop needs
6090        // another signal sent, so a bound this large is never reached in practice.
6091        const ATTEMPTS: usize = 16;
6092        let mut attempts = 0;
6093        let mut last_error = None;
6094        // The kernel's state before an injection that a signal stopped, until the
6095        // next read records the stop.
6096        let mut stopped = None;
6097        // The first held signal that a stop replaced, as the refusal to return once
6098        // the mask is back.
6099        let mut loss = None;
6100        while attempts < ATTEMPTS {
6101            let state = read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?;
6102            if let Some(before) = stopped.take() {
6103                let replaced = self.absorb_restoration_stop(&before, &state);
6104                loss = loss.or(replaced);
6105            }
6106            if state.blocked == guest_mask {
6107                return loss.map_or(Ok(()), Err);
6108            }
6109            attempts += 1;
6110            match inject_signal_mask(guest, guest_mask, scratch).await {
6111                Ok(()) => return loss.map_or(Ok(()), Err),
6112                // Stopped by a signal: the next read records the stop and decides
6113                // whether the mask took effect.
6114                Err(errno) if probe_was_interrupted_by_signal(errno) => {
6115                    last_error = Some(errno);
6116                    stopped = Some(state);
6117                }
6118                // The call could not run, so the mask is unchanged.
6119                Err(errno) => {
6120                    last_error = Some(errno);
6121                    break;
6122                }
6123            }
6124        }
6125        let state = read_wait_signal_state(self.pid, self.tid)?;
6126        if let Some(before) = stopped.take() {
6127            let replaced = self.absorb_restoration_stop(&before, &state);
6128            loss = loss.or(replaced);
6129        }
6130        if state.blocked == guest_mask {
6131            return loss.map_or(Ok(()), Err);
6132        }
6133        Err(Error::Tool(anyhow::Error::new(
6134            BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored {
6135                pid: self.pid,
6136                tid: self.tid,
6137                attempts,
6138                last_error,
6139            },
6140        )))
6141    }
6142
6143    /// Record a signal stop of an injection of `restore`, given the kernel's state
6144    /// `before` the injection and `after` it, as `inject_absorbing` records a stop
6145    /// of a probe: the backend holds the signal that stopped it in place of any it
6146    /// held. Returns the `HeldSignalRefusal` when that replaced a held signal
6147    /// whose loss matters, or one that could not be identified
6148    /// (`would_replace_precious`, `holds_precious`), naming the held signal as it
6149    /// was before the stop.
6150    ///
6151    /// A stop is identified only when exactly the signal that the kernel would
6152    /// take next under the mask `before` left its queue and the mask did not
6153    /// change (`stop_took_only`); a stop after which the mask took effect, or one
6154    /// that `before` did not show, is recorded as unidentified. The call's result
6155    /// is already decided, so a signal that would have ended the wait is kept as
6156    /// one whose delivery matters.
6157    fn absorb_restoration_stop(
6158        &mut self,
6159        before: &KernelSignalState,
6160        after: &KernelSignalState,
6161    ) -> Option<Error> {
6162        let identified = before
6163            .next_dequeued(before.blocked)
6164            .filter(|&(signal, queue)| stop_took_only(before, after, signal, queue));
6165        let Some((signal, queue)) = identified else {
6166            let loss = self
6167                .holds_precious()
6168                .then(|| self.refusal(None, HeldSignalLoss::Restoration));
6169            tracing::trace!(
6170                "[tid {}] a signal stop that cannot be identified stopped the mask restoration; it replaced the held signal {:?}",
6171                self.tid,
6172                self.held
6173            );
6174            self.held = None;
6175            self.held_unidentified = true;
6176            return loss;
6177        };
6178        let loss = self
6179            .would_replace_precious(signal, queue)
6180            .then(|| self.refusal(Some(signal), HeldSignalLoss::Restoration));
6181        let kind = match self.stop_verdict(before, signal) {
6182            StopVerdict::Absorb(kind) => kind,
6183            StopVerdict::End(_) => HeldKind::Precious,
6184        };
6185        let kind = self.held.map_or(kind, |held| held.kind.max(kind));
6186        tracing::trace!(
6187            "[tid {}] signal {} stopped the mask restoration and is held ({:?}) in place of {:?}",
6188            self.tid,
6189            signal,
6190            kind,
6191            self.held
6192        );
6193        self.held = Some(HeldSignal {
6194            signal,
6195            queue,
6196            kind,
6197        });
6198        self.held_unidentified = false;
6199        loss
6200    }
6201}
6202
6203/// The wait's result once `restore` has put the guest's mask back. A
6204/// [`HeldSignalRefusal`] from the restoration (`HeldSignalLoss::Restoration`)
6205/// replaces `result`, as a loss during the wait does, unless `result` is
6206/// already such a refusal, which came first; the caller then applies the
6207/// unsupported-operation policy (`refuse_held_signal_loss`). Every other
6208/// restoration error, such as [`BlockedWaitSignalError::MaskNotRestored`], is
6209/// returned as the error that ends the run, as before.
6210pub(crate) fn result_after_restore(
6211    restored: Result<(), Error>,
6212    result: Result<i64, Error>,
6213) -> Result<Result<i64, Error>, Error> {
6214    let is_refusal =
6215        |error: &Error| matches!(error, Error::Tool(error) if error.is::<HeldSignalRefusal>());
6216    match restored {
6217        Ok(()) => Ok(result),
6218        Err(refusal) if is_refusal(&refusal) => match &result {
6219            Err(error) if is_refusal(error) => Ok(result),
6220            _ => Ok(Err(refusal)),
6221        },
6222        Err(error) => Err(error),
6223    }
6224}
6225
6226/// Replace the guest's signal mask with `mask`, written to `scratch` or, when the
6227/// caller holds no scratch-stack guard, to a fresh one.
6228async fn inject_signal_mask<'a, T, G>(
6229    guest: &mut G,
6230    mask: KernelSigset,
6231    scratch: Option<AddrMut<'a, KernelSigset>>,
6232) -> Result<(), Errno>
6233where
6234    T: RecordOrReplay,
6235    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6236{
6237    match scratch {
6238        Some(cell) => {
6239            guest.memory().write_value(cell, &mask)?;
6240            guest
6241                .inject(set_signal_mask_call(cell.into()))
6242                .await
6243                .map(drop)
6244        }
6245        None => {
6246            let mut stack = guest.stack().await;
6247            let cell = stack.push(mask);
6248            let _guard = stack.commit().map_err(|_| Errno::EFAULT)?;
6249            guest.inject(set_signal_mask_call(cell)).await.map(drop)
6250        }
6251    }
6252}
6253
6254/// `rt_sigprocmask(SIG_SETMASK, cell, NULL)`.
6255fn set_signal_mask_call(cell: Addr<'_, KernelSigset>) -> syscalls::RtSigprocmask {
6256    syscalls::RtSigprocmask::new()
6257        .with_how(libc::SIG_SETMASK)
6258        .with_set(Some(cell.cast()))
6259        .with_oldset(None)
6260        .with_sigsetsize(KERNEL_SIGSET_SIZE)
6261}
6262
6263/// Whether a signal stop between the kernel states `before` and `after` took
6264/// exactly `signal` off `queue`: it is no longer there, no other signal left
6265/// either queue, and the mask and dispositions did not change. Signals may have
6266/// arrived in between.
6267fn stop_took_only(
6268    before: &KernelSignalState,
6269    after: &KernelSignalState,
6270    signal: i32,
6271    queue: SignalQueue,
6272) -> bool {
6273    let bit = kernel_sigset_bit(signal);
6274    let other = match queue {
6275        SignalQueue::Thread => SignalQueue::Shared,
6276        SignalQueue::Shared => SignalQueue::Thread,
6277    };
6278    before.blocked == after.blocked
6279        && before.ignored == after.ignored
6280        && before.caught == after.caught
6281        && after.queued(queue) & bit == 0
6282        && before.queued(queue) & !bit & !after.queued(queue) == 0
6283        && before.queued(other) & !after.queued(other) == 0
6284}
6285
6286/// Whether an injected call's error means a signal stopped the guest around it
6287/// rather than that the call produced a result: the backend's restart errno, or
6288/// `EINTR` where a backend runs the call itself. None of these calls blocks.
6289pub(crate) fn probe_was_interrupted_by_signal(errno: Errno) -> bool {
6290    matches!(
6291        errno,
6292        Errno::EINTR
6293            | Errno::ERESTARTSYS
6294            | Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR
6295            | Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
6296            | Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
6297    )
6298}
6299
6300pub(crate) async fn record_retry_event<G, C, T>(guest: &mut G, call: C)
6301where
6302    C: SyscallInfo,
6303    T: RecordOrReplay,
6304    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6305{
6306    let dettid = guest.thread_state().dettid;
6307    let cfg = &guest.config();
6308    if cfg.sequentialize_threads && cfg.observes_schedevents() {
6309        trace_schedevent(
6310            guest,
6311            with_guest_time(
6312                guest,
6313                SchedEvent::syscall(dettid, call.number(), SyscallPhase::Polling),
6314            ),
6315            true,
6316        )
6317        .await;
6318    }
6319}
6320
6321// A helper function for enriching the schedevent with local information.
6322pub fn with_guest_time<G, T>(guest: &G, event: SchedEvent) -> SchedEvent
6323where
6324    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6325    T: RecordOrReplay,
6326{
6327    let dettime = &guest.thread_state().thread_logical_time;
6328    event.with_dettime(dettime)
6329}
6330
6331// Enrich the event with the RIP register from the current guest state, but only if it is unset.
6332pub async fn with_guest_rip<G, T>(guest: &mut G, mut event: SchedEvent) -> SchedEvent
6333where
6334    G: Guest<Detcore<T>>,
6335    T: RecordOrReplay,
6336{
6337    assert!(event.end_rip.is_none());
6338
6339    let regs = guest.regs().await;
6340    let end_rip =
6341        NonZeroUsize::new(crate::arch::instruction_pointer(&regs).try_into().unwrap()).unwrap();
6342    event.end_rip = Some(end_rip);
6343    event
6344}
6345
6346// Convert to absolute logical time point for the timeout.
6347// 0 duration means no timeout, and this will return None.
6348pub async fn millis_duration_to_absolute_timeout<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
6349    guest: &mut G,
6350    timeout_millis: i32,
6351) -> Option<LogicalTime> {
6352    match positive_millis_as_nanos(timeout_millis) {
6353        Some(timeout_nanos) => nanos_duration_to_absolute_timeout(guest, timeout_nanos).await,
6354        None => None,
6355    }
6356}
6357
6358/// Milliseconds to nanoseconds for a strictly positive timeout; `None` for the
6359/// non-positive values Linux treats as "return immediately" (0) or "wait
6360/// forever" (-1), neither of which is a deadline.
6361///
6362/// Kept as a separate, unit-bracketed function on purpose. This conversion was
6363/// previously inlined as `* 1000` instead of `* 1_000_000`, which made every
6364/// finite deadline 1000x too short (a 1 ms timeout expired after 1 us). That
6365/// is invisible in an end-to-end test that only checks a syscall's return
6366/// value, so the arithmetic is pinned here by `millis_to_nanos_conversion`.
6367fn positive_millis_as_nanos(timeout_millis: i32) -> Option<u128> {
6368    (timeout_millis > 0).then(|| (timeout_millis as u128) * 1_000_000)
6369}
6370
6371// Convert to absolute logical time point for the timeout.
6372// 0 duration means no timeout, and this will return None.
6373pub async fn nanos_duration_to_absolute_timeout<G: Guest<Detcore<T>>, T: RecordOrReplay>(
6374    guest: &mut G,
6375    timeout_nanos: u128,
6376) -> Option<LogicalTime> {
6377    if timeout_nanos > 0 {
6378        let ns_delta = Duration::from_nanos(timeout_nanos as u64);
6379        let base_time = thread_observe_time(guest).await;
6380        let target_time = base_time + ns_delta;
6381        Some(target_time)
6382    } else {
6383        None
6384    }
6385}
6386
6387/// The number of `pollfd` entries `poll` and `ppoll` read. Linux declares
6388/// their `nfds` parameter `unsigned int`, so only the low 32 bits of the
6389/// register count; a guest may leave the high word set. Every reader of a
6390/// guest's pollfd array sizes it from this, never from `nfds` itself.
6391pub fn poll_nfds(nfds: libc::nfds_t) -> u32 {
6392    nfds as u32
6393}

6422    #[test]
6423    fn an_ignored_signal_shield_blocks_only_what_the_guest_ignores() {
6424        use crate::syscalls::threads::kernel_sigset_bit as bit;
6425        let state = |blocked, ignored, caught| KernelSignalState {
6426            blocked,
6427            ignored,
6428            caught,
6429            ..Default::default()
6430        };
6431        let default_ignored =
6432            bit(libc::SIGCHLD) | bit(libc::SIGCONT) | bit(libc::SIGURG) | bit(libc::SIGWINCH);
6433        // With every disposition at its default, the shield blocks exactly the
6434        // default-ignored signals, on top of the thread's own mask.
6435        assert_eq!(
6436            ignored_signal_shield_mask(&state(bit(libc::SIGUSR2), 0, 0)),
6437            Some(bit(libc::SIGUSR2) | default_ignored)
6438        );
6439        // A signal set to SIG_IGN joins them; a caught one leaves them.
6440        assert_eq!(
6441            ignored_signal_shield_mask(&state(0, bit(libc::SIGUSR1), bit(libc::SIGCHLD))),
6442            Some(bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | (default_ignored & !bit(libc::SIGCHLD)))
6443        );
6444        // Nothing to block when every ignored signal is caught or already blocked.
6445        assert_eq!(
6446            ignored_signal_shield_mask(&state(
6447                bit(libc::SIGCONT) | bit(libc::SIGURG),
6448                0,
6449                bit(libc::SIGCHLD) | bit(libc::SIGWINCH)
6450            )),
6451            None
6452        );
6453        // A refused change leaves the wait under the guest's own mask, unless the
6454        // backend could not confirm what the mask is.
6455        for refused in [
6456            MaskChangeRefused::Unsupported,
6457            MaskChangeRefused::Gone,
6458            MaskChangeRefused::RestorePending {
6459                saved: 0,
6460                effective: 1,
6461            },
6462            MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
6463                errno: Errno::ESRCH,
6464                mask_unknown: false,
6465            },
6466        ] {
6467            assert!(shield_refusal_leaves_the_mask_known(&refused), "{refused}");
6468        }
6469        assert!(!shield_refusal_leaves_the_mask_known(
6470            &MaskChangeRefused::Failed {
6471                errno: Errno::ESRCH,
6472                mask_unknown: true,
6473            }
6474        ));

6477    /// Linux polls every entry with a non-negative descriptor and ignores the
6478    /// rest (fs/select.c `do_pollfd`), so only those decide whether a poll is
6479    /// guest-held; the `events` and `revents` halves are not descriptors.
6480    #[test]
6481    fn pollfd_descriptors_are_the_non_negative_entries() {
6482        let entries = [
6483            libc::pollfd {
6484                fd: 7,
6485                events: libc::POLLIN,
6486                revents: 0,
6487            },
6488            libc::pollfd {
6489                fd: -1,
6490                events: libc::POLLIN,
6491                revents: 0,

6494                fd: 0,
6495                events: libc::POLLOUT,
6496                revents: libc::POLLHUP,
6497            },

6500            .iter()
6501            .flat_map(|entry| {
6502                let mut bytes = entry.fd.to_ne_bytes().to_vec();
6503                bytes.extend(entry.events.to_ne_bytes());
6504                bytes.extend(entry.revents.to_ne_bytes());
6505                bytes
6506            })
6507            .collect();
6508        assert_eq!(pollfd_descriptors(&bytes), vec![7, 0]);

6512    /// Bracket the millisecond-to-nanosecond timeout conversion in both
6513    /// directions: the non-positive values that are NOT deadlines, and the
6514    /// positive values whose magnitude must be exactly 1e6 ns per ms.
6515    ///
6516    /// The 1 ms case is the specific regression guard: an inlined `* 1000`
6517    /// yields 1_000 here instead of 1_000_000, i.e. a deadline 1000x too
6518    /// short. Asserting the exact value (not merely "nonzero" or "greater
6519    /// than") is what makes that failure visible.
6520    #[test]
6521    fn millis_to_nanos_conversion() {
6522        // Not deadlines: -1 is "infinite", 0 is "return immediately".
6523        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(-1), None);
6524        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(i32::MIN), None);
6525        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(0), None);
6526
6527        // Positive timeouts: exactly 1e6 nanoseconds per millisecond.
6528        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(1), Some(1_000_000));
6529        assert_eq!(positive_millis_as_nanos(1_000), Some(1_000_000_000));
6530        assert_eq!(
6531            positive_millis_as_nanos(i32::MAX),
6532            Some(i32::MAX as u128 * 1_000_000)
6533        );
6534
6535        // The scale itself, stated independently of any single case so a
6536        // future refactor cannot satisfy the above by coincidence.
6537        for millis in [1, 2, 7, 250, 1_000, 86_400_000] {
6538            assert_eq!(
6539                positive_millis_as_nanos(millis),
6540                Some(millis as u128 * 1_000_000),
6541                "1 ms must convert to 1_000_000 ns, not 1_000"
6542            );
6543        }
6544    }

6561    /// `MSG_DONTWAIT` keeps every socket send and receive from waiting,
6562    /// whatever else its flags carry, and no other flag does: recvmmsg's
6563    /// `MSG_WAITFORONE` still waits for the first datagram. Calls with no
6564    /// per-call flags always follow the file.
6565    #[test]
6566    fn only_msg_dontwait_keeps_a_socket_call_from_waiting() {
6567        use reverie::syscalls::*;
6568        let dontwait = libc::MSG_DONTWAIT;
6569        let others = libc::MSG_PEEK | libc::MSG_WAITALL | libc::MSG_NOSIGNAL | libc::MSG_TRUNC;
6570        let cases: [(&str, bool, bool); 6] = [
6571            (
6572                "recvfrom",
6573                Recvfrom::new()
6574                    .with_flags(others | dontwait)
6575                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
6576                Recvfrom::new().with_flags(others).flags_forbid_waiting(),
6577            ),
6578            (
6579                "recvmsg",
6580                Recvmsg::new().with_flags(dontwait).flags_forbid_waiting(),
6581                Recvmsg::new().with_flags(others).flags_forbid_waiting(),
6582            ),
6583            (
6584                "recvmmsg",
6585                Recvmmsg::new()
6586                    .with_flags((libc::MSG_WAITFORONE | dontwait) as u32)
6587                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
6588                Recvmmsg::new()
6589                    .with_flags(libc::MSG_WAITFORONE as u32)
6590                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
6591            ),
6592            (
6593                "sendto",
6594                Sendto::new()
6595                    .with_flags(dontwait as u32)
6596                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
6597                Sendto::new()
6598                    .with_flags(others as u32)
6599                    .flags_forbid_waiting(),
6600            ),
6601            (
6602                "sendmsg",
6603                Sendmsg::new().with_flags(dontwait).flags_forbid_waiting(),
6604                Sendmsg::new().with_flags(others).flags_forbid_waiting(),
6605            ),
6606            (
6607                "sendmmsg",
6608                Sendmmsg::new().with_flags(dontwait).flags_forbid_waiting(),
6609                Sendmmsg::new().with_flags(others).flags_forbid_waiting(),
6610            ),
6611        ];
6612        for (name, with_dontwait, without) in cases {
6613            assert!(with_dontwait, "{name} with MSG_DONTWAIT may wait");
6614            assert!(!without, "{name} without MSG_DONTWAIT never waits");
6615        }
6616        assert!(!Read::new().flags_forbid_waiting());
6617        assert!(
6618            Preadv2::new()
6619                .with_flags(libc::RWF_NOWAIT)
6620                .flags_forbid_waiting(),
6621            "preadv2 with RWF_NOWAIT may wait"
6622        );
6623        assert!(
6624            !Preadv2::new()
6625                .with_flags(libc::RWF_HIPRI)
6626                .flags_forbid_waiting(),
6627            "preadv2 without RWF_NOWAIT never waits"
6628        );
6629        assert!(!Accept4::new().flags_forbid_waiting());
6630        assert!(!Connect::new().flags_forbid_waiting());
6631    }

6633    /// The `ioaction_based_on_fd_status` decision itself: a call whose own
6634    /// flags forbid waiting (MSG_DONTWAIT, RWF_NOWAIT) on a descriptor the
6635    /// guest left blocking runs once (PassThru), where the same call without
6636    /// them is retried (NonblockizeRetry). A mutant dropping the flags term
6637    /// fails this test.
6638    #[test]
6639    fn ioaction_decision_runs_a_nowait_call_once_on_a_blocking_descriptor() {
6640        use super::IOAction;
6641        use super::ioaction_for_fd_status;
6642        // FT with no-wait flags: runs once, as Linux does.
6643        assert_eq!(
6644            ioaction_for_fd_status(3, false, true, true),
6645            IOAction::PassThru
6646        );
6647        // FT without them: simulate blocking by retrying.
6648        assert_eq!(
6649            ioaction_for_fd_status(3, false, true, false),
6650            IOAction::NonblockizeRetry
6651        );
6652        // TT already runs once, flags or not; FF can only block externally.
6653        assert_eq!(
6654            ioaction_for_fd_status(3, true, true, false),
6655            IOAction::PassThru
6656        );
6657        assert_eq!(
6658            ioaction_for_fd_status(3, false, false, true),
6659            IOAction::Blocking
6660        );
6661    }

6665    /// `MSG_WAITFORONE` still waits for the first datagram. Calls with no
6666    /// per-call flags always follow the file.
6667    /// The three receive calls read the error queue exactly when their flags

6671    fn msg_errqueue_marks_only_a_receive_as_an_error_queue_read() {

6681            Recvmmsg::new()
6682                .with_flags(errqueue as u32)
6683                .reads_error_queue()
6684        );
6685        assert!(
6686            !Recvfrom::new()
6687                .with_flags(libc::MSG_DONTWAIT)
6688                .reads_error_queue()
6689        );
6690        assert!(
6691            !Recvmsg::new()
6692                .with_flags(libc::MSG_PEEK)
6693                .reads_error_queue()
6694        );
6695        assert!(
6696            !Recvmmsg::new()
6697                .with_flags(libc::MSG_WAITFORONE as u32)
6698                .reads_error_queue()
6699        );
6700        assert!(!Recvmsg::new().with_flags(errqueue).flags_forbid_waiting());
6701        assert!(
6702            !Sendto::new()
6703                .with_flags(errqueue as u32)
6704                .reads_error_queue()
6705        );
6706        assert!(!Sendmsg::new().with_flags(errqueue).reads_error_queue());

6711    #[test]
6712    fn signal_interruption_errno_matches_linux_restart_policy() {
6713        assert_eq!(
6714            reverie::syscalls::Poll::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
6715            Errno::EINTR
6716        );
6717        assert_eq!(
6718            reverie::syscalls::Ppoll::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
6719            Errno::EINTR
6720        );
6721        assert_eq!(
6722            reverie::syscalls::EpollWait::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
6723            Errno::EINTR
6724        );
6725        let sigtimedwait = reverie::syscalls::RtSigtimedwait::new();
6726        assert_eq!(sigtimedwait.signal_interrupt_errno(), Errno::EINTR);
6727        assert!(sigtimedwait.syscall_would_have_blocked(Err(Errno::EAGAIN)));
6728        assert_eq!(sigtimedwait.timeout_return_val(), Err(Errno::EAGAIN));
6729        assert_eq!(
6730            reverie::syscalls::Read::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
6731            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
6732        );
6733        // A zero-progress writev interruption returns this internal errno on
6734        // ptrace so Linux applies the handler's SA_RESTART policy.
6735        assert_eq!(
6736            reverie::syscalls::Writev::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
6737            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
6738        );
6739        assert_eq!(
6740            reverie::syscalls::Futex::new().signal_interrupt_errno(),
6741            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
6742        );
6743    }

6745    #[test]
6746    fn kernel_restart_errno_matches_linux_restart_policy() {
6747        // Signal-state interruption hands the kernel the wait's own restart code, so
6748        // the guest's disposition decides between a handler's EINTR and a restart
6749        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
6750        // A poll with a positive timeout and a timed futex wait end with Linux's own
6751        // code: a handler turns it into EINTR, and with no handler the kernel runs
6752        // restart_syscall, which Detcore resumes with the deadline it kept
6753        // (`RestartBlock`, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3358).
6754        assert_eq!(
6755            reverie::syscalls::Poll::new()
6756                .with_timeout(300)
6757                .kernel_restart_errno(),
6758            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
6759        );
6760        // A zero timeout never blocks and a negative one never expires, so there is
6761        // no deadline to keep, and running the call again is Linux's restart.
6762        assert_eq!(
6763            reverie::syscalls::Poll::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
6764            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
6765        );
6766        assert_eq!(
6767            reverie::syscalls::Poll::new()
6768                .with_timeout(-1)
6769                .kernel_restart_errno(),
6770            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
6771        );
6772        assert_eq!(
6773            reverie::syscalls::Ppoll::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
6774            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND
6775        );
6776        // epoll_wait and sigtimedwait never restart after a handler.
6777        assert_eq!(
6778            reverie::syscalls::EpollWait::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
6779            Errno::EINTR
6780        );
6781        assert_eq!(
6782            reverie::syscalls::RtSigtimedwait::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
6783            Errno::EINTR
6784        );
6785        assert_eq!(
6786            reverie::syscalls::Futex::new().kernel_restart_errno(),
6787            Errno::ERESTARTSYS
6788        );
6789        // A timed wait is never restarted after a handler runs. FUTEX_WAIT's timeout
6790        // is relative, so its deadline is kept as poll's is.
6791        let timeout = reverie::syscalls::Addr::from_raw(0x1000).unwrap();
6792        assert_eq!(
6793            reverie::syscalls::Futex::new()
6794                .with_timeout(Some(timeout))
6795                .kernel_restart_errno(),
6796            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
6797        );
6798        // FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET's timeout is an absolute deadline, which Linux copies
6799        // into the restart block as it does FUTEX_WAIT's, so a deadline the guest
6800        // moves in memory after the wait began has no effect. Running the call
6801        // again, which ERESTARTNOHAND did, read the moved deadline (round-10
6802        // finding Medium 4 on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361).
6803        let bitset = reverie::syscalls::Futex::new()
6804            .with_futex_op(libc::FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET | libc::FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG)
6805            .with_val3(-1);
6806        assert_eq!(bitset.kernel_restart_errno(), Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
6807        assert!(!bitset.restart_keeps_deadline());
6808        assert_eq!(
6809            bitset.with_timeout(Some(timeout)).kernel_restart_errno(),
6810            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
6811        );
6812        assert!(bitset.with_timeout(Some(timeout)).restart_keeps_deadline());
6813        // FUTEX_LOCK_PI and FUTEX_LOCK_PI2 are always restarted, timed or not, and
6814        // the restarted call reads its absolute deadline again (`futex_lock_pi`).
6815        for op in [
6816            libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI,
6817            libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI | libc::FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG,
6818            libc::FUTEX_LOCK_PI2 | libc::FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME,
6819        ] {
6820            let lock = reverie::syscalls::Futex::new().with_futex_op(op);
6821            assert_eq!(lock.kernel_restart_errno(), Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR);
6822            let timed = lock.with_timeout(Some(timeout));
6823            assert_eq!(timed.kernel_restart_errno(), Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR);
6824            assert!(!timed.restart_keeps_deadline());
6825        }
6826    }

6828    #[test]
6829    fn a_held_signal_is_reported_unless_it_is_sigstop() {
6830        // The backend passes a held signal on unreported when the call returns
6831        // ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK, so a held signal other than SIGSTOP ends the wait
6832        // with ERESTARTNOHAND, which a handler also turns into EINTR.
6833        for signal in [libc::SIGUSR1, libc::SIGTERM, libc::SIGTSTP, libc::SIGCHLD] {
6834            assert_eq!(
6835                held_signal_restart_errno(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK, signal),
6836                Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND,
6837                "signal {signal}"
6838            );
6839        }
6840        // SIGSTOP is never reported, and its restart must keep the deadline.
6841        assert_eq!(
6842            held_signal_restart_errno(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK, libc::SIGSTOP),
6843            Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK
6844        );
6845        // Every other restart code is the call's own.
6846        for errno in [
6847            Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND,
6848            Errno::ERESTARTSYS,
6849            Errno::ERESTARTNOINTR,
6850            Errno::EINTR,
6851        ] {
6852            for signal in [libc::SIGUSR1, libc::SIGSTOP] {
6853                assert_eq!(held_signal_restart_errno(errno, signal), errno);
6854            }
6855        }
6856    }
6857
6858    #[test]
6859    fn resumed_kernel_wait_result_maps_only_erestartsys() {
6860        // The backend's code for a signal that stopped the injected restart
6861        // before it ran; the kernel's restart block is still in place.
6862        assert_eq!(
6863            resumed_kernel_wait_result(Err(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)),
6864            Err(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK)
6865        );
6866        // Every other result is the restarted wait's own.
6867        for result in [
6868            Ok(0),
6869            Err(Errno::ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK),
6870            Err(Errno::EINTR),
6871            Err(Errno::ETIMEDOUT),
6872            Err(Errno::EAGAIN),
6873        ] {
6874            assert_eq!(resumed_kernel_wait_result(result), result);
6875        }
6876    }
6877
6878    #[test]
6879    fn a_restart_block_resumes_only_at_the_interrupted_call() {
6880        let timeout = reverie::syscalls::Addr::from_raw(0x1000).unwrap();
6881        let block = RestartBlock {
6882            rip: 0x4000_1234,
6883            deadline: Some(LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000)),
6884            call: RestartCall::Futex(reverie::syscalls::Futex::new().with_timeout(Some(timeout))),
6885        };
6886        // The kernel's restart runs restart_syscall at the interrupted call's address.
6887        assert_eq!(block.resumed_at(0x4000_1234), Some(block));
6888        // A restart_syscall anywhere else is the guest's own call.
6889        assert_eq!(block.resumed_at(0x4000_1236), None);
6890        assert_eq!(block.resumed_at(0x4000_1232), None);
6891    }

6893    #[test]
6894    fn writev_signal_result_uses_disposition_and_progress() {

6896        for disposition in [
6897            WaitSignalDisposition::Interrupt,
6898            WaitSignalDisposition::Restart,
6899        ] {
6900            assert!(matches!(
6901                interrupted_write_result(&call, 0, Some(disposition)),
6902                Some(Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS)))
6903            ));
6904            assert!(matches!(
6905                interrupted_write_result(&call, 17, Some(disposition)),
6906                Some(Ok(17))
6907            ));
6908        }
6909        assert!(interrupted_write_result(&call, 0, None).is_none());
6910        assert!(interrupted_write_result(&call, 17, None).is_none());
