8772    /// A guest with a caught `SIGCHLD` pending, outside its mask. With
8773    /// `gated_backend`, its configuration is the one under which the scheduler
8774    /// models signal targets: serialized threads and a backend that reports the
8775    /// kernel's signal state.
8776    fn caught_sigchld_guest(gated_backend: bool) -> (WaitGuest, Kernel) {
8777        let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
8778        guest.config.sequentialize_threads = gated_backend;
8779        detcore_model::config::set_kernel_signal_facts(&mut guest.config.backend, gated_backend);
8780        {
8781            let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
8782            kernel.pending = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
8783            kernel.caught = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
8784        }
8785        (guest, kernel)
8786    }
8787
8788    /// A caught `SIGCHLD` pending outside the guest's mask, which the scheduler
8789    /// did not commit in this turn (`admit`), never ends a gated
8790    /// wait, on any backend and whoever sent it: `/proc` cannot tell a
8791    /// `SIGCHLD` a guest or the scheduler sent at a deterministic point from the
8792    /// one the kernel posts for a child event at a moment set by host timing
8793    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). The signal stays queued
8794    /// and is delivered when the call returns. The waits of `select` and
8795    /// `pselect6` hold nothing and end for it, as Linux ends them for any caught
8796    /// signal (`core_sys_select`).
8797    #[tokio::test]
8798    async fn a_pending_caught_sigchld_ends_a_select_wait_but_no_gated_wait() {
8799        for gated_backend in [false, true] {
8800            let (guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(gated_backend);
8801            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
8802
8803            let gated = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
8804            assert!(
8805                !gated.interrupted().unwrap(),
8806                "a pending caught SIGCHLD does not end a gated wait \
8807                 (gated_backend={gated_backend})"
8808            );
8809
8810            let select = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest);
8811            assert!(
8812                select.interrupted().unwrap(),
8813                "the pending caught SIGCHLD ends a select wait (gated_backend={gated_backend})"
8814            );
8815            assert_eq!(
8816                kernel.lock().unwrap().pending,
8817                kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD),
8818                "the signal stays queued for the guest's handler"
8819            );
8820        }
8821    }
8822
8823    /// A caught `SIGCHLD` the scheduler committed to the thread ends a gated
8824    /// wait, but only in the turn whose resume names it
8825    /// (`KernelSignalWait::admit`), and never when a host-timed
8826    /// source a guest armed can post `SIGCHLD` too: that copy could arrive at a
8827    /// moment host timing sets (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
8828    #[tokio::test]
8829    async fn a_committed_sigchld_ends_a_gated_wait_unless_a_host_timed_source_can_post_it() {
8830        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
8831        let (guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
8832        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
8833
8834        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
8835        assert!(
8836            !wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
8837            "an uncommitted SIGCHLD is held"
8838        );
8839        wait.admit(chld, 0);
8840        assert!(
8841            wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
8842            "a committed SIGCHLD ends the wait"
8843        );
8844        wait.admit(0, 0);
8845        assert!(
8846            !wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
8847            "the next turn's resume names nothing, so the SIGCHLD is held again"
8848        );
8849
8850        let mut host_timed = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
8851        host_timed.hold_until_return(chld);
8852        host_timed.admit(chld, 0);
8853        assert!(
8854            !host_timed.interrupted().unwrap(),
8855            "a SIGCHLD a host-timed source can post stays held although committed"
8856        );
8857    }
8858
8859    /// A `SIGCHLD` a guest sent this thread, which the schedule recorded in its
8860    /// private queue and the turn admits (`KernelSignalWait::admit`), ends a
8861    /// gated wait from the thread's own queue only: one pending only on the
8862    /// shared queue, which a host-timed child event can fill, decides nothing.
8863    /// It is admitted for the turn alone, and never when a host-timed source
8864    /// can post `SIGCHLD` (R2b-2 stage 3,
8865    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273).
8866    #[tokio::test]
8867    async fn an_admitted_private_sigchld_ends_a_gated_wait_from_the_threads_own_queue_only() {
8868        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
8869        let (guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
8870        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
8871
8872        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
8873        wait.admit(0, chld);
8874        assert!(
8875            wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
8876            "the thread's own copy ends the wait"
8877        );
8878        assert!(
8879            wait.interrupts_only_by_committed(
8880                &read_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid()).unwrap()
8881            ),
8882            "only the admitted copy ends it, so the turn's probe runs first"
8883        );
8884        kernel.lock().unwrap().shared = chld;
8885        assert!(
8886            !wait.interrupted().unwrap(),
8887            "a SIGCHLD pending only on the shared queue is held"
8888        );
8889        kernel.lock().unwrap().shared = 0;
8890        wait.admit(0, 0);
8891        assert!(!wait.interrupted().unwrap(), "the next turn holds it again");
8892
8893        let mut host_timed = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
8894        host_timed.hold_until_return(chld);
8895        host_timed.admit(0, chld);
8896        assert!(
8897            !host_timed.interrupted().unwrap(),
8898            "a SIGCHLD a host-timed source can post stays held"
8899        );
8900    }

8902    /// An admitted private `SIGCHLD` that only the wait mask lets in is
8903    /// delivered under that mask (`interrupts_only_under_wait_mask`), as a
8904    /// committed one is: an `epoll_pwait` whose temporary mask unblocks a
8905    /// `SIGCHLD` the thread's own mask blocks (R2b-2 stage 3).
8906    #[tokio::test]
8907    async fn an_admitted_private_sigchld_that_only_the_wait_mask_lets_in_is_delivered_under_it() {
8908        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
8909        let (guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
8910        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
8911        kernel.lock().unwrap().blocked |= chld;
8912        let mut wait =
8913            KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::EINTR).with_wait_mask(Some(0));
8914        let state = read_wait_signal_state(guest.pid(), guest.tid()).unwrap();
8915        assert!(
8916            !wait.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state),
8917            "held while not admitted"
8918        );
8919        wait.admit(0, chld);
8920        assert!(wait.interrupts_only_under_wait_mask(&state));
8921    }

8923    /// `admit_under_block` keeps a recorded private `SIGCHLD` only once every
8924    /// blockable signal is blocked in place, and only if the thread's own
8925    /// queue holds `SIGCHLD`, read after the block. A turn that admits nothing
8926    /// makes no request; a refused setter keeps the wait's fallback, the
8927    /// injected `block` after the first probe; a wait whose earlier injected
8928    /// `block` failed (`unblockable`, no `saved_mask`) keeps nothing (R2b-2
8929    /// stage 3, M3c of the rev5 review).
8930    #[tokio::test]
8931    async fn a_recorded_private_sigchld_is_kept_only_under_a_block_in_place() {
8932        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
8933        // The block publishes the guest's own mask, already published here,
8934        // so no request leaves the test (`publish_wait_mask`).
8935        let mut published = PublishedWaitMask(Some(guest_mask()));
8936
8937        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
8938        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
8939        kernel.lock().unwrap().setter.push_back(None);
8940        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
8941        assert_eq!(
8942            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, 0, &mut published)
8943                .await
8944                .unwrap(),
8945            chld,
8946            "blocked in place, and the thread's own queue holds it"
8947        );
8948        assert!(wait.blocked_in_place);
8949        wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
8950        drop(_proc);
8951
8952        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
8953        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
8954        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
8955        assert_eq!(
8956            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, 0, 0, &mut published)
8957                .await
8958                .unwrap(),
8959            0
8960        );
8961        assert!(
8962            kernel.lock().unwrap().set_calls.is_empty(),
8963            "nothing admitted, no request"
8964        );
8965        assert_eq!(
8966            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, chld, &mut published)
8967                .await
8968                .unwrap(),
8969            0,
8970            "a SIGCHLD a host-timed source can post is not admitted"
8971        );
8972        assert!(kernel.lock().unwrap().set_calls.is_empty());
8973        drop(_proc);
8974
8975        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
8976        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
8977        kernel.lock().unwrap().shared = chld;
8978        kernel.lock().unwrap().setter.push_back(None);
8979        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
8980        assert_eq!(
8981            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, 0, &mut published)
8982                .await
8983                .unwrap(),
8984            0,
8985            "only on the shared queue: not the recorded copy"
8986        );
8987        wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
8988        drop(_proc);
8989
8990        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
8991        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
8992        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
8993        assert_eq!(
8994            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, 0, &mut published)
8995                .await
8996                .unwrap(),
8997            0,
8998            "the setter refuses (no answer queued)"
8999        );
9000        assert!(
9001            wait.needs_block(),
9002            "the injected block after the first probe stays"
9003        );
9004        drop(_proc);
9005
9006        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
9007        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
9008        let mut wait = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
9009        wait.unblockable = true;
9010        assert_eq!(
9011            wait.admit_under_block(&mut guest, 0, chld, 0, &mut published)
9012                .await
9013                .unwrap(),
9014            0,
9015            "an earlier injected block failed: no block, no private copy"
9016        );
9017        assert!(kernel.lock().unwrap().set_calls.is_empty());
9018    }
9019
9020    /// A pipe turn (`turn_signals_with_block`) counts the recorded private
9021    /// `SIGCHLD` only where the gate holds, a block is in force and the
9022    /// thread's own queue holds it. Not on the scalar writer's first attempt,
9023    /// the guest's own write, which blocks nothing (`may_block` false): an
9024    /// injection of that turn could take the copy into the backend's single
9025    /// held slot. Not without the gate, as on a socket. Not from the shared
9026    /// queue alone (R2b-2 stage 3).
9027    #[tokio::test]
9028    async fn a_pipe_turn_counts_a_recorded_private_sigchld_only_under_a_block_in_place() {
9029        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
9030        let turn = |may_block: bool, gate: bool, shared: bool| async move {
9031            // Thread 1, the thread state's own number, so a request may leave.
9032            let (mut guest, kernel) = WaitGuest::new(Pid::from_raw(1), guest_mask());
9033            {
9034                let mut kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
9035                kernel.pending = chld;
9036                kernel.caught = chld;
9037                kernel.shared = if shared { chld } else { 0 };
9038                kernel.setter.push_back(None);
9039                kernel.private_record = Some((0, chld));
9040            }
9041            let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
9042            let mut wait = Some(KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTSYS));
9043            let mut published = PublishedWaitMask(Some(guest_mask()));
9044            let pending =
9045                turn_signals_with_block(&mut guest, &mut wait, may_block, 0, gate, &mut published)
9046                    .await
9047                    .unwrap()
9048                    .pending;
9049            if let Some(wait) = wait.as_mut() {
9050                wait.restore(&mut guest, None).await.unwrap();
9051            }
9052            let blocked_in_place = !kernel.lock().unwrap().set_calls.is_empty();
9053            (pending & chld, blocked_in_place)
9054        };
9055        assert_eq!(
9056            turn(true, true, false).await,
9057            (chld, true),
9058            "blocked in place: admitted"
9059        );
9060        assert_eq!(
9061            turn(false, true, false).await,
9062            (0, false),
9063            "the writer's first attempt blocks nothing: held"
9064        );
9065        assert_eq!(turn(true, false, false).await, (0, true), "no gate: held");
9066        assert_eq!(
9067            turn(true, true, true).await,
9068            (0, true),
9069            "the shared queue alone: held"
9070        );
9071    }
9072
9073    /// The pipe path's hold leaves out an admitted private `SIGCHLD`
9074    /// (`turn_signals_before_discard`'s `private`): it counts in the turn's
9075    /// `pending`, where without it the hold keeps it out (R2b-2 stage 3).
9076    #[test]
9077    fn a_pipe_turn_counts_an_admitted_private_sigchld() {
9078        let chld = kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
9079        let state = KernelSignalState {
9080            pending: chld,
9081            thread_pending: chld,
9082            caught: chld,
9083            ..KernelSignalState::default()
9084        };
9085        assert_eq!(
9086            turn_signals_before_discard(&state, 0, 0, 0, NamedRealTime::Woken, 0).pending,
9087            0,
9088            "held"
9089        );
9090        assert_eq!(
9091            turn_signals_before_discard(&state, 0, 0, 0, NamedRealTime::Woken, chld).pending,
9092            chld,
9093            "admitted"
9094        );
9095    }

9097    /// The same `SIGCHLD` ends a select wait before an injection that is not a
9098    /// probe (`inject_absorbing`: the change of mask that blocks signals for the
9099    /// wait), with `ERESTARTNOHAND`, which the handler's run turns into `EINTR`.
9100    /// The waits of `select` and `pselect6` make every probe with
9101    /// `inject_first_probe`. A gated wait makes the injection, and the `SIGCHLD`
9102    /// that stops it is held until the call returns.
9103    #[tokio::test]
9104    async fn a_pending_caught_sigchld_ends_a_select_wait_before_the_injection() {
9105        let (mut guest, kernel) = caught_sigchld_guest(true);
9106        kernel.lock().unwrap().stops_for_pending = true;
9107        let _proc = scripted_proc(&kernel);
9108
9109        let mut select = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest);
9110        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut select, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
9111        assert!(
9112            matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND))),
9113            "{result:?}"
9114        );
9115        {
9116            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
9117            assert!(kernel.requested.is_empty(), "nothing is injected");
9118            assert_eq!(kernel.pending, kernel_sigset_bit(libc::SIGCHLD));
9119        }
9120        assert_eq!(select.held, None);
9121
9122        let mut gated = KernelSignalWait::new(&guest, 0, false, Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND);
9123        let result = inject_mask_absorbing(&mut gated, &mut guest, guest_mask()).await;
9124        assert!(matches!(result, Ok(Ok(0))), "{result:?}");
9125        {
9126            let kernel = kernel.lock().unwrap();
9127            assert_eq!(kernel.taken, vec![libc::SIGCHLD]);
9128            assert_eq!(kernel.requested.len(), 2, "stopped once, then ran");
9129        }
9130        assert_eq!(gated.held.map(|held| held.kind), Some(HeldKind::Precious));
9131    }

9133    /// The kernel's next dequeue: the private queue before the shared one, a
9134    /// synchronous signal first, then the lowest number, outside the mask.
9135    #[test]
9136    fn next_dequeued_follows_the_kernel_order() {
9137        let bit = kernel_sigset_bit;
9138        let state = KernelSignalState {
9139            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGUSR2) | bit(libc::SIGSEGV),
9140            shared_pending: bit(libc::SIGHUP),
9141            ..KernelSignalState::default()
9142        };
9143        assert_eq!(
9144            state.next_dequeued(0),
9145            Some((libc::SIGSEGV, SignalQueue::Thread))
9146        );
9147        assert_eq!(
9148            state.next_dequeued(bit(libc::SIGSEGV)),
9149            Some((libc::SIGUSR2, SignalQueue::Thread))
9150        );
9151        assert_eq!(
9152            state.next_dequeued(bit(libc::SIGSEGV) | bit(libc::SIGUSR2)),
9153            Some((libc::SIGHUP, SignalQueue::Shared))
9154        );
9155        assert_eq!(state.next_dequeued(!0), None);
9156    }

9158    /// A stop is identified only when exactly the predicted signal left its
9159    /// queue and the mask and dispositions are unchanged; arrivals do not matter.
9160    #[test]
9161    fn a_stop_is_identified_only_by_exactly_its_signal() {
9162        let bit = kernel_sigset_bit;
9163        let before = KernelSignalState {
9164            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | bit(libc::SIGWINCH),
9165            shared_pending: bit(libc::SIGHUP),
9166            ..KernelSignalState::default()
9167        };
9168        let took = |after: KernelSignalState, signal, queue| {
9169            stop_took_only(&before, &after, signal, queue)
9170        };
9171        let after = KernelSignalState {
9172            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGWINCH) | bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
9173            ..before
9174        };
9175        assert!(took(after, libc::SIGUSR1, SignalQueue::Thread));
9176        assert!(
9177            !took(after, libc::SIGWINCH, SignalQueue::Thread),
9178            "SIGWINCH is still queued"
9179        );
9180        let two_left = KernelSignalState {
9181            thread_pending: 0,
9182            ..before
9183        };
9184        assert!(!took(two_left, libc::SIGUSR1, SignalQueue::Thread));
9185        let shared_left = KernelSignalState {
9186            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGWINCH),
9187            shared_pending: 0,
9188            ..before
9189        };
9190        assert!(!took(shared_left, libc::SIGUSR1, SignalQueue::Thread));
9191        let mask_changed = KernelSignalState {
9192            blocked: bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
9193            ..after
9194        };
9195        assert!(!took(mask_changed, libc::SIGUSR1, SignalQueue::Thread));
9196        let disposition_changed = KernelSignalState {
9197            ignored: bit(libc::SIGWINCH),
9198            ..after
9199        };
9200        assert!(!took(
9201            disposition_changed,
9202            libc::SIGUSR1,
9203            SignalQueue::Thread
9204        ));
9205    }

9207    /// A select wait with a pselect6 temporary mask (`with_wait_mask`) holds a
9208    /// caught signal that the temporary mask blocks, and the guest's own mask
9209    /// does not, when it stops an injection before `block` takes effect, as
9210    /// Linux keeps it pending for the whole call; without the temporary mask
9211    /// the same stop ends the wait, and a signal only the temporary mask
9212    /// unblocks ends it too (review of
9213    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4051).
9214    #[test]
9215    fn a_signal_the_temporary_mask_blocks_is_held_not_ended() {
9216        let bit = kernel_sigset_bit;
9217        let (guest, _kernel) = WaitGuest::live(guest_mask());
9218        let before = KernelSignalState {
9219            pending: bit(libc::SIGALRM),
9220            thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGALRM),
9221            blocked: guest_mask(),
9222            caught: bit(libc::SIGALRM) | bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
9223            ..KernelSignalState::default()
9224        };
9225        let plain = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest);
9226        assert_eq!(
9227            plain.stop_verdict(&before, libc::SIGALRM),
9228            StopVerdict::End(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND)
9229        );
9230        let masked = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest).with_wait_mask(Some(bit(libc::SIGALRM)));
9231        assert_eq!(
9232            masked.stop_verdict(&before, libc::SIGALRM),
9233            StopVerdict::Absorb(HeldKind::Precious)
9234        );
9235        let unblocking = KernelSignalWait::for_select(&guest).with_wait_mask(Some(0));
9236        assert_eq!(
9237            unblocking.stop_verdict(&before, libc::SIGUSR2),
9238            StopVerdict::End(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND)
9239        );
9240    }
9241}

9243#[cfg(test)]
9244mod turn_signal_tests {

9247    fn bit(signal: libc::c_int) -> KernelSigset {

9265    /// Rule 3 of R2b-1 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273): with
9266    /// no progress only a pending copy ends the call; after progress a named
9267    /// wake does too.
9268    #[test]

9280        assert!(pending.ends(false));
9281        assert!(pending.ends(true));

9285    /// A caught SIGCHLD pending at a poll's turn is held unless the scheduler
9286    /// committed it, and a host-timed signal is held even then (arm A8).

9288    fn the_hold_leaves_out_an_uncommitted_sigchld_and_every_host_timed_signal() {
9289        let chld = bit(libc::SIGCHLD);

9306    /// A named signal counts only if the call's mask leaves it unblocked
9307    /// (rule 2). A real-time one counts only if its disposition delivers it
9308    /// for `writev`, which the drain never filters (rule 2), and as woken for
9309    /// the generic poll and the scalar writer, whose drain already tested it
9310    /// (rule 1), so a flush after the wake does not undo it (the Claude
9311    /// implementation review of R2b-1, F1).
9312    #[test]
9313    fn a_named_signal_counts_only_unblocked_and_a_real_time_one_by_its_call() {
9314        use NamedRealTime::ByDisposition;
9315        use NamedRealTime::Woken;
9316        let usr1 = bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
9317        let rt = bit(libc::SIGRTMIN());
9318        let s = state(0, usr1, usr1);
9319        for real_time in [Woken, ByDisposition] {
9320            assert_eq!(
9321                turn_signals_before_discard(&s, usr1, 0, usr1, real_time, 0).named,
9322                0
9323            );
9324            assert_eq!(
9325                turn_signals_before_discard(&s, 0, 0, usr1, real_time, 0).named,
9326                usr1
9327            );
9328        }
9329        let ignored_rt = KernelSignalState {
9330            ignored: rt,
9331            ..state(0, 0, 0)
9332        };
9333        assert_eq!(
9334            turn_signals_before_discard(&ignored_rt, 0, 0, rt, ByDisposition, 0).named,
9335            0
9336        );
9337        assert_eq!(
9338            turn_signals_before_discard(&ignored_rt, 0, 0, rt, Woken, 0).named,
9339            rt
9340        );
9341        assert_eq!(
9342            turn_signals_before_discard(&ignored_rt, rt, 0, rt, Woken, 0).named,
9343            0
9344        );
9345        let caught_rt = state(0, rt, 0);
9346        assert_eq!(
9347            turn_signals_before_discard(&caught_rt, 0, 0, rt, ByDisposition, 0).named,
9348            rt
9349        );
9350    }

9353/// The mask a thread is stopped under where its blocking call returned, until
9354/// its continuation turn (`continuation_mask`).
9355#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
9356pub(crate) enum ContinuationMask {
9357    /// The call's temporary mask: the call ran and a signal ended it.
9358    Temporary,
9359    /// Not known to the scheduler, in record and replay alike.
9360    Unknown,
9361    /// The thread's own mask, which the kernel restored before the call
9362    /// returned and holds in record and replay alike (with the signals it
9363    /// ignores blocked over it until after the continuation, when the call
9364    /// raised an `IgnoredSignalShield`).
9365    Restored,
9366}
9367
9368/// The mask `call`, having returned `result`, leaves its thread stopped under,
9369/// decided from what the kernel did, which the raw result tells and replay
9370/// serves as recorded:
9371/// - pselect6 and ppoll that a signal ended return `-ERESTARTNOHAND`, or the
9372///   `-EINTR` that `poll_select_finish` can still turn it into after keeping
9373///   the mask (a timeout write-back that faults, or the STICKY_TIMEOUTS
9374///   personality); epoll_pwait and epoll_pwait2 return `-EINTR`. Linux then
9375///   delivers the signal under the temporary mask and `rt_sigreturn` restores
9376///   the saved one (`restore_saved_sigmask_unless`, fs/select.c, fs/eventpoll.c
9377///   and kernel/signal.c at v6.9): `Temporary`.
9378/// - Their normal return: Linux restored the saved mask before returning. Their
9379///   `-ERESTARTSYS`, which the host reports when the signal reached the thread
9380///   before the call ran: the kernel never installed the mask, and the
9381///   recording holds that result. Either way `Restored`.
9382/// - rt_sigsuspend: `Unknown`, whatever its result. Whether it ran is not
9383///   recorded: record injects it live, where a signal arriving first yields a
9384///   host-timed `-ERESTARTSYS` (the kernel never installed the mask), and
9385///   replay re-injects it with retry, which never shows that. A rule on its
9386///   result would differ between the two (the Claude review of d1b9404c), and
9387///   a known temporary mask would claim one the kernel may not have installed
9388///   (the Codex review of da662bb2). The scheduler treats an unknown mask
9389///   alike in both: no `SIGCHLD` taker or signal target, no discard.
9390/// - Any other call: `Restored`; it installed no temporary mask.
9391pub(crate) fn continuation_mask(call: Syscall, result: &Result<i64, Error>) -> ContinuationMask {
9392    let ended_by = |errno: Errno| matches!(result, Err(Error::Errno(error)) if *error == errno);
9393    let kept = match call {
9394        Syscall::RtSigsuspend(_) => return ContinuationMask::Unknown,
9395        Syscall::Pselect6(_) | Syscall::Ppoll(_) => {
9396            ended_by(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND) || ended_by(Errno::EINTR)
9397        }
9398        Syscall::EpollPwait(_) | Syscall::Other(Sysno::epoll_pwait2, _) => ended_by(Errno::EINTR),
9399        _ => false,
9400    };
9401    if kept {
9402        ContinuationMask::Temporary
9403    } else {
9404        ContinuationMask::Restored
9405    }
9406}
9407
9408#[cfg(test)]
9409mod temporary_mask_tests {
9410    use super::*;
9411
9412    /// The continuation mask follows what the kernel did: the temporary mask
9413    /// for an interrupted pselect6 or ppoll (`-ERESTARTNOHAND`, or the `-EINTR`
9414    /// it can become after the kernel kept the mask) and an interrupted
9415    /// epoll_pwait or epoll_pwait2 (`-EINTR`); the restored own mask for their
9416    /// normal return, a call the signal reached before it ran (`-ERESTARTSYS`)
9417    /// or another errno; unknown for every rt_sigsuspend, whose `-ERESTARTSYS`
9418    /// is host-timed in record and absent in replay; restored for a call
9419    /// without a temporary mask.
9420    #[test]
9421    fn the_continuation_mask_follows_what_the_kernel_did() {
9422        let restart = Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTNOHAND));
9423        let eintr = Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EINTR));
9424        let pselect = Syscall::Pselect6(syscalls::Pselect6::new());
9425        let ppoll = Syscall::Ppoll(syscalls::Ppoll::new());
9426        let epoll = Syscall::EpollPwait(syscalls::EpollPwait::new());
9427        let epoll2 = Syscall::Other(
9428            Sysno::epoll_pwait2,
9429            reverie::syscalls::SyscallArgs::new(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
9430        );
9431        let before_entry = Err(Error::Errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS));
9432        let sigsuspend = Syscall::RtSigsuspend(syscalls::RtSigsuspend::new());
9433        let read = Syscall::Read(syscalls::Read::new());
9434        let ebadf = Err(Error::Errno(Errno::EBADF));
9435        use ContinuationMask::*;
9436        for call in [pselect, ppoll] {
9437            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &restart), Temporary, "{call:?}");
9438            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &eintr), Temporary, "{call:?}");
9439            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &before_entry), Restored, "{call:?}");
9440            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &ebadf), Restored, "{call:?}");
9441            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &Ok(1)), Restored, "{call:?}");
9442        }
9443        for result in [&restart, &eintr, &before_entry, &Ok(0)] {
9444            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(sigsuspend, result), Unknown, "{result:?}");
9445        }
9446        for call in [epoll, epoll2] {
9447            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &eintr), Temporary, "{call:?}");
9448            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &restart), Restored, "{call:?}");
9449            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &before_entry), Restored, "{call:?}");
9450            assert_eq!(continuation_mask(call, &Ok(0)), Restored, "{call:?}");
9451        }
9452        assert_eq!(continuation_mask(read, &restart), Restored);
9453    }
9454}

9460    fn refusal(operation: reverie::UnsupportedOperation) -> Option<reverie::UnsupportedRefusal> {

9469    /// no refusal, or a refusal another call site owns (flock, process
9470    /// groups, a signal), is not judged here.

9472    fn only_a_tool_decided_refusal_is_an_internal_failure() {
9473        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(7);

9475            refusal(reverie::UnsupportedOperation::ToolDecided),

9491            tool_decided_injection_failure(None, dettid, Sysno::getpgrp),

9499        ] {

9501                tool_decided_injection_failure(refusal(operation), dettid, Sysno::getpgrp),
